%{ for pattern in exclude_paths ~}
  "${pattern}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

# Alert configuration
NTFY_URL="${ntfy_url}"
NTFY_PRIORITY="${ntfy_priority}"
NTFY_TAGS="${ntfy_tags}"

# =============================================================================
# Helper Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"
}

send_alert() {
    local title="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local priority="$${3:-$${NTFY_PRIORITY}}"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Title: $${title}" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${message}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# =============================================================================
# Pre-Backup Commands (Database Dumps, etc.)
# =============================================================================

run_pre_backup_hooks() {
    log "Running pre-backup hooks..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
%{ for cmd in pre_backup_commands ~}
    # ${cmd.name}
    log "  - ${cmd.name}"
    if timeout ${cmd.timeout} bash -c '${cmd.command}'; then
        log "    ✓ Success"
    else
        log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $$?)"
        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "Pre-backup hook failed: ${cmd.name}" \
            "high"
        return 1
    fi

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions
# =============================================================================

cleanup_temp_files() {
    log "Cleaning up temporary dump files..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Backup Function
# =============================================================================

run_backup() {
    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"
    local backup_time=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    # Set PBS fingerprint environment variable for certificate verification
    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    log "Command: $${backup_cmd}"

    # Run backup
    if eval "$${backup_cmd}"; then
        local end_time=$(date +%s)
        local duration=$((end_time - start_time))

        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s"

        # Prune old backups
        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \
            --repository "$PBS_REPOSITORY" \
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}
            --keep-last "$${RETENTION}"

        log "✓ Prune completed"

        # Cleanup temporary files
        cleanup_temp_files

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else
        local exit_code=$$?
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${exit_code}"

        send_alert "Backup Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "PBS backup failed for ${namespace} (exit code: $${exit_code})" \
            "high"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    # Run pre-backup hooks
    if ! run_pre_backup_hooks; then
        log "Pre-backup hooks failed, aborting backup"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Run backup
    if ! run_backup; then
        log "Backup failed"
        exit 1
    fi

    log "All tasks completed successfully"
    exit 0
}

# Run main function
main

# =============================================================================
# n8n LXC - Workflow Automation
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 502
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Plus traefik-route module for self-service routing.
# =============================================================================

module "n8n" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  # Identity
  name         = "n8n"
  container_id = 502

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores          = 2
  memory         = 2048
  swap           = 1024
  rootfs_size    = 8
  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"

  # SSH
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Container options - unprivileged for security
  unprivileged = true
  template     = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox notes
  service_description = "Workflow automation platform"
  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://n8n.${var.domain_internal}/"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.n8n}:5678/"
  }
  services = [
    { name = "n8n", port = 5678, info = "Web UI and API" }
  ]
  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Docker Deployment

**Compose file:** `/config/docker-compose.yml`
**Data volume:** `n8n_data`

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f n8n
```

**Restart n8n:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart n8n
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=n8n` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["n8n", "automation"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.n8n.container_id
  container_ip   = module.n8n.ip_address
  container_name = "n8n"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-502"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "SQLite backup"
      command = "cp /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite.backup"
      timeout = 60
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,n8n"
  }

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "n8n"
  backend_url = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "n8n.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.n8n.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.n8n.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.n8n.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.n8n_route.internal_url
    direct   = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678/"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.n8n_route.remote_config_path
}

volumes:

I found the issues. There are **two problems**:

## Issue 1: Wrong SQLite file path

The pre-backup command is looking for:
```
/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite
```

But the docker-compose shows the volume is named `n8n_data` (not `config_n8n_data`), and Docker volumes by default are stored based on the project directory name. Since the compose file is in `/config`, the actual volume path is likely:
```
/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite
```

Wait, that's actually correct because Docker prefixes with the compose project name (which defaults to the directory name - "config" in this case). But the SQLite database for n8n is stored at `.n8n/database.sqlite` inside the volume.

## Issue 2: Exit code capture bug in the backup script

Looking at line 78 and 173-174:
```bash
log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $$?)"  # Line 78 - $$? captures exit code of log, not the command
...
local exit_code=$$?  # Line 173 - Same issue, captures exit code of log, not eval
```

The exit code `689098` looks like garbage because the actual exit code was never properly captured.

Let me verify the n8n data path and fix both issues:

run_pre_backup_hooks() {

        log "    ✓ Success"
    else

        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions

cleanup_temp_files() {

    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}

    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"

    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"

%{ if namespace != "" ~}

        send_alert "Backup Failed: ${container_name}" \

            "high"

        return 1
    fi
}

content.text:
## Summary

I found and fixed **two issues** in [pbs-backup.sh.tftpl](tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl):

### 1. Exit code capture bug (the `689098` error)
The script was trying to capture exit codes using `$$?` after running the `log` function, which captured the exit code of `log` instead of the actual failing command. Fixed by:
- Capturing exit code immediately after the failing command runs
- Using `local backup_exit_code=0; eval ... || backup_exit_code=$$?` pattern

### 2. Root cause of the failure
The "Pre-backup hook failed: SQLite backup" error means the `cp` command is failing because the SQLite file doesn't exist at:
```
/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite
```

**To debug this**, SSH into the n8n container (502) and check:
```bash
ssh root@<n8n-ip>
ls -la /var/lib/docker/volumes/
ls -la /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/
```

This will show you:
1. What the actual volume name is (might not be `config_n8n_data`)
2. Whether `database.sqlite` exists in that location

Once you confirm the correct path, update the pre_backup_commands in [n8n/main.tf:96](tofu/apps/n8n/main.tf#L96).

Would you like me to SSH in and check the actual path, or would you prefer to do that?
the n8n's IP is 10.100.5.102

# Prometheus Configuration
# Receives metrics from OpenTelemetry Collector and scrapes additional targets

global:
  scrape_interval: 30s
  evaluation_interval: 30s
  external_labels:
    monitor: 'homelab'

# Alerting configuration
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
    - static_configs:
        - targets:
            - alertmanager:9093

# Rule files for alerts
rule_files:
  - /etc/prometheus/alerts/*.yml

# Scrape configurations
scrape_configs:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Monitoring Stack Self-Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================

  # Prometheus self-monitoring
  - job_name: 'prometheus'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['localhost:9090']

  # OpenTelemetry Collector metrics
  - job_name: 'otel-collector'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['otel-collector:8888']

  # Alertmanager metrics
  - job_name: 'alertmanager'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['alertmanager:9093']

  # Grafana metrics
  - job_name: 'grafana'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['grafana:3000']

  # ==========================================================================
  # Traefik Reverse Proxy Metrics
  # ==========================================================================
  - job_name: 'traefik'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['10.100.2.200:8082']
        labels:
          instance: 'traefik'
          lxc_id: '200'

  # ==========================================================================
  # AdGuard Home - DNS Metrics
  # Native Prometheus metrics not yet available in v0.107.70
  # TODO: Enable when PR #7937 is merged, or deploy adguard-exporter sidecar
  # https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdGuardHome/pull/7937
  # ==========================================================================
  # - job_name: 'adguard'
  #   static_configs:
  #     - targets: ['192.168.1.196:9618']
  #       labels:
  #         instance: 'adguard'
  #         lxc_id: '101'

  # ==========================================================================
  # Immich - Photo Management Metrics
  # Metrics pushed via OTEL to otel-collector (no scrape needed)
  # ==========================================================================

  # ==========================================================================
  # Jellyfin - Media Server Metrics
  # Requires: Prometheus plugin installed in Jellyfin
  # ==========================================================================
  # - job_name: 'jellyfin'
  #   static_configs:
  #     - targets: ['10.100.4.101:8096']
  #       labels:
  #         instance: 'jellyfin'
  #         lxc_id: '226'

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - Status Page Metrics
  # ==========================================================================
  - job_name: 'uptime-kuma'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['uptime-kuma:3001']
        labels:
          instance: 'uptime-kuma'
    metrics_path: /metrics

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push Notification Metrics
  # NOTE: Disabled - Docker DNS resolves 'ntfy' to external DNS (ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev)
  # instead of container name due to search domain. Low-value metrics anyway.
  # ==========================================================================
  # - job_name: 'ntfy'
  #   static_configs:
  #     - targets: ['ntfy:9090']
  #       labels:
  #         instance: 'ntfy'
  #   metrics_path: /metrics

# ==========================================================================
# Metrics Coverage Summary
# ==========================================================================
#
# SCRAPED (Pull):
#   - prometheus, alertmanager, grafana, otel-collector (self-monitoring)
#   - traefik (reverse proxy metrics)
#   - uptime-kuma (status page metrics)
#
# PUSHED (via OTEL):
#   - Proxmox VE (node, VM, storage metrics)
#   - Immich (photo library metrics) - enable in Settings > Telemetry
#
# NOT YET AVAILABLE:
#   - AdGuard: No native support, PR #7937 pending
#   - Jellyfin: Requires plugin installation
#   - OpenWebUI: No metrics endpoint
#   - n8n: Requires N8N_METRICS=true env var
#

# Remote write receiver enabled via --web.enable-remote-write-receiver flag
# This allows OTEL collector to push metrics

# Homelab Alert Rules
# Only includes alerts for metrics we actually collect

groups:
  - name: services
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      # Prometheus target down
      - alert: TargetDown
        expr: up == 0
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Target {{ $labels.instance }} is down"
          description: "Prometheus cannot reach {{ $labels.job }} target {{ $labels.instance }}"

      # Traefik high error rate
      - alert: TraefikHighErrorRate
        expr: sum(rate(traefik_entrypoint_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(traefik_entrypoint_requests_total[5m])) > 0.05
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "High error rate on Traefik"
          description: "More than 5% of requests are returning 5xx errors"

      # Traefik backend down
      - alert: TraefikBackendDown
        expr: traefik_service_server_up == 0
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Traefik backend {{ $labels.service }} is down"
          description: "Backend service {{ $labels.service }} is not responding"

  - name: proxmox
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      # Proxmox host high CPU
      - alert: ProxmoxHighCPU
        expr: proxmox_node_cpustat_cpu_percent > 80
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "High CPU on Proxmox node"
          description: "Proxmox node CPU usage above 80% for 10 minutes (current: {{ $value | printf \"%.1f\" }}%)"

      # Proxmox host memory high
      - alert: ProxmoxHighMemory
        expr: (proxmox_node_memory_memused_bytes / proxmox_node_memory_memtotal_bytes) * 100 > 85
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "High memory on Proxmox node"
          description: "Proxmox node memory usage above 85% for 10 minutes"

      # Proxmox storage low
      - alert: ProxmoxStorageLow
        expr: (proxmox_storage_used_bytes / proxmox_storage_total_bytes) * 100 > 85
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "Low storage on {{ $labels.storage }}"
          description: "Proxmox storage {{ $labels.storage }} is above 85% used"

      # Proxmox storage critical
      - alert: ProxmoxStorageCritical
        expr: (proxmox_storage_used_bytes / proxmox_storage_total_bytes) * 100 > 95
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
        annotations:
          summary: "Critical storage on {{ $labels.storage }}"
          description: "Proxmox storage {{ $labels.storage }} is above 95% used"

      # LXC/VM down (no metrics for 5 minutes)
      - alert: ProxmoxVMDown
        expr: changes(proxmox_vm_uptime_seconds[5m]) == 0 and proxmox_vm_uptime_seconds > 0
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "VM/LXC {{ $labels.name }} may be unresponsive"
          description: "No uptime changes detected for VM/LXC {{ $labels.vmid }} ({{ $labels.name }})"

  - name: monitoring
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      # Prometheus TSDB high cardinality
      - alert: PrometheusTSDBHighCardinality
        expr: prometheus_tsdb_head_series > 100000
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
        annotations:
          summary: "Prometheus high time series count"
          description: "Prometheus has more than 100k active time series (current: {{ $value }})"

Based on the search results, here's what I found about disabling authentication for Uptime Kuma's Prometheus metrics endpoint:

## Uptime Kuma Prometheus Metrics Authentication

### Default Behavior
By default, HTTP basic authentication is used to secure access to the Prometheus metrics endpoint.(no content)You can configure Prometheus with basic authentication using your Uptime Kuma username and password.

### API Key Authentication
As soon as you add your first API key, the use of basic authentication for the endpoint will be permanently disabled.(no content)Authentication is then done by passing the API key in the Authorization header.

### Disabling Authentication Entirely
To disable auth from Uptime Kuma, go to Settings > Advanced > Disable Auth.

### Known Issue (March 2024)
There was a GitHub issue (#4628) reported in March 2024 about this behavior:
A user reported on March 29, 2024 that they had disabled user authentication and added Authelia as a middleware, with both the /metrics and /api/push endpoints configured as 'bypass'.(no content)They found that the API token was no longer required anymore to access /metrics, when they expected it would still be required.

### Historical Issue
An older issue from 2022 reported that even though a site had auth explicitly turned off, it still required username and password when visiting the /metrics endpoint, which was considered a bug.

In summary, if you want to completely disable authentication for the Prometheus metrics endpoint, you need to disable authentication entirely in Uptime Kuma's settings (Settings > Advanced > Disable Auth). Note that this will also disable auth for the entire application, not just the metrics endpoint.

# Homelab Infrastructure

OpenTofu-managed homelab on Proxmox. All commands run from local machine.

## Beads - AI Issue Tracking

This repo uses [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) for AI-native issue tracking. Beads helps AI agents manage complex, multi-step tasks by tracking dependencies between work items.
BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: run 'bd onboard' and follow the instructions

### Quick Commands

```bash
# Find ready work (no blockers)
task beads:ready

# List all issues
task beads:list
task beads:list STATUS=in_progress

# Create an issue
task beads:create TITLE="Add new LXC container for XYZ"

# View issue details
task beads:show ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Update status
task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=in_progress
task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=done

# Close completed work
task beads:close ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Add dependencies (FROM blocks TO)
task beads:dep FROM=proxmox-homelab-1 TO=proxmox-homelab-2

# View dependency tree
task beads:dep:tree ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Sync with git
task beads:sync
```

### For AI Agents

When starting work on this repo:

1. Run `bd ready` to see available tasks
2. Pick an issue and run `bd update <id> --status in_progress`
3. Complete the work
4. Run `bd close <id>` when done

Use `bd prime` to generate context for your session. Dependencies are tracked automatically - issues marked as "blocking" others will show up in the `bd ready` output once completed.

## Quick Reference

```bash
# OpenTofu workflow
task tofu:init APP=dashboards
task tofu:plan APP=dashboards
task tofu:apply APP=dashboards

# Utility commands
task tofu:ssh APP=dashboards           # SSH to LXC
task tofu:sync:compose APP=dashboards  # Sync compose files
task tofu:logs APP=dashboards SERVICE=homepage

# Desktop LXC (temporary GUI for downloads)
task desktop:create
task desktop:info
task desktop:destroy

# Backup operations
task backup:status                 # View backup status
task backup:now APP=immich         # Manual backup
task backup:all                    # Backup all containers
task backup:list APP=immich        # List backups
task backup:restore BACKUP=file TARGET_ID=305
task backup:immich:db              # Dump Immich database

# IP address management
task ip:next                       # Get next available IP for new LXC
task ip:list                       # Show all allocated IPs

# Beads issue tracking
task beads:ready                   # Show ready work (no blockers)
task beads:list                    # List all issues
task beads:create TITLE="..."      # Create new issue
task beads:show ID=...             # View issue details
task beads:close ID=...            # Complete an issue
```

## Architecture

- **Proxmox Host**: 192.168.1.215 (SSH: `ssh root@homelab`)
- **Traefik LXC**: 192.168.1.162 (ID: 200)
- **Monitoring LXC**: 192.168.1.229 (ID: 500)
- **IaC**: OpenTofu with bpg/proxmox provider
- **Secrets**: 1Password CLI (`op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"`)

## Documentation

- **[MIGRATION.md](tofu/MIGRATION.md)** - Guide for migrating apps to docker-lxc module pattern
- **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** - This file (project overview and quick reference)

## Project Structure

```text
tofu/
├── MIGRATION.md       # Migration guide for docker-lxc pattern
├── apps/              # Per-app configs with own state
│   ├── dashboards/    # Homepage + Dashy (ID: 201)
│   ├── immich/        # Photo management (ID: 304)
│   ├── monitoring/    # Prometheus + Grafana + Alerting (ID: 500)
│   ├── network-services/  # AdGuard DNS (ID: 101)
│   ├── openwebui/     # AI chat (ID: 501)
│   ├── portainer/     # Container UI (ID: 100)
│   └── traefik/       # Reverse proxy (ID: 200)
├── configs/traefik/dynamic/  # Generated route configs
├── modules/           # Reusable modules
└── shared.tf          # Common vars (symlinked)
```

## Key Modules

- **lxc-base**: Base LXC container with static IP support
- **docker-host**: LXC + Docker + compose deployment
- **file-sync**: Rsync file transfers to LXCs
- **proxmox-notes**: Update LXC description in Proxmox UI

## IP Address Management

All static IPs are tracked in `tofu/ip-registry.tf` (symlinked to all apps).

### IP Ranges

| Range | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| 192.168.1.1-99 | Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches) |
| 192.168.1.100-149 | Core services (Traefik, Portainer, DNS) |
| 192.168.1.150-199 | LXC containers (apps) - **preferred for new deployments** |
| 192.168.1.200-224 | Reserved for manual/temporary use |
| 192.168.1.225-254 | Special services & overflow |

### Deploying a New Service

1. Get the next available IP:

   ```bash
   task ip:next
   # Output: Next available IP: 192.168.1.150
   # For lxc-base module: ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
   ```

2. Add the IP to `tofu/ip-registry.tf`:

   ```hcl
   apps = {
     # ... existing entries ...
     my_new_service = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC XXX - Description
   }
   ```

3. Use in your app's main.tf:

   ```hcl
   module "lxc" {
     source = "../../modules/lxc-base"
     # ...
     ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
     gateway    = "192.168.1.1"
   }
   ```

### Viewing All Allocations

```bash
task ip:list
```

## Network Domains

- `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` - Internal (Traefik websecure)
- `*.rambtech.dev` - Public (Cloudflare tunnel via web entrypoint)

## Monitoring Stack

The monitoring LXC (ID: 500, IP: 192.168.1.229) runs:

| Component | Port | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| OpenTelemetry Collector | 4317/4318 | OTLP receiver (gRPC/HTTP) |
| Prometheus | 9090 | Metrics storage + alerting |
| Alertmanager | 9093 | Alert routing (ntfy + Discord) |
| Grafana | 3000 | Dashboards |
| Uptime Kuma | 3001 | HTTP monitoring |
| ntfy | 8080 | Push notifications |

### Key URLs

- Grafana: `https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Prometheus: `https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Alertmanager: `https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Uptime Kuma: `https://status.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- ntfy: `https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev`

### Syncing Monitoring Config

```bash
rsync -avz tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ root@192.168.1.229:/config/
ssh root@192.168.1.229 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
```

## 1Password Integration

Secrets are managed via the 1Password OpenTofu provider (`1password/onepassword`).

### Key Files

- `tofu/onepassword.tf` - Data sources + `local.op` helper (symlinked to apps)
- `tofu/versions.tf` - Provider configs using `local.op.*`

### Available Secrets

```hcl
local.op.proxmox_api_token       # Proxmox API authentication
local.op.cloudflare_api_token    # Cloudflare DNS/tunnel API
local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token # Cloudflare tunnel token
local.op.grafana_admin_password  # Grafana admin password
local.op.discord_webhook_url     # Discord alertmanager webhook
```

### Adding New Secrets

1. Create item in 1Password `homelab` vault
2. Add data source to `tofu/onepassword.tf`:

   ```hcl
   data "onepassword_item" "myservice" {
     vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
     title = "myservice"
   }
   ```

3. Add to `local.op` map in same file:

   ```hcl
   op = {
     myservice_password = data.onepassword_item.myservice.password
     # For section fields, flatten first then lookup:
     myservice_api_key = lookup(local._myservice_fields, "api_key", "")
   }
   ```

4. Use in modules: `local.op.myservice_password`

### Field Access Patterns

```hcl
# Main password field
data.onepassword_item.myitem.password

# Credential field (API keys)
data.onepassword_item.myitem.credential

# Custom fields in sections (must flatten):
locals {
  _myitem_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.myitem.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)
}
# Then: lookup(local._myitem_fields, "field_label", "")
```

### Why TF_VAR for State Encryption

State encryption runs before providers initialize, so it cannot use the 1Password provider:

```yaml
# Taskfile.yml
env:
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"
```

### 1Password Items (homelab vault)

| Item | Fields |
|------|--------|
| `opentofu` | password, proxmox_api_token (section) |
| `Cloudflare` | tunnel_token, ddns_api_token (sections) |
| `grafana` | password |
| `discord-alertmanager-webhook` | credential |

## Important Notes

- SSH to Proxmox: `ssh root@homelab`
- SSH to Monitoring: `ssh root@192.168.1.229`
- Use IP addresses in provisioners (not hostnames)
- State files are encrypted and committed to git
- Each app has independent state in `tofu/apps/<app>/`
- 1Password CLI v2.23.0+ required (uses biometric auth)

# Homelab Infrastructure Automation
# https://taskfile.dev

version: '3'

vars:
  PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.TASKFILE_DIR}}"
  TOFU_DIR: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}/tofu"

env:
  # State encryption passphrase - MUST be TF_VAR because encryption runs before providers
  # All other secrets are now fetched via 1Password provider directly in OpenTofu
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: |
      if [ -n "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase" ]; then
        echo "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase"
      else
        op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password" 2>/dev/null || echo ""
      fi

# =============================================================================
# Included Taskfiles (flattened into main namespace)
# =============================================================================
includes:
  tofu:
    taskfile: ./tasks/tofu.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  backup:
    taskfile: ./tasks/backup.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  cloud:
    taskfile: ./tasks/cloud.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  template:
    taskfile: ./tasks/template.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  pbs:
    taskfile: ./tasks/pbs.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  importer:
    taskfile: ./tasks/immich-importer.yml
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"
  beads:
    taskfile: ./tasks/beads.yml
    flatten: true
    vars:
      PROJECT_ROOT: "{{.PROJECT_ROOT}}"

tasks:
  # ===========================================================================
  # Desktop LXC (Temporary GUI for Downloads)
  # ===========================================================================

  desktop:create:
    desc: "Create temporary GUI desktop LXC for downloading Google Takeout"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/desktop-lxc/create.sh

  desktop:destroy:
    desc: "Destroy temporary GUI desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/desktop-lxc/destroy.sh

  desktop:info:
    desc: "Show VNC connection info for desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - |
        IP=$(ssh root@homelab "pct exec 600 -- ip -4 addr show eth0 | grep inet | awk '{print \$2}' | cut -d/ -f1" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -z "$IP" ]; then
          echo "Desktop LXC (600) is not running or does not exist."
          echo "Run 'task desktop:create' first."
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "=== Desktop LXC VNC Connection ==="
        echo ""
        echo "VNC Host: $IP:5901"
        echo ""
        echo "macOS: Open Finder, Cmd+K, enter vnc://$IP:5901"
        echo ""
        echo "Downloads save to: /downloads (mounted to /tank/photo-import)"

  desktop:restart-vnc:
    desc: "Restart VNC server on desktop LXC"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "Restarting VNC server..."
        ssh root@homelab "pct exec 600 -- bash -c 'vncserver -kill :1 2>/dev/null || true; vncserver :1 -geometry 1920x1080 -depth 24 -localhost no'"
        echo "VNC server restarted on display :1"

# OpenTofu IaC Commands
# https://taskfile.dev
#
# Each app has its own state file in tofu/apps/<app>/
# Use APP=dashboards|openwebui|portainer|etc to specify which app

version: '3'

vars:
  TOFU_DIR: "tofu"

tasks:
  tofu:init:
    desc: "Initialize OpenTofu for an app (APP=dashboards|openwebui|portainer)"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu init
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:plan:
    desc: "Plan infrastructure changes for an app"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - pwd
      - tofu plan -out=tfplan
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    preconditions:
      - sh: test -d .terraform
        msg: "Run 'task tofu:init APP={{.APP}}' first"

  tofu:apply:
    desc: "Apply planned infrastructure changes for an app (optional: REPLACE='resource.name')"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu apply {{if .REPLACE}}-replace='{{.REPLACE}}' -auto-approve{{else}}tfplan{{end}}
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    preconditions:
      - sh: '{{if .REPLACE}}true{{else}}test -f tfplan{{end}}'
        msg: "Run 'task tofu:plan APP={{.APP}}' first"

  tofu:destroy:
    desc: "Destroy an app's infrastructure"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - echo "⚠️  This will destroy {{.APP}} infrastructure!"
      - tofu destroy
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    prompt: "Are you sure you want to destroy {{.APP}}?"

  tofu:output:
    desc: "Show infrastructure outputs for an app"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu output
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:state:
    desc: "List all resources in an app's state"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu state list
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:state:rm:
    desc: "Remove a resource from state (APP, RESOURCE)"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu state rm '{{.RESOURCE}}'
    requires:
      vars: [APP, RESOURCE]

  tofu:import:
    desc: "Import existing resource into state (APP, ADDR, ID)"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu import '{{.ADDR}}' '{{.ID}}'
    requires:
      vars: [APP, ADDR, ID]

  tofu:show:
    desc: "Show saved plan details for an app"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu show tfplan
    requires:
      vars: [APP]
    preconditions:
      - sh: test -f tfplan
        msg: "Run 'task tofu:plan APP={{.APP}}' first"

  tofu:fmt:
    desc: "Format all Terraform files"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu fmt -recursive

  tofu:validate:
    desc: "Validate an app's configuration"
    dir: "{{.TOFU_DIR}}/apps/{{.APP}}"
    cmds:
      - tofu validate
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:encryption:setup:
    desc: "Set up state encryption passphrase in 1Password"
    cmds:
      - |
        echo "Creating 1Password item for state encryption..."
        PASSPHRASE=$(openssl rand -base64 32)
        op item create \
          --category=password \
          --title="opentofu" \
          --vault="homelab" \
          "password=$PASSPHRASE" \
          "notes=OpenTofu state encryption passphrase for homelab IaC"
        echo "✅ Created 1Password item 'opentofu'"
        echo "The passphrase will be automatically retrieved when running tofu commands"

  tofu:encryption:test:
    desc: "Test state encryption passphrase retrieval"
    cmds:
      - |
        if [ -n "$TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase" ]; then
          echo "✅ State encryption passphrase is set (${#TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase} chars)"
        else
          echo "❌ State encryption passphrase not set"
          echo "Run 'task tofu:encryption:setup' or set TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase"
          exit 1
        fi

  tofu:ssh:
    desc: "SSH to a deployed LXC by app name"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/tofu/ssh.sh {{.APP}}
    requires:
      vars: [APP]

  tofu:logs:
    desc: "View Docker logs from a deployed app"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/tofu/logs.sh {{.APP}} {{.SERVICE}}
    requires:
      vars: [APP, SERVICE]

  tofu:info:
    desc: "Show OpenTofu IaC status"
    cmds:
      - ./scripts/tofu/info.sh

input.prompt: What is the correct format for using an API key with Prometheus metrics? How should the Authorization header be formatted?

content.content:
# API Key Authorization Format for Prometheus Metrics

Based on the documentation, the correct format uses basic authentication with the API key as the password field.

## Command Line Format

For curl requests, the syntax is:

> "curl -u":<key>" uptime.kuma/metrics"

The colon (`:`) before the key is required because basic authentication expects a username and password separated by a colon. The username field remains empty.

## Prometheus Configuration

In your Prometheus scrape config, structure it as:

> "basic_auth: password: <api key>"

The username field doesn't need to be set since it's unused by the system.

## Key Points

- The API key functions as the password in basic authentication
- Always include the `:` separator, even without a username
- Treat API keys with the same security as passwords—they provide access to potentially sensitive metrics data
- Keys can be temporarily disabled or deleted through the settings page if needed

# Alertmanager Configuration
# Routes alerts to ntfy for centralized notification aggregation

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# Route tree
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'severity']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: 'ntfy'

  routes:
    # Critical alerts - immediate notification with high priority
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: 'ntfy-critical'
      group_wait: 10s
      repeat_interval: 1h

    # Warning alerts - batched notifications with default priority
    - match:
        severity: warning
      receiver: 'ntfy'
      group_wait: 1m
      repeat_interval: 4h

# Inhibition rules
inhibit_rules:
  # Inhibit warning if critical is firing for same alertname
  - source_match:
      severity: 'critical'
    target_match:
      severity: 'warning'
    equal: ['alertname', 'instance']

# Receivers
receivers:
  # ntfy receiver for warnings
  - name: 'ntfy'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy - centralized notification aggregator
      # Discord integration will be configured via ntfy webhook subscription
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?priority=default&tags=warning,homelab'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10

  # ntfy receiver for critical alerts
  - name: 'ntfy-critical'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with urgent priority
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?priority=urgent&tags=rotating_light,critical'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10

# Templates for message formatting
templates:
  - '/etc/alertmanager/templates/*.tmpl'

Based on my search results, here's what I found about ntfy Alertmanager webhook message formatting templates:

## ntfy Alertmanager Webhook Integration

### Built-in Alertmanager Template

Templating lets you format a JSON message body into human-friendly message and title text using Go templates. This is specifically useful when combined with webhooks from services such as GitHub, Grafana, Alertmanager, or other services that emit JSON webhooks.(no content)ntfy has a pre-defined `alertmanager` template that formats Alertmanager webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts). You can see the template at `alertmanager.yml`.

### How to Use Templates

To define your own custom templates, place a template file in the template directory (defaults to `/etc/ntfy/templates`, can be overridden with `template-dir`) and set the `X-Template` header or query parameter to the name of the template file (without the `.yml` extension). For example, if you have a template file `/etc/ntfy/templates/myapp.yml`, you can set the header `X-Template: myapp` or the query parameter `?template=myapp` to use it.(no content)Template files must have the `.yml` (not: `.yaml!`) extension and must be formatted as YAML. They may contain `title` and `message` keys, which are interpreted as Go templates.

### Pre-defined Templates Available

The following pre-defined templates are available:
- `github`: Formats a subset of GitHub webhook payloads (PRs, issues, new star, new watcher, new comment)
- `grafana`: Formats Grafana webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts)
- `alertmanager`: Formats Alertmanager webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts)(no content)To override the pre-defined templates, you can place a file with the same name in the template directory.

### Alternative: alertmanager-ntfy Service

There's also a separate project called `alertmanager-ntfy` which is a service that forwards Prometheus Alertmanager notifications to ntfy.sh. It is highly customizable, allowing you to dynamically configure the ntfy notification based on the properties of the alert that is being handled.(no content)Some of the ntfy notification options also accept a gval expression, rather than just a hardcoded value. This allows you to dynamically decide the value of certain notification properties based on the alert that the service is currently handling. For example, if an alert is resolved, you may want to show a different icon than when an alert is currently firing.

### Recent ntfy Features (2024)

Recent ntfy releases added pre-defined templates and custom templates for enhanced JSON webhook support, as well as support of advanced template functions based on the Sprig library.(no content)The release added support for message templating in the ntfy server, which allows you to include a message and/or title template that will be filled with values from a JSON body (e.g. `curl -gd '{"alert":"Disk space low"}' "ntfy.sh/mytopic?tpl=1&m={{.alert}}"`). This is great for services that let you specify a webhook URL but do not let you change the webhook body (such as GitHub, or Grafana).

### Another Bridge Option: ntfy-alertmanager

There's also `ntfy-alertmanager` which supports markdown formatting for notifications. You can optionally provide a path for a rendering template to fine-tune the notification body. It lets you define a decreasing order of labels in the config file and map those labels to tags, priority, an icon, an email address or an alternative ntfy topic.

Based on my search results, here's what I found about ntfy Alertmanager webhook message formatting templates:

## ntfy Alertmanager Webhook Integration

### Built-in Alertmanager Template

Templating lets you format a JSON message body into human-friendly message and title text using Go templates. This is specifically useful when combined with webhooks from services such as GitHub, Grafana, Alertmanager, or other services that emit JSON webhooks.(no content)ntfy has a pre-defined `alertmanager` template that formats Alertmanager webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts). You can see the template at `alertmanager.yml`.

### How to Use Templates

To define your own custom templates, place a template file in the template directory (defaults to `/etc/ntfy/templates`, can be overridden with `template-dir`) and set the `X-Template` header or query parameter to the name of the template file (without the `.yml` extension). For example, if you have a template file `/etc/ntfy/templates/myapp.yml`, you can set the header `X-Template: myapp` or the query parameter `?template=myapp` to use it.(no content)Template files must have the `.yml` (not: `.yaml!`) extension and must be formatted as YAML. They may contain `title` and `message` keys, which are interpreted as Go templates.

### Pre-defined Templates Available

The following pre-defined templates are available:
- `github`: Formats a subset of GitHub webhook payloads (PRs, issues, new star, new watcher, new comment)
- `grafana`: Formats Grafana webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts)
- `alertmanager`: Formats Alertmanager webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts)(no content)To override the pre-defined templates, you can place a file with the same name in the template directory.

### Alternative: alertmanager-ntfy Service

There's also a separate project called `alertmanager-ntfy` which is a service that forwards Prometheus Alertmanager notifications to ntfy.sh. It is highly customizable, allowing you to dynamically configure the ntfy notification based on the properties of the alert that is being handled.(no content)Some of the ntfy notification options also accept a gval expression, rather than just a hardcoded value. This allows you to dynamically decide the value of certain notification properties based on the alert that the service is currently handling. For example, if an alert is resolved, you may want to show a different icon than when an alert is currently firing.

### Recent ntfy Features (2024)

Recent ntfy releases added pre-defined templates and custom templates for enhanced JSON webhook support, as well as support of advanced template functions based on the Sprig library.(no content)The release added support for message templating in the ntfy server, which allows you to include a message and/or title template that will be filled with values from a JSON body (e.g. `curl -gd '{"alert":"Disk space low"}' "ntfy.sh/mytopic?tpl=1&m={{.alert}}"`). This is great for services that let you specify a webhook URL but do not let you change the webhook body (such as GitHub, or Grafana).

### Another Bridge Option: ntfy-alertmanager

There's also `ntfy-alertmanager` which supports markdown formatting for notifications. You can optionally provide a path for a rendering template to fine-tune the notification body. It lets you define a decreasing order of labels in the config file and map those labels to tags, priority, an icon, an email address or an alternative ntfy topic.

# Alertmanager Configuration
# Routes alerts to ntfy for centralized notification aggregation

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# Route tree
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'severity']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: 'ntfy'

  routes:
    # Critical alerts - immediate notification with high priority
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: 'ntfy-critical'
      group_wait: 10s
      repeat_interval: 1h

    # Warning alerts - batched notifications with default priority
    - match:
        severity: warning
      receiver: 'ntfy'
      group_wait: 1m
      repeat_interval: 4h

inhibit_rules:

  - source_match:

You're right, I apologize for jumping ahead.

Looking at the built-in alertmanager template, it already includes a link back to Prometheus via the `Source: {{ .generatorURL }}` field. That will show the Prometheus query URL that triggered the alert.

However, the `generatorURL` that Prometheus sends uses its internal hostname (like `0c501b27369d:9090` from your earlier alerts), which isn't accessible externally. 

We could either:
1. **Configure Prometheus `external_url`** - Set this in Prometheus config so it generates proper URLs like `https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev/...`
2. **Create a custom ntfy template** - Override the built-in template to use a hardcoded Prometheus URL

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # OpenTelemetry Collector - Central telemetry receiver and router
  # ==========================================================================
  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.115.1
    container_name: otel-collector
    command: ["--config=/etc/otelcol/config.yaml"]
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver
      - "8888:8888"   # Prometheus metrics (collector self-metrics)
      - "8889:8889"   # Prometheus exporter (for scraped metrics)
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector/config.yaml:/etc/otelcol/config.yaml:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "/otelcol-contrib", "components"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9093/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.4.0
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.11.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-monitoring
  portainer-edge-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:2.33.5
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:
  portainer_agent_data:

  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.11.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:

      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db

    deploy:

          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped

      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-monitoring
  portainer-edge-agent:
    image: portainer/agent:2.33.5
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

content.content:
# Pulse: Infrastructure Monitoring Platform

## Main Features

Pulse is "a modern, unified dashboard for monitoring your infrastructure across Proxmox, Docker, and Kubernetes." Key capabilities include:

- **Unified Monitoring**: Consolidates metrics from Proxmox VE, PBS, PMG, Docker, and Kubernetes in one interface
- **Smart Alerts**: Notifications via Discord, Slack, Telegram, and email
- **Auto-Discovery**: Automatically locates Proxmox nodes on your network
- **Metrics History**: Persistent storage with configurable data retention
- **Backup Explorer**: Visualizes backup jobs and storage consumption

## Docker & Proxmox Integration

The platform works across multiple deployment models:

- **Docker/Podman**: Monitors container and Swarm service metrics
- **Proxmox VE/PBS/PMG**: Provides "full monitoring and management"
- **OCI Containers**: Supports Proxmox 9.1+ native container functionality

Installation options include a one-liner Proxmox LXC deployment or Docker containerization on port 7655.

## Multi-Host Monitoring

Yes—Pulse handles distributed infrastructure. It monitors "health and metrics for PVE, PBS, PMG, Docker, and Kubernetes in one place," enabling sysadmins and MSPs to manage multiple nodes centrally.

## Key Capabilities (v5.0+)

- **Pulse AI**: Natural language chat assistant, scheduled health checks ("Patrol"), alert analysis, and usage cost tracking
- **Security**: Encrypted credentials, strict API scoping, OIDC/SSO support, privacy-focused design
- **One-click updates**: Streamlined upgrade process

## Tech Stack

- **Backend**: Go (64.8%)
- **Frontend**: TypeScript (28.9%)
- **Deployment**: Shell scripts (5.4%), Docker, Kubernetes, Helm

## Arcane Docker Management

Arcane is a Modern Docker Management solution, designed for everyone.(no content)It provides everything you need to get started with Docker container management.

### Core Features

Arcane covers five main feature domains: Docker resource management (containers, images, volumes, networks), multi-environment support for managing remote Docker hosts, the self-upgrade system, automated image update detection, and Docker Compose project management.

### Multi-Host / Multi-Environment Support

Arcane's multi-environment architecture enables managing multiple Docker hosts (local or remote) from a single Arcane instance. It covers the environment data model, agent pairing mechanism, WebSocket proxying for real-time operations, and health monitoring.(no content)The EnvironmentService enables management of multiple Docker hosts from a single Arcane instance. It supports both local Docker daemons and remote Docker hosts running Arcane agents. The environment service implements agent pairing through a bootstrap token exchange mechanism.

### Remote Agent Setup

Remote Environments let Arcane manage containers on other hosts through a stripped down version of Arcane itself.(no content)You run the Agent on a remote machine (with access to its Docker daemon), pair it to your Arcane manager using a one-time Bootstrap Token, and both sides store an Agent Token for all future requests.

### Environment Service Capabilities

The Environment Service manages multiple Docker environments in Arcane, enabling unified management of both local and remote Docker hosts.(no content)The Environment Service implements transparent WebSocket proxying to forward Docker API WebSocket connections (container logs, stats, exec shells) to remote agents.

### Installation

The simplest way to run Arcane is using a single docker run command. For versions 1.7.2 and earlier, use ghcr.io/ofkm/arcane:latest. For versions after 1.7.2, use ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest.(no content)All Arcane repos have moved to the @getarcaneapp org on GitHub.

## Pulse by rcourtman - Overview

Pulse is a modern, unified dashboard for monitoring your infrastructure across Proxmox, Docker, and Kubernetes. ## Key Features

### Unified Monitoring Capabilities
Features include unified monitoring for PVE, PBS, PMG, Docker, and Kubernetes in one place, smart alerts via Discord, Slack, Telegram, Email, and more, auto-discovery that automatically finds Proxmox nodes on your network, metrics history with persistent storage and configurable retention, backup explorer for visualizing backup jobs and storage usage, and a chat assistant for asking questions about your infrastructure in natural language.

### Docker Monitoring
Pulse can monitor Docker and Podman hosts alongside your Proxmox infrastructure.(no content)Docker monitoring includes container metrics (CPU, Memory, Network, Disk I/O), health checks that track container health status and restart loops, Swarm support with auto-detection of Swarm mode and service/task data, and multi-target capability to report to multiple Pulse servers for HA.

### Proxmox Integration
Proxmox features include auto-discovery that finds Proxmox nodes automatically with one-line installation scripts, cluster monitoring, enterprise security with encrypted credentials, CSRF protection, rate limiting, secure sessions, and bcrypt password hashing, detailed audit logging that tracks logins, configuration changes, and alert history, and live monitoring for real-time performance of VMs, containers, storage, and nodes.

## Architecture
Pulse is a real-time monitoring system designed for Proxmox VE, Proxmox Backup Server, and Docker/Host infrastructure. It is built with a Go backend and a SolidJS frontend, focusing on low latency, high concurrency, and a premium user experience. The system operates as a single binary that serves both the API and the static frontend assets.(no content)For data collection, Proxmox metrics are polled via the Monitoring Engine at a 2-second default interval, while Docker/Host agents push metrics to Pulse at their configured interval (default: 30 seconds).

## Portainer Overview

Portainer is container management software that provides a Docker GUI and a UI-based management tool to simplify Kubernetes and Docker container operations.(no content)It provides a graphical interface for managing containers, networks, and volumes, helping teams handle Kubernetes and Docker environments without relying solely on command-line tools.

## Top Portainer Alternatives

### 1. **Dockge**
Dockge has quickly become the top Portainer alternative, especially if you work with Docker Compose a lot. It gives you a fast, lightweight interface that makes stack management super easy.(no content)While it's not as feature-rich as Portainer, what many users found was a container management tool that meets their needs without any of the extra fluff. Dockge isn't quite a Portainer replacement, but depending on what you use Portainer for, it might work for you.(no content)Portainer has a lot of network management options, full volume controls, an event log, and it even gives you the ability to see every property of a container. Dockge has none of that, but if you're someone who considers themselves to be more of a casual user, then Dockge makes it significantly easier to deploy applications.

### 2. **Rancher**
When comparing Portainer vs Rancher, the key difference is that Portainer provides a UI for managing Kubernetes and Docker, while Rancher is a full Kubernetes management platform designed for multi-cluster orchestration.(no content)If your team runs Kubernetes across multiple clusters, cloud providers, or on-premise environments, Rancher provides a centralized way to manage them all.

### 3. **Komodo**
Komodo is a web app that allows you to have a solution that can give structure to management of your IT infrastructure centered around Docker. This includes things like managing your Docker container hosts, building container images, deploying them, and automated processes.(no content)One advantage of Komodo's containers dashboard compared to Portainer is that you see an aggregated view of all containers across all hosts. This is a capability that some wish Portainer had as it is helpful to have a holistic view. If you are running dozens, hundreds, or even more containers, it makes it much easier to find where a container is running without having to first know the container host specifically.

### 4. **Lazydocker**
Lazydocker takes a completely different approach with a terminal-based UI for Docker. While it's not web-based like the others, its speed and keyboard shortcuts have made it a favorite for many developers in 2025.(no content)For those who prefer the terminal and need maximum speed, Lazydocker is hard to beat.

### 5. **Cockpit Project**
Cockpit Project is the most popular Linux alternative to Portainer.(no content)Cockpit Project is Free and Open Source.

### 6. **Other Enterprise Alternatives**
Red Hat OpenShift is an enterprise Kubernetes solution with built-in CI/CD and security. Lens is an open-source Kubernetes management tool for cluster visualization. KubeSphere is a Kubernetes DevOps platform with automation and multi-tenancy.

## Why Users Look for Alternatives

Some users are tired of Portainer's heavy resource use, don't like the community edition limits, or want special features for their containers.(no content)Portainer provides a UI for managing Kubernetes and Docker, but container orchestration is only part of the equation. Deploying, scaling, and automating workloads require more than a graphical interface. If your team manages production workloads, multi-cluster environments, and infrastructure provisioning, they often need a system that integrates these operations into a single workflow.

## Recommendation Summary

The best Portainer alternative depends on your workflow and priorities. If you mostly use Docker Compose and want a simple, lightweight experience, Dockge is a great choice. It focuses on stack management with a clean interface and minimal resource usage. If you work with both Docker and Kubernetes, Kompose UI offers the smoothest transition between the two. Its built-in conversion tools and multi-environment support make it ideal for hybrid setups.

content.content:
# Remote Environments in Arcane

## How They Work

Remote Environments enable Arcane to manage containers across multiple hosts. According to the documentation, "Remote Environments let Arcane manage containers on other hosts through a stripped down version of Arcane itself." The system uses a pairing mechanism where an Agent running on a remote machine connects to your central Arcane manager.

## Architecture for Multi-Host Management

The setup involves three key components:

1. **Central Manager**: Your main Arcane instance that must be reachable from agent hosts
2. **Remote Agent**: A lightweight version running on each remote Docker host
3. **Authentication**: Uses a one-time Bootstrap Token for initial pairing, then stores an Agent Token for ongoing requests

As explained in the docs, "You run the Agent on a remote machine (with access to its Docker daemon), pair it to your Arcane manager using a one-time Bootstrap Token, and both sides store an Agent Token for all future requests."

## Agent Setup Options

You can deploy the agent via Docker Compose or as a standalone binary. The Docker Compose approach requires setting `AGENT_MODE=true` and `AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` environment variables, plus mounting the Docker socket.

## Security Practice

After successful pairing, you should "remove the bootstrap token from the Agent after successful pairing and restart it." The Agent continues operating using its stored Agent Token for all subsequent communications.

**Network requirement**: Ensure TCP port 3553 is accessible from your manager to each agent host.
