# =============================================================================
# 1Password Provider Configuration
# =============================================================================
# This file provides direct 1Password integration for secret management.
# Secrets are fetched at plan/apply time using the 1Password CLI.
#
# Authentication: Uses 1Password CLI with biometric unlock
# Ensure `op` CLI v2.23.0+ is installed and signed in
#
# Usage: Symlink this file to any app that needs 1Password secrets
#   ln -s ../../../onepassword.tf tofu/apps/<app>/onepassword.tf
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password Vault Reference
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_vault" "homelab" {
  name = "homelab"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core Infrastructure Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenTofu state encryption and Proxmox credentials
data "onepassword_item" "opentofu" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "opentofu"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cloudflare Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "cloudflare" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "Cloudflare"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "grafana" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "grafana"
}

data "onepassword_item" "discord_webhook" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "discord-alertmanager-webhook"
}

data "onepassword_item" "uptime_kuma" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "uptime-kuma"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Portainer Edge Agent Credentials
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each Edge environment in Portainer has unique credentials stored in 1Password.
# Item format: "portainer-edge-<app-name>" with fields:
#   - edge_id: UUID for the Edge environment
#   - edge_key: Base64-encoded connection key
#
# Create items in 1Password:
#   op item create --category=login --title="portainer-edge-dashboards" \
#     --vault=homelab edge_id=<uuid> edge_key=<base64-key>

data "onepassword_item" "portainer_edge" {
  for_each = toset([
    "dashboards",
    "authelia",
    "monitoring",
    "obsidian-sync",
    "jellyfin",
    "immich",
    "n8n",
    "openwebui",
    "traefik",
    "network-services",
    "media-management",
    "documents",
  ])

  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "portainer-edge-${each.key}"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper Locals - Flatten 1Password fields for easy access
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 1Password provider returns fields in a nested structure.
# Custom fields are inside section blocks.

locals {
  # Flatten all section fields from opentofu item into a map by label
  _opentofu_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.opentofu.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Flatten all section fields from cloudflare item into a map by label
  _cloudflare_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # 1Password secrets - access via local.op.<secret_name>
  op = {
    # State encryption passphrase (main password field)
    state_encryption_passphrase = data.onepassword_item.opentofu.password

    # Proxmox API token (custom field in section)
    proxmox_api_token = lookup(local._opentofu_section_fields, "proxmox_api_token", "")

    # Cloudflare (custom fields in sections + standard fields)
    cloudflare_email        = data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.username
    cloudflare_tunnel_token = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "tunnel_token", "")
    cloudflare_api_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "ddns_api_token", lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", ""))
    cloudflare_dns_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", "")

    # Monitoring
    grafana_admin_password  = data.onepassword_item.grafana.password
    discord_webhook_url     = data.onepassword_item.discord_webhook.credential
    uptime_kuma_username    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.username
    uptime_kuma_password    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.password
  }

  # Portainer Edge credentials - access via local.portainer_edge["app-name"]
  # Each entry has .edge_id and .edge_key
  portainer_edge = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => {
      edge_id  = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_id", "")
      edge_key = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_key", "")
    }
  }

  # Helper to flatten Portainer Edge item fields
  _portainer_edge_fields = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => merge(
      # Include top-level fields (username/password/etc)
      {
        "edge_id"  = try(item.username, "")
        "edge_key" = try(item.password, "")
      },
      # Include section fields
      merge([
        for s in try(item.section, []) : {
          for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
        }
      ]...)
    )
  }
}

    { name = "ntfy", port = 8080, info = "Push notifications" },

**OTLP gRPC:** ${local.lan_ips.monitoring}:4317

  --id homelab-otel \

  --server ${local.lan_ips.monitoring} \

- `homelab-status` - Uptime Kuma notifications

  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

}

# =============================================================================
# 1Password Provider Configuration
# =============================================================================
# This file provides direct 1Password integration for secret management.
# Secrets are fetched at plan/apply time using the 1Password CLI.
#
# Authentication: Uses 1Password CLI with biometric unlock
# Ensure `op` CLI v2.23.0+ is installed and signed in
#
# Usage: Symlink this file to any app that needs 1Password secrets
#   ln -s ../../../onepassword.tf tofu/apps/<app>/onepassword.tf
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password Vault Reference
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_vault" "homelab" {
  name = "homelab"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core Infrastructure Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenTofu state encryption and Proxmox credentials
data "onepassword_item" "opentofu" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "opentofu"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cloudflare Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "cloudflare" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "Cloudflare"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "grafana" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "grafana"
}

data "onepassword_item" "discord_webhook" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "discord-alertmanager-webhook"
}

data "onepassword_item" "uptime_kuma" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "uptime-kuma"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Portainer Edge Agent Credentials
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each Edge environment in Portainer has unique credentials stored in 1Password.
# Item format: "portainer-edge-<app-name>" with fields:
#   - edge_id: UUID for the Edge environment
#   - edge_key: Base64-encoded connection key
#
# Create items in 1Password:
#   op item create --category=login --title="portainer-edge-dashboards" \
#     --vault=homelab edge_id=<uuid> edge_key=<base64-key>

data "onepassword_item" "portainer_edge" {
  for_each = toset([
    "dashboards",
    "authelia",
    "monitoring",
    "obsidian-sync",
    "jellyfin",
    "immich",
    "n8n",
    "openwebui",
    "traefik",
    "network-services",
    "media-management",
    "documents",
  ])

  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "portainer-edge-${each.key}"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper Locals - Flatten 1Password fields for easy access
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 1Password provider returns fields in a nested structure.
# Custom fields are inside section blocks.

locals {
  # Flatten all section fields from opentofu item into a map by label
  _opentofu_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.opentofu.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Flatten all section fields from cloudflare item into a map by label
  _cloudflare_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # 1Password secrets - access via local.op.<secret_name>
  op = {
    # State encryption passphrase (main password field)
    state_encryption_passphrase = data.onepassword_item.opentofu.password

    # Proxmox API token (custom field in section)
    proxmox_api_token = lookup(local._opentofu_section_fields, "proxmox_api_token", "")

    # Cloudflare (custom fields in sections + standard fields)
    cloudflare_email        = data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.username
    cloudflare_tunnel_token = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "tunnel_token", "")
    cloudflare_api_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "ddns_api_token", lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", ""))
    cloudflare_dns_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", "")

    # Monitoring
    grafana_admin_password  = data.onepassword_item.grafana.password
    discord_webhook_url     = data.onepassword_item.discord_webhook.credential
    uptime_kuma_username    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.username
    uptime_kuma_password    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.password
  }

  # Portainer Edge credentials - access via local.portainer_edge["app-name"]
  # Each entry has .edge_id and .edge_key
  portainer_edge = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => {
      edge_id  = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_id", "")
      edge_key = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_key", "")
    }
  }

  # Helper to flatten Portainer Edge item fields
  _portainer_edge_fields = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => merge(
      # Include top-level fields (username/password/etc)
      {
        "edge_id"  = try(item.username, "")
        "edge_key" = try(item.password, "")
      },
      # Include section fields
      merge([
        for s in try(item.section, []) : {
          for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
        }
      ]...)
    )
  }
}

    "monitoring",
    "obsidian-sync",
    "jellyfin",
    "immich",
    "n8n",
    "openwebui",
    "traefik",
    "network-services",
    "media-management",
    "documents",
  ])

  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "portainer-edge-${each.key}"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper Locals - Flatten 1Password fields for easy access
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 1Password provider returns fields in a nested structure.
# Custom fields are inside section blocks.

locals {
  # Flatten all section fields from opentofu item into a map by label
  _opentofu_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.opentofu.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Flatten all section fields from cloudflare item into a map by label
  _cloudflare_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Flatten all section fields from arcane item into a map by label
  _arcane_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.arcane.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # 1Password secrets - access via local.op.<secret_name>
  op = {
    # State encryption passphrase (main password field)
    state_encryption_passphrase = data.onepassword_item.opentofu.password

    # Proxmox API token (custom field in section)
    proxmox_api_token = lookup(local._opentofu_section_fields, "proxmox_api_token", "")

    # Cloudflare (custom fields in sections + standard fields)
    cloudflare_email        = data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.username
    cloudflare_tunnel_token = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "tunnel_token", "")
    cloudflare_api_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "ddns_api_token", lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", ""))
    cloudflare_dns_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", "")

    # Monitoring
    grafana_admin_password  = data.onepassword_item.grafana.password
    discord_webhook_url     = data.onepassword_item.discord_webhook.credential
    uptime_kuma_username    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.username
    uptime_kuma_password    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.password
  }

  # Portainer Edge credentials - access via local.portainer_edge["app-name"]
  # Each entry has .edge_id and .edge_key
  portainer_edge = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => {
      edge_id  = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_id", "")
      edge_key = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_key", "")
    }
  }

  # Helper to flatten Portainer Edge item fields
  _portainer_edge_fields = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => merge(
      # Include top-level fields (username/password/etc)
      {
        "edge_id"  = try(item.username, "")
        "edge_key" = try(item.password, "")
      },
      # Include section fields
      merge([
        for s in try(item.section, []) : {
          for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
        }
      ]...)
    )
  }
}

input.content:
# =============================================================================
# Container Management LXC - Pulse + Arcane
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 104
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Container monitoring (Pulse) and management (Arcane) to replace Portainer.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 104
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 16
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Container Management LXC
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "container_mgmt" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "container-mgmt"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only - no LAN access needed)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.core.container_mgmt}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 512

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Container Management"
  service_description = "Pulse monitoring + Arcane container management (Portainer replacement)"

  service_urls = {
    pulse  = "https://pulse.${var.domain_internal}"
    arcane = "https://arcane.${var.domain_internal}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Pulse", port = 7655, info = "Proxmox + Docker monitoring" },
    { name = "Arcane", port = 3552, info = "Docker container management" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Pulse - Container Monitoring

Real-time monitoring for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
- Dashboard: https://pulse.${var.domain_internal}
- Proxmox metrics via PVE API
- Docker metrics via socket

## Arcane - Container Management

Docker container management with update detection.
- Dashboard: https://arcane.${var.domain_internal}
- Remote agents connect from other LXCs

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f pulse
cd /config && docker compose logs -f arcane
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=container-mgmt` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["pulse", "arcane", "management"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

resource "local_sensitive_file" "container_mgmt_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    pulse_admin_user      = local.op.pulse_admin_user
    pulse_admin_password  = local.op.pulse_admin_password
    arcane_encryption_key = local.op.arcane_encryption_key
    arcane_jwt_secret     = local.op.arcane_jwt_secret
  })
  filename        = "${path.module}/.terraform/container-mgmt.env"
  file_permission = "0600"
}

resource "filesync_file" "container_mgmt_env" {
  source      = local_sensitive_file.container_mgmt_env.filename
  destination = "/config/.env"
  host        = module.container_mgmt.ip_address

  mode = "0600"

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "pulse_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "pulse"
  backend_url = "http://${module.container_mgmt.ip_address}:7655"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "pulse.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

module "arcane_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "arcane"
  backend_url = "http://${module.container_mgmt.ip_address}:3552"

  internal_domain = "arcane.${var.domain_internal}"

  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "container_mgmt_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.container_mgmt.container_id
  container_ip   = module.container_mgmt.ip_address
  container_name = "container-mgmt"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "Sun 03:00" # Weekly backup
    retention = "4"         # Keep 4 weekly backups
    namespace = "lxc-104"

    pre_backup_commands = [] # No database - config only

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,container-mgmt"
  }

  depends_on = [module.container_mgmt]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.container_mgmt.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    pulse  = module.pulse_route.internal_url
    arcane = module.arcane_route.internal_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    pulse  = module.pulse_route.remote_config_path
    arcane = module.arcane_route.remote_config_path
  }
}

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Pulse - Proxmox and Docker Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================
  # Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
  # Lightweight alternative to full observability stacks.
  pulse:
    image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:latest
    container_name: pulse
    ports:
      - "7655:7655"
    environment:
      # Proxmox VE connection (configured in web UI after first launch)
      # Uses existing proxmox_api_token from 1Password
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - pulse_data:/app/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7655/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Arcane - Docker Container Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # Modern Docker management UI with update detection.
  # Manages containers via remote agents on other LXCs.
  arcane:
    image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest
    container_name: arcane
    ports:
      - "3552:3000"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - APP_URL=https://arcane.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - ENCRYPTION_KEY=${ARCANE_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - JWT_SECRET=${ARCANE_JWT_SECRET}
    volumes:
      - arcane_data:/app/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

volumes:
  pulse_data:
  arcane_data:

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Pulse - Proxmox and Docker Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================
  # Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
  # Lightweight alternative to full observability stacks.
  pulse:
    image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:latest
    container_name: pulse
    ports:
      - "7655:7655"
    environment:
      # Proxmox VE connection (configured in web UI after first launch)
      # Uses existing proxmox_api_token from 1Password
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - pulse_data:/app/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7655/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Arcane - Docker Container Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # Modern Docker management UI with update detection.
  # Manages containers via remote agents on other LXCs.
  arcane:
    image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest
    container_name: arcane
    ports:
      - "3552:3000"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - APP_URL=https://arcane.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - ENCRYPTION_KEY=${ARCANE_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - JWT_SECRET=${ARCANE_JWT_SECRET}
    volumes:
      - arcane_data:/app/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Pulse - Proxmox and Docker Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================
  # Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
  # Lightweight alternative to full observability stacks.
  pulse:
    image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:latest
    container_name: pulse
    ports:
      - "7655:7655"
    environment:
      # Proxmox VE connection (configured in web UI after first launch)
      # Uses existing proxmox_api_token from 1Password
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - pulse_data:/app/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7655/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Arcane - Docker Container Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # Modern Docker management UI with update detection.
  # Manages containers via remote agents on other LXCs.
  arcane:
    image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest
    container_name: arcane
    ports:
      - "3552:3000"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - APP_URL=https://arcane.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - ENCRYPTION_KEY=${ARCANE_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - JWT_SECRET=${ARCANE_JWT_SECRET}
    volumes:
      - arcane_data:/app/data
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

# Arcane Docker Compose Configuration with Socket Proxy

## Core Setup

The documentation provides a complete compose.yaml configuration featuring two services:

**Docker Socket Proxy Service:**
- Image: `tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest`
- Container name: `arcane-docker-proxy`
- Mounted socket: `/var/run/docker.sock:ro` (read-only)
- Network: `arcane-internal` (internal bridge)

**Arcane Service:**
- Image: `ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest`
- Port: `3552:3552`
- Data volume: `arcane-data:/app/data`

## Required Environment Variables

**For Arcane:**
```
DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
PUID=1000
PGID=1000
ENCRYPTION_KEY=[generated value]
JWT_SECRET=[generated value]
```

**For Socket Proxy (access control):**
Essential endpoints set to `1`: `EVENTS`, `PING`, `VERSION`, `CONTAINERS`, `EXEC`, `IMAGES`, `NETWORKS`, `VOLUMES`, `POST`, `INFO`

Security-critical settings disabled: `AUTH=0`, `SECRETS=0`

## Key Features

The configuration establishes a "security layer" through the proxy rather than direct socket access. Arcane depends on the proxy service via `depends_on`, ensuring startup order. The setup includes health checks monitoring the `/api/health` endpoint.

**Initial credentials:** Username `arcane` / Password `arcane-admin`

- Image: `tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest`
- Container name: `arcane-docker-proxy`
- Mounted socket: `/var/run/docker.sock:ro` (read-only)
- Network: `arcane-internal` (internal bridge)

**Arcane Service:**
- Image: `ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest`
- Port: `3552:3552`
- Data volume: `arcane-data:/app/data`

## Required Environment Variables

**For Arcane:**
```
DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
PUID=1000
PGID=1000
ENCRYPTION_KEY=[generated value]
JWT_SECRET=[generated value]
```

**For Socket Proxy (access control):**
Essential endpoints set to `1`: `EVENTS`, `PING`, `VERSION`, `CONTAINERS`, `EXEC`, `IMAGES`, `NETWORKS`, `VOLUMES`, `POST`, `INFO`

Security-critical settings disabled: `AUTH=0`, `SECRETS=0`

## Key Features

The configuration establishes a "security layer" through the proxy rather than direct socket access. Arcane depends on the proxy service via `depends_on`, ensuring startup order. The setup includes health checks monitoring the `/api/health` endpoint.

**Initial credentials:** Username `arcane` / Password `arcane-admin`

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Docker Socket Proxy - Secure Docker API access
  # ==========================================================================
  # Provides a filtered API proxy to Docker socket for security
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest
    container_name: docker-socket-proxy
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    environment:
      # Container management
      - CONTAINERS=1
      - EXEC=1
      - IMAGES=1
      - NETWORKS=1
      - VOLUMES=1
      - POST=1
      # Status/info
      - EVENTS=1
      - PING=1
      - VERSION=1
      - INFO=1
      # Security: disable sensitive endpoints
      - AUTH=0
      - SECRETS=0
    networks:
      - internal
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.1'
        reservations:
          memory: 32m
          cpus: '0.05'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:2375/version || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3

# =============================================================================
# LXC Sidecars Module
# =============================================================================
# Manages sidecar services for LXC containers:
#   - Backup: proxmox-backup-client with PBS integration
#   - DIUN: Docker image update notifications (future)
#   - Promtail: Log collection for Loki (future)
#   - cAdvisor: Container metrics (future)
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Backup Sidecar (PBS Client)
# =============================================================================

resource "ansible_navigator_run" "configure_backup" {
  count = var.backup != null && var.backup.enabled ? 1 : 0

  triggers = {
    container_id        = var.container_id
    container_ip        = var.container_ip
    namespace           = var.backup.namespace
    schedule            = var.backup.schedule
    retention           = var.backup.retention
    pre_backup_commands = jsonencode(var.backup.pre_backup_commands)
    include_paths       = jsonencode(var.backup.include_paths)
    exclude_paths       = jsonencode(var.backup.exclude_paths)
    pbs_server          = var.backup.pbs_server
    pbs_datastore       = var.backup.pbs_datastore
  }

  execution_environment = {
    enabled = false  # Run ansible directly on host, not in container
  }

  ansible_options = {
    private_keys = [{
      name = "homelab"
      data = file(var.proxmox_ssh_private_key_path)
    }]
  }

  playbook = templatefile("${path.module}/templates/configure-backup-playbook.yml.tftpl", {
    container_id        = var.container_id
    container_ip        = var.container_ip
    container_name      = var.container_name
    namespace           = var.backup.namespace
    schedule            = var.backup.schedule
    retention           = var.backup.retention
    pre_backup_commands = var.backup.pre_backup_commands
    include_paths       = var.backup.include_paths
    exclude_paths       = var.backup.exclude_paths
    pbs_server          = var.backup.pbs_server
    pbs_datastore       = var.backup.pbs_datastore
    pbs_user            = var.backup.pbs_user
    pbs_password_cmd    = var.backup.pbs_password_cmd
    ntfy_url            = var.backup.ntfy_url
    ntfy_priority       = var.backup.ntfy_priority
    ntfy_tags           = var.backup.ntfy_tags
    backup_script       = templatefile("${path.module}/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl", {
      container_id        = var.container_id
      container_name      = var.container_name
      namespace           = var.backup.namespace
      schedule            = var.backup.schedule
      retention           = var.backup.retention
      pre_backup_commands = var.backup.pre_backup_commands
      include_paths       = var.backup.include_paths
      exclude_paths       = var.backup.exclude_paths
      ntfy_url            = var.backup.ntfy_url
      ntfy_priority       = var.backup.ntfy_priority
      ntfy_tags           = var.backup.ntfy_tags
    })
  })

  inventory = yamlencode({
    lxc = {
      hosts = {
        (var.container_name) = {
          ansible_host = var.container_ip
          ansible_user = "root"
        }
      }
    }
  })
}

# =============================================================================
# Future Sidecars (Placeholder)
# =============================================================================

# TODO: Add DIUN docker-compose deployment when diun_enabled = true
# TODO: Add Promtail docker-compose deployment when promtail_enabled = true
# TODO: Add cAdvisor docker-compose deployment when cadvisor_enabled = true

# =============================================================================
# LXC Sidecars Module Variables
# =============================================================================
# This module manages sidecar services for LXC containers:
#   - Backup (proxmox-backup-client with PBS)
#   - DIUN (Docker image update notifications) - Future
#   - Promtail (Log collection for Loki) - Future
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Container Information
# =============================================================================

variable "container_id" {
  description = "LXC container ID"
  type        = number
}

variable "container_ip" {
  description = "Container IP address (without CIDR)"
  type        = string
}

variable "container_name" {
  description = "Container hostname"
  type        = string
}

# =============================================================================
# Proxmox SSH Connection (for Ansible deployment)
# =============================================================================

variable "proxmox_ssh_host" {
  description = "Proxmox host SSH address"
  type        = string
}

variable "proxmox_ssh_private_key_path" {
  description = "Path to SSH private key for Proxmox host"
  type        = string
}

# =============================================================================
# Backup Configuration
# =============================================================================

variable "backup" {
  description = "Backup configuration for PBS client"
  type = object({
    enabled     = bool
    schedule    = string                    # "daily", "02:00", "Sun 03:00"
    retention   = optional(string, "7")     # Keep N backups
    namespace   = string                    # PBS namespace (usually container name)

    # Pre-backup commands (database dumps, etc.)
    pre_backup_commands = optional(list(object({
      name    = string
      command = string
      timeout = optional(number, 300)
    })), [])

    # Paths to backup/exclude
    include_paths = optional(list(string), ["/config"])
    exclude_paths = optional(list(string), ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"])

    # PBS server settings
    pbs_server     = optional(string, "10.100.1.102")
    pbs_datastore  = optional(string, "homelab")
    pbs_user       = optional(string, "backup@pbs")
    pbs_password_cmd = optional(string, "op read 'op://homelab/PBS - Proxmox Backup Server/password'")

    # Alert settings
    ntfy_url      = optional(string, "http://10.100.5.100:8080/homelab-alerts")
    ntfy_priority = optional(string, "default")
    ntfy_tags     = optional(string, "backup")
  })
  default = null

  validation {
    condition = var.backup == null || (
      var.backup.enabled == true && var.backup.namespace != ""
    )
    error_message = "If backup is enabled, namespace must be provided."
  }

  validation {
    condition = var.backup == null || (
      var.backup.schedule == "daily" ||
      can(regex("^[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$", var.backup.schedule)) ||
      can(regex("^(mon|tue|wed|thu|fri|sat|sun) [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$", lower(var.backup.schedule)))
    )
    error_message = "Schedule must be 'daily', 'HH:MM', or 'day HH:MM' (e.g., 'Sun 03:00')."
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# Future Sidecars (Placeholder)
# =============================================================================

variable "diun_enabled" {
  description = "Enable DIUN for Docker image update notifications"
  type        = bool
  default     = false
}

variable "promtail_enabled" {
  description = "Enable Promtail for log collection"
  type        = bool
  default     = false
}

variable "cadvisor_enabled" {
  description = "Enable cAdvisor for container metrics"

     4→# =============================================================================

     6→# It configures proxmox-backup-client for zero-downtime incremental backups.
     7→# =============================================================================

    10→  hosts: ${container_name}
    11→  gather_facts: true
    12→
    13→  vars:
    14→    container_id: ${container_id}
    15→    namespace: ${namespace}
    16→    schedule: ${schedule}
    17→    retention: ${retention}
    18→    pbs_server: ${pbs_server}
    19→    pbs_datastore: ${pbs_datastore}
    20→    pbs_user: ${pbs_user}
    21→    pbs_password_cmd: ${pbs_password_cmd}
    22→    pbs_repository: ${pbs_user}@${pbs_server}:${pbs_datastore}
    23→
    24→    backup_script_dir: /usr/local/bin/pbs-backup
    25→    backup_script_path: /usr/local/bin/pbs-backup/backup-${container_id}.sh
    26→    log_dir: /var/log/pbs-backups
    27→    log_file: /var/log/pbs-backups/${namespace}.log
    28→
    29→    systemd_service_name: pbs-backup-${container_id}.service
    30→    systemd_timer_name: pbs-backup-${container_id}.timer
    31→
    32→    ntfy_url: ${ntfy_url}
    33→    ntfy_priority: ${ntfy_priority}
    34→    ntfy_tags: ${ntfy_tags}
    35→
    36→  tasks:
    37→    # =========================================================================
    38→    # Install proxmox-backup-client
    39→    # =========================================================================

    41→      ansible.builtin.command:

    43→      register: pbs_client_check
    44→      changed_when: false
    45→      failed_when: false

    49→        name:
    50→          - curl
    51→          - ca-certificates
    52→        state: present
    53→        update_cache: true
    54→      when: pbs_client_check.rc != 0
    55→
    56→    - name: Download proxmox-backup-client binary
    57→      ansible.builtin.get_url:

    59→        dest: /usr/local/bin/proxmox-backup-client

    61→        checksum: sha256:85b477e2f17b86947f332cfe71ccfc365e1c9821a7a748899b13fcffbcd0c8f9
    62→      when: pbs_client_check.rc != 0

   160→          Wants=network-online.target

---
# =============================================================================
# Configure PBS Backup Client in LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
# It configures proxmox-backup-client for zero-downtime incremental backups.
# =============================================================================

- name: Configure PBS backup for ${container_name}
  hosts: ${container_name}
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    container_id: ${container_id}
    namespace: ${namespace}
    schedule: ${schedule}
    retention: ${retention}
    pbs_server: ${pbs_server}
    pbs_datastore: ${pbs_datastore}
    pbs_user: ${pbs_user}
    pbs_password_cmd: ${pbs_password_cmd}
    pbs_repository: ${pbs_user}@${pbs_server}:${pbs_datastore}

    backup_script_dir: /usr/local/bin/pbs-backup
    backup_script_path: /usr/local/bin/pbs-backup/backup-${container_id}.sh
    log_dir: /var/log/pbs-backups
    log_file: /var/log/pbs-backups/${namespace}.log

    systemd_service_name: pbs-backup-${container_id}.service
    systemd_timer_name: pbs-backup-${container_id}.timer

    ntfy_url: ${ntfy_url}
    ntfy_priority: ${ntfy_priority}
    ntfy_tags: ${ntfy_tags}

  tasks:
    # =========================================================================
    # Install proxmox-backup-client
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Check if proxmox-backup-client is already installed
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: which proxmox-backup-client
      register: pbs_client_check
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Install proxmox-backup-client dependencies
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        name:
          - curl
          - ca-certificates
        state: present
        update_cache: true
      when: pbs_client_check.rc != 0

    - name: Download proxmox-backup-client binary
      ansible.builtin.get_url:
        url: https://cloud-pbs.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/proxmox-backup-client
        dest: /usr/local/bin/proxmox-backup-client
        mode: '0755'
        checksum: sha256:85b477e2f17b86947f332cfe71ccfc365e1c9821a7a748899b13fcffbcd0c8f9
      when: pbs_client_check.rc != 0

    - name: Verify proxmox-backup-client installation
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: proxmox-backup-client version
      register: pbs_version_check
      changed_when: false

    - name: Display proxmox-backup-client version
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg: "{{ pbs_version_check.stdout }}"

    # =========================================================================
    # Configure PBS Password
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create PBS encryption key directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /root/.config/proxmox-backup
        state: directory
        mode: '0700'

    - name: Get PBS certificate fingerprint
      ansible.builtin.shell:
        cmd: |
          ssh root@{{ pbs_server }} "proxmox-backup-manager cert info" | \
          grep "Fingerprint (sha256):" | \
          awk '{print $NF}'
      register: pbs_fingerprint
      changed_when: false
      delegate_to: localhost

    - name: Get PBS password from 1Password
      ansible.builtin.shell:
        cmd: ${pbs_password_cmd}
      register: pbs_password
      changed_when: false
      delegate_to: localhost
      no_log: true

    - name: Store PBS password and fingerprint in environment file
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          PBS_REPOSITORY={{ pbs_repository }}
          PBS_NAMESPACE={{ namespace }}
          PBS_PASSWORD={{ pbs_password.stdout }}
          PBS_FINGERPRINT={{ pbs_fingerprint.stdout }}
        dest: /root/.pbs-backup-env
        mode: '0600'
      no_log: true

    # =========================================================================
    # Create PBS Namespace (if specified and doesn't exist)
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create PBS namespace
      ansible.builtin.shell:
        cmd: |
          set -a
          source /root/.pbs-backup-env
          set +a
          proxmox-backup-client namespace create {{ namespace }} --repository {{ pbs_repository }}
        executable: /bin/bash
      register: namespace_create
      changed_when: "'created namespace' in namespace_create.stdout or namespace_create.rc == 0"
      failed_when: false
      no_log: true
      when: namespace != ""

    # =========================================================================
    # Create Backup Script
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create backup script directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ backup_script_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Create log directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ log_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    - name: Deploy backup script
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          ${indent(10, backup_script)}
        dest: "{{ backup_script_path }}"
        mode: '0755'

    # =========================================================================
    # Create Systemd Service & Timer
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create systemd service
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          [Unit]
          Description=PBS Backup for ${container_name} (${namespace})
          After=network-online.target
          Wants=network-online.target

          [Service]
          Type=oneshot
          EnvironmentFile=/root/.pbs-backup-env
          ExecStart={{ backup_script_path }}
          StandardOutput=append:{{ log_file }}
          StandardError=append:{{ log_file }}

          # Resource limits
          CPUQuota=50%
          MemoryMax=1G

          [Install]
          WantedBy=multi-user.target
        dest: /etc/systemd/system/{{ systemd_service_name }}
        mode: '0644'
      register: service_file

    - name: Determine systemd timer schedule
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        timer_oncalendar: |-
          {%- if schedule == "daily" -%}
          daily
          {%- elif schedule | regex_search('^[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$') -%}
          *-*-* {{ schedule }}
          {%- else -%}
          {{ schedule }}
          {%- endif -%}

    - name: Create systemd timer
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          [Unit]
          Description=Timer for PBS Backup of ${container_name}

          [Timer]
          OnCalendar={{ timer_oncalendar }}
          Persistent=true
          RandomizedDelaySec=5min

          [Install]
          WantedBy=timers.target
        dest: /etc/systemd/system/{{ systemd_timer_name }}
        mode: '0644'
      register: timer_file

    - name: Reload systemd daemon
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        daemon_reload: true
      when: service_file is changed or timer_file is changed

    - name: Enable and start timer
      ansible.builtin.systemd:
        name: "{{ systemd_timer_name }}"
        enabled: true
        state: started

    # =========================================================================
    # Verify Configuration
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Check timer status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: systemctl status {{ systemd_timer_name }}
      register: timer_status
      changed_when: false
      failed_when: false

    - name: Display configuration summary
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== PBS Backup Configured for ${container_name} ==="
          - ""
          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
          - "Namespace: ${namespace}"
          - "Schedule: {{ timer_oncalendar }}"
          - "Repository: {{ pbs_repository }}"
          - "Log file: {{ log_file }}"
          - ""
          - "Manual trigger:"
          - "  systemctl start {{ systemd_service_name }}"
          - ""
          - "Check timer:"
          - "  systemctl list-timers {{ systemd_timer_name }}"
          - ""
          - "View logs:"
          - "  tail -f {{ log_file }}"

## Arcane Docker Remote Agent Headless Setup

Remote Environments let Arcane manage containers on other hosts through a stripped down version of Arcane itself.(no content)You run the Agent on a remote machine (with access to its Docker daemon), pair it to your Arcane manager using a one-time Bootstrap Token, and both sides store an Agent Token for all future requests.

### Docker Compose Setup for the Agent

The agent uses the `ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest` image. Here's the docker-compose configuration:

```yaml
services:
  arcane-agent:
    image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest
    container_name: arcane-agent
    ports:
      - '3553:3553'
    environment:
      - AGENT_MODE=true
      # Use a strong, temporary bootstrap token for pairing:
      - AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=this-is-my-test-bs-token
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - agent-data:/app/data
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  agent-data: {}
```

### Key Environment Variables

- **AGENT_MODE** (required): Set to `true` to run in Agent mode.
- **AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN** (pairing only): One-time secret used to mint the Agent Token.

### Troubleshooting

- **401/403 during pairing**: Bootstrap token mismatch; ensure AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN equals the value provided in Arcane.
- **Connection errors**: Ensure port 3553 is reachable from the Manager to the Agent host.
- **Docker access issues**: Verify /var/run/docker.sock is mounted and the container user has permissions.

### Image Repository Note

All Arcane repos have moved to the @getarcaneapp org on GitHub. This means the images used for Arcane for all future releases (past 1.7.2) will use the new repositories.(no content)For versions 1.7.2 and earlier, use `ghcr.io/ofkm/arcane:latest`. For versions after 1.7.2, use `ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest`.

## Pulse Docker Agent Setup for Remote Host Monitoring

Pulse is a responsive monitoring platform for Proxmox VE, PBS, and Docker with real-time metrics across nodes and containers.

### Installing the Docker Agent

You can monitor Docker and Podman hosts alongside your Proxmox infrastructure. Generate an installation command in the UI: Settings → Agents → Docker Agents → "Install New Agent"

```bash
curl -fsSL http://<pulse-ip>:7655/install-docker-agent.sh | \
  sudo bash -s -- --url http://<pulse-ip>:7655 --token <api-token>
```

This creates a pulse-docker-agent systemd service.

### Running Agent as a Container

You can run the agent as a container instead of a system service:

```bash
docker run -d \
  --name pulse-agent \
  --pid=host --uts=host \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -e PULSE_URL="http://pulse:7655" \
  -e PULSE_TOKEN="<token>" \
  ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
```

### Features

The Docker agent provides:
- Container Metrics: CPU, Memory, Network, Disk I/O
- Health Checks: Tracks container health status and restart loops
- Swarm Support: Auto-detects Swarm mode and reports service/task data
- Multi-Target: Can report to multiple Pulse servers for HA

### Configuration

The agent is configured via flags or environment variables (in /etc/pulse/pulse-docker-agent.env).

### Troubleshooting

If a host was previously removed, you must "Allow re-enroll" in Settings → Docker → Removed Hosts.(no content)For permission denied (socket) errors, ensure the pulse-docker user is in the docker group using `sudo usermod -aG docker pulse-docker`.(no content)If you see duplicate hosts or agents flip-flopping in the UI, they share a machine-id.

### Host Agent (for non-Docker hosts)

You can also monitor standalone Linux, macOS, and Windows servers that don't run Proxmox or Docker. Generate an installation command in the UI: Settings → Agents → Host Agents → "Install New Agent"(no content)The Host Agent provides:
- System Metrics: CPU, Memory, Disk, Network I/O
- Temperature: Auto-detects sensors via lm-sensors (Linux)
- RAID Monitoring: Auto-detects mdadm arrays (Linux)
- Smart Alerts: Integrated with Pulse's alerting engine

# LXC Sidecars Module Variables
# =============================================================================
# This module manages sidecar services for LXC containers:
#   - Backup (proxmox-backup-client with PBS)
#   - DIUN (Docker image update notifications) - Future
#   - Promtail (Log collection for Loki) - Future
# =============================================================================

# =============================================================================
# Container Information
# =============================================================================

variable "container_id" {
  description = "LXC container ID"
  type        = number
}

variable "container_ip" {
  description = "Container IP address (without CIDR)"
  type        = string
}

variable "container_name" {
  description = "Container hostname"
  type        = string
}

# =============================================================================
# Proxmox SSH Connection (for Ansible deployment)
# =============================================================================

variable "proxmox_ssh_host" {
  description = "Proxmox host SSH address"
  type        = string
}

variable "proxmox_ssh_private_key_path" {
  description = "Path to SSH private key for Proxmox host"
  type        = string
}

# =============================================================================
# Backup Configuration
# =============================================================================

variable "backup" {
  description = "Backup configuration for PBS client"
  type = object({
    enabled     = bool
    schedule    = string                    # "daily", "02:00", "Sun 03:00"
    retention   = optional(string, "7")     # Keep N backups
    namespace   = string                    # PBS namespace (usually container name)

    # Pre-backup commands (database dumps, etc.)
    pre_backup_commands = optional(list(object({
      name    = string
      command = string
      timeout = optional(number, 300)
    })), [])

    # Paths to backup/exclude
    include_paths = optional(list(string), ["/config"])
    exclude_paths = optional(list(string), ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"])

    # PBS server settings
    pbs_server     = optional(string, "10.100.1.102")
    pbs_datastore  = optional(string, "homelab")
    pbs_user       = optional(string, "backup@pbs")
    pbs_password_cmd = optional(string, "op read 'op://homelab/PBS - Proxmox Backup Server/password'")

    # Alert settings
    ntfy_url      = optional(string, "http://10.100.5.100:8080/homelab-alerts")
    ntfy_priority = optional(string, "default")
    ntfy_tags     = optional(string, "backup")
  })
  default = null

  validation {
    condition = var.backup == null || (
      var.backup.enabled == true && var.backup.namespace != ""
    )
    error_message = "If backup is enabled, namespace must be provided."
  }

  validation {
    condition = var.backup == null || (
      var.backup.schedule == "daily" ||
      can(regex("^[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$", var.backup.schedule)) ||
      can(regex("^(mon|tue|wed|thu|fri|sat|sun) [0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$", lower(var.backup.schedule)))
    )
    error_message = "Schedule must be 'daily', 'HH:MM', or 'day HH:MM' (e.g., 'Sun 03:00')."
  }
}

  type        = bool
  default     = false
}

variable "cadvisor_enabled" {
  description = "Enable cAdvisor for container metrics"
  type        = bool

---
# =============================================================================
# Configure Pulse Docker Agent in LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
# It deploys the Pulse Docker agent for container monitoring.
# =============================================================================

- name: Configure Pulse agent for ${container_name}
  hosts: ${container_name}
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    container_id: ${container_id}
    container_name: ${container_name}
    pulse_url: ${pulse_url}
    pulse_token: ${pulse_token}

    agent_compose_dir: /config/sidecars
    agent_compose_file: /config/sidecars/pulse-agent.yml

  tasks:
    # =========================================================================
    # Create Sidecar Directory
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create sidecars directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ agent_compose_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Pulse Agent Docker Compose
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Deploy Pulse agent docker-compose
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          services:
            pulse-agent:
              image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
              container_name: pulse-agent
              pid: host
              uts: host
              environment:
                - PULSE_URL={{ pulse_url }}
                - PULSE_TOKEN={{ pulse_token }}
              volumes:
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.25'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 64m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
              healthcheck:
                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep pulse-docker-agent || exit 1"]
                interval: 30s
                timeout: 10s
                retries: 3
                start_period: 30s
        dest: "{{ agent_compose_file }}"
        mode: '0644'
      register: compose_file

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Agent Container
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Pull Pulse agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
      changed_when: true

    - name: Deploy Pulse agent container
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker compose -f {{ agent_compose_file }} up -d --remove-orphans
      register: deploy_result
      changed_when: "'Started' in deploy_result.stderr or 'Creating' in deploy_result.stderr"

    # =========================================================================
    # Verify Deployment
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Wait for agent to start
      ansible.builtin.pause:
        seconds: 5

    - name: Check agent container status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=pulse-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: agent_status
      changed_when: false

    - name: Display deployment summary
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== Pulse Agent Deployed for ${container_name} ==="
          - ""
          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
          - "Pulse URL: {{ pulse_url }}"
          - "Agent Status: {{ agent_status.stdout }}"
          - ""
          - "View logs:"
          - "  docker logs -f pulse-agent"
          - ""
          - "Restart agent:"
          - "  docker compose -f {{ agent_compose_file }} restart"

---
# =============================================================================
# Configure Pulse Docker Agent in LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
# It deploys the Pulse Docker agent for container monitoring.
# =============================================================================

- name: Configure Pulse agent for ${container_name}
  hosts: ${container_name}
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    container_id: ${container_id}
    container_name: ${container_name}
    pulse_url: ${pulse_url}
    pulse_token: ${pulse_token}

    agent_compose_dir: /config/sidecars
    agent_compose_file: /config/sidecars/pulse-agent.yml

  tasks:
    # =========================================================================
    # Create Sidecar Directory
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create sidecars directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ agent_compose_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Pulse Agent Docker Compose
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Deploy Pulse agent docker-compose
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          services:
            pulse-agent:
              image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
              container_name: pulse-agent
              pid: host
              uts: host
              environment:
                - PULSE_URL={{ pulse_url }}
                - PULSE_TOKEN={{ pulse_token }}
              volumes:
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.25'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 64m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
              healthcheck:
                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep pulse-docker-agent || exit 1"]
                interval: 30s
                timeout: 10s
                retries: 3
                start_period: 30s
        dest: "{{ agent_compose_file }}"
        mode: '0644'
      register: compose_file

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Agent Container
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Pull Pulse agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
      changed_when: true

    - name: Deploy Pulse agent container
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker compose -f {{ agent_compose_file }} up -d --remove-orphans
      register: deploy_result
      changed_when: "'Started' in deploy_result.stderr or 'Creating' in deploy_result.stderr"

    # =========================================================================
    # Verify Deployment
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Wait for agent to start
      ansible.builtin.pause:
        seconds: 5

    - name: Check agent container status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=pulse-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: agent_status
      changed_when: false

    - name: Display deployment summary
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== Pulse Agent Deployed for ${container_name} ==="
          - ""
          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
          - "Pulse URL: {{ pulse_url }}"
          - "Agent Status: {{ agent_status.stdout }}"
          - ""
          - "View logs:"
          - "  docker logs -f pulse-agent"
          - ""
          - "Restart agent:"
          - "  docker compose -f {{ agent_compose_file }} restart"

# Pulse Environment Variables and Docker Connectivity

## Environment Variables

Pulse uses two environment variables:

1. **PULSE_IMAGE**: Specifies the Docker image to use (defaults to `rcoaltman/pulse:latest`)
2. **PULSE_PORT**: Sets the service port (defaults to `7655`)
3. **TZ**: Configures the timezone (defaults to `UTC`)

## Docker Connectivity

The configuration shows **no direct Docker socket access**. Instead, Pulse relies on an agent-based approach for monitoring.

## Agent Support

The documentation explicitly mentions two temperature monitoring options:

- **Pulse Agent (Recommended)**: Install `pulse-agent` on each Proxmox host with `--enable-proxmox` flag
- **Pulse Sensor Proxy (Deprecated)**: An older host-side proxy method available via socket mounting at `/run/pulse-sensor-proxy:ro`

The configuration notes that the sensor proxy approach is deprecated, favoring the modern agent installation method for distributed Proxmox host monitoring.

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Docker Socket Proxy - Secure Docker API access
  # ==========================================================================
  # Provides a filtered API proxy to Docker socket for security
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest
    container_name: docker-socket-proxy
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    environment:
      # Container management
      - CONTAINERS=1
      - EXEC=1
      - IMAGES=1
      - NETWORKS=1
      - VOLUMES=1
      - POST=1
      # Status/info
      - EVENTS=1
      - PING=1
      - VERSION=1
      - INFO=1
      # Security: disable sensitive endpoints
      - AUTH=0
      - SECRETS=0
    networks:
      - internal
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.1'
        reservations:
          memory: 32m
          cpus: '0.05'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:2375/version || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Pulse - Proxmox and Docker Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================
  # Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
  # Lightweight alternative to full observability stacks.
  pulse:
    image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:latest
    container_name: pulse
    ports:
      - "7655:7655"
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
    networks:
      - internal
      - default
    depends_on:
      - docker-socket-proxy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7655/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Arcane - Docker Container Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # Modern Docker management UI with update detection.
  # Manages containers via remote agents on other LXCs.
  arcane:
    image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest
    container_name: arcane
    ports:
      - "3552:3552"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - APP_URL=https://arcane.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375

      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

## Pulse Docker Agent

Pulse is a responsive monitoring platform for Proxmox VE, PBS, and Docker with real-time metrics across nodes and containers.

### What It Does

Agents collect Docker container stats, host metrics, and temperatures locally. It uses a push-based model where agents initiate connections to Pulse, not vice versa.(no content)Docker/Host agents push metrics to Pulse at their configured interval (default: 30s).

### Running the Docker Agent

To run the agent as a container:
```
docker run -d \
  --name pulse-agent \
  --pid=host --uts=host \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -e PULSE_URL="http://pulse:7655" \
  -e PULSE_TOKEN="<token>" \
  ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
```

### Deployment Options

A Helm chart is available that deploys the Pulse hub (web UI + API) and, optionally, the Docker monitoring agent.(no content)The Docker agent can be deployed as a DaemonSet or Deployment, and requires access to the Docker socket by default.

### Troubleshooting

If a host was previously removed, you must "Allow re-enroll" in Settings → Docker → Removed Hosts.(no content)For permission denied errors on the socket, ensure the pulse-docker user is in the docker group (`sudo usermod -aG docker pulse-docker`).(no content)If agents flip-flop in the UI showing duplicate hosts, they share a machine-id.

### Recent Updates

Pulse 5.0 introduces an optional AI assistant that brings intelligent monitoring to your infrastructure, including natural language queries and automated health checks with the Patrol Service.

content.content:
# Pulse Unified Agent: Docker Monitoring Setup

## How It Works

The unified agent combines host, Docker, and Kubernetes monitoring in a single binary. For Docker specifically, it "automatically detects available platforms on the target machine" and enables Docker monitoring if `docker info` or `podman info` succeeds.

## Required Environment Variables

Two critical variables are needed:

- **PULSE_URL**: The Pulse server address (e.g., `http://localhost:7655`)
- **PULSE_TOKEN**: Your API authentication token

These can be set as command-line flags (`--url`, `--token`) or environment variables during installation.

## Generating Agent Tokens

The documentation doesn't explain token generation. You must generate tokens through the Pulse UI: **Settings > Agents > "Install New Agent"**, which provides a pre-configured installation command with your unique token.

## Deployment Process

The basic installation command is:
```bash
curl -fsSL http://<pulse-ip>:7655/install.sh | \
  bash -s -- --url http://<pulse-ip>:7655 --token <token>
```

For Docker-only monitoring on remote hosts:
```bash
curl -fsSL http://<pulse-ip>:7655/install.sh | \
  bash -s -- --url http://<pulse-ip>:7655 --token <token> \
  --disable-host --enable-docker
```

The installer automatically removes legacy agents and sets up systemd services on Linux or launchd on macOS.

content.text:
Good question. Let me think through the trade-offs:

**Option 1: Per-LXC items** (e.g., `pulse-agent-n8n`, `arcane-agent-n8n`)
- Pros: Granular control, easy to revoke per-host, matches security best practices
- Cons: Many 1Password items (12+ LXCs × 2 agents = 24+ items), more tofu data sources

**Option 2: Centralized items** (e.g., `pulse-agents`, `arcane-agents` with sections per LXC)
- Pros: Fewer items, organized in one place, easier to manage
- Cons: Revoking one host means updating the shared item

**Option 3: Single shared token per service** (one Pulse token, one Arcane token for all)
- Pros: Simplest setup, minimal 1Password items
- Cons: If compromised, all agents affected; can't revoke per-host

Given your mention of adding node-exporter and logging agents in the future, I'd recommend:

**Centralized per-service with sections** - One 1Password item per agent type with a section for each LXC:

```
pulse-agents:
  sections:
    n8n: {token: "xxx"}
    immich: {token: "yyy"}
    jellyfin: {token: "zzz"}

arcane-agents:
  sections:
    n8n: {bootstrap_token: "xxx"}
    immich: {bootstrap_token: "yyy"}
```

This scales well when you add more agent types (node-exporter, promtail, etc.) - you'd have:
- `pulse-agents` 
- `arcane-agents`
- `node-exporter-agents` (future)
- `promtail-agents` (future)

Each with per-LXC sections. Want me to proceed with this structure?
