# =============================================================================
# 1Password Provider Configuration
# =============================================================================
# This file provides direct 1Password integration for secret management.
# Secrets are fetched at plan/apply time using the 1Password CLI.
#
# Authentication: Uses 1Password CLI with biometric unlock
# Ensure `op` CLI v2.23.0+ is installed and signed in
#
# Usage: Symlink this file to any app that needs 1Password secrets
#   ln -s ../../../onepassword.tf tofu/apps/<app>/onepassword.tf
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password Vault Reference
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_vault" "homelab" {
  name = "homelab"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core Infrastructure Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenTofu state encryption and Proxmox credentials
data "onepassword_item" "opentofu" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "opentofu"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cloudflare Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "cloudflare" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "Cloudflare"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "grafana" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "grafana"
}

data "onepassword_item" "discord_webhook" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "discord-alertmanager-webhook"
}

data "onepassword_item" "uptime_kuma" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "uptime-kuma"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Container Management Secrets (Pulse + Arcane)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "pulse" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "pulse"
}

data "onepassword_item" "arcane" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "arcane"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Portainer Edge Agent Credentials
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each Edge environment in Portainer has unique credentials stored in 1Password.
# Item format: "portainer-edge-<app-name>" with fields:
#   - edge_id: UUID for the Edge environment
#   - edge_key: Base64-encoded connection key
#
# Create items in 1Password:
#   op item create --category=login --title="portainer-edge-dashboards" \
#     --vault=homelab edge_id=<uuid> edge_key=<base64-key>

data "onepassword_item" "portainer_edge" {
  for_each = toset([
    "dashboards",
    "authelia",
    "monitoring",
    "obsidian-sync",
    "jellyfin",
    "immich",
    "n8n",
    "openwebui",
    "traefik",
    "network-services",
    "media-management",
    "documents",
  ])

  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "portainer-edge-${each.key}"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper Locals - Flatten 1Password fields for easy access
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 1Password provider returns fields in a nested structure.
# Custom fields are inside section blocks.

locals {
  # Flatten all section fields from opentofu item into a map by label
  _opentofu_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.opentofu.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Flatten all section fields from cloudflare item into a map by label
  _cloudflare_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Flatten all section fields from arcane item into a map by label
  _arcane_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.arcane.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # 1Password secrets - access via local.op.<secret_name>
  op = {
    # State encryption passphrase (main password field)
    state_encryption_passphrase = data.onepassword_item.opentofu.password

    # Proxmox API token (custom field in section)
    proxmox_api_token = lookup(local._opentofu_section_fields, "proxmox_api_token", "")

    # Cloudflare (custom fields in sections + standard fields)
    cloudflare_email        = data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.username
    cloudflare_tunnel_token = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "tunnel_token", "")
    cloudflare_api_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "ddns_api_token", lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", ""))
    cloudflare_dns_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", "")

    # Monitoring
    grafana_admin_password  = data.onepassword_item.grafana.password
    discord_webhook_url     = data.onepassword_item.discord_webhook.credential
    uptime_kuma_username    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.username
    uptime_kuma_password    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.password

    # Container Management (Pulse + Arcane)
    pulse_admin_user     = data.onepassword_item.pulse.username
    pulse_admin_password = data.onepassword_item.pulse.password
    arcane_encryption_key = lookup(local._arcane_section_fields, "encryption_key", "")
    arcane_jwt_secret     = lookup(local._arcane_section_fields, "jwt_secret", "")
  }

  # Portainer Edge credentials - access via local.portainer_edge["app-name"]
  # Each entry has .edge_id and .edge_key
  portainer_edge = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => {
      edge_id  = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_id", "")
      edge_key = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_key", "")
    }
  }

  # Helper to flatten Portainer Edge item fields
  _portainer_edge_fields = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => merge(
      # Include top-level fields (username/password/etc)
      {
        "edge_id"  = try(item.username, "")
        "edge_key" = try(item.password, "")
      },
      # Include section fields
      merge([
        for s in try(item.section, []) : {
          for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
        }
      ]...)
    )
  }
}

# Core Infrastructure Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# OpenTofu state encryption and Proxmox credentials
data "onepassword_item" "opentofu" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "opentofu"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cloudflare Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "cloudflare" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "Cloudflare"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monitoring Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "grafana" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "grafana"
}

data "onepassword_item" "discord_webhook" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "discord-alertmanager-webhook"
}

data "onepassword_item" "uptime_kuma" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "uptime-kuma"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Container Management Secrets (Pulse + Arcane)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "pulse" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "pulse"
}

data "onepassword_item" "arcane" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "arcane"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Agent Tokens (per-LXC tokens stored in centralized items)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structure: One item per agent type with sections for each LXC
#   pulse-agents:
#     n8n.token, immich.token, jellyfin.token, ...
#   arcane-agents:
#     n8n.bootstrap_token, immich.bootstrap_token, ...

data "onepassword_item" "pulse_agents" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "pulse-agents"
}

data "onepassword_item" "arcane_agents" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "arcane-agents"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Portainer Edge Agent Credentials
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Each Edge environment in Portainer has unique credentials stored in 1Password.
# Item format: "portainer-edge-<app-name>" with fields:
#   - edge_id: UUID for the Edge environment
#   - edge_key: Base64-encoded connection key
#
# Create items in 1Password:
#   op item create --category=login --title="portainer-edge-dashboards" \
#     --vault=homelab edge_id=<uuid> edge_key=<base64-key>

data "onepassword_item" "portainer_edge" {
  for_each = toset([
    "dashboards",
    "authelia",
    "monitoring",
    "obsidian-sync",
    "jellyfin",
    "immich",
    "n8n",
    "openwebui",
    "traefik",
    "network-services",
    "media-management",
    "documents",
  ])

  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "portainer-edge-${each.key}"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helper Locals - Flatten 1Password fields for easy access
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The 1Password provider returns fields in a nested structure.
# Custom fields are inside section blocks.

locals {
  # Flatten all section fields from opentofu item into a map by label
  _opentofu_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.opentofu.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Flatten all section fields from cloudflare item into a map by label
  _cloudflare_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Flatten all section fields from arcane item into a map by label
  _arcane_section_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.arcane.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # 1Password secrets - access via local.op.<secret_name>
  op = {
    # State encryption passphrase (main password field)
    state_encryption_passphrase = data.onepassword_item.opentofu.password

    # Proxmox API token (custom field in section)
    proxmox_api_token = lookup(local._opentofu_section_fields, "proxmox_api_token", "")

    # Cloudflare (custom fields in sections + standard fields)
    cloudflare_email        = data.onepassword_item.cloudflare.username
    cloudflare_tunnel_token = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "tunnel_token", "")
    cloudflare_api_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "ddns_api_token", lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", ""))
    cloudflare_dns_token    = lookup(local._cloudflare_section_fields, "Api token - traefik", "")

    # Monitoring
    grafana_admin_password  = data.onepassword_item.grafana.password
    discord_webhook_url     = data.onepassword_item.discord_webhook.credential
    uptime_kuma_username    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.username
    uptime_kuma_password    = data.onepassword_item.uptime_kuma.password

    # Container Management (Pulse + Arcane)
    pulse_admin_user     = data.onepassword_item.pulse.username
    pulse_admin_password = data.onepassword_item.pulse.password
    arcane_encryption_key = lookup(local._arcane_section_fields, "encryption_key", "")
    arcane_jwt_secret     = lookup(local._arcane_section_fields, "jwt_secret", "")
  }

  # Portainer Edge credentials - access via local.portainer_edge["app-name"]
  # Each entry has .edge_id and .edge_key
  portainer_edge = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => {
      edge_id  = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_id", "")
      edge_key = lookup(local._portainer_edge_fields[name], "edge_key", "")
    }
  }

  # Helper to flatten Portainer Edge item fields
  _portainer_edge_fields = {
    for name, item in data.onepassword_item.portainer_edge : name => merge(
      # Include top-level fields (username/password/etc)
      {
        "edge_id"  = try(item.username, "")
        "edge_key" = try(item.password, "")
      },
      # Include section fields
      merge([
        for s in try(item.section, []) : {
          for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
        }
      ]...)
    )
  }
}

# =============================================================================
# n8n LXC - Workflow Automation
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 502
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Plus traefik-route module for self-service routing.
# =============================================================================

module "n8n" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  # Identity
  name         = "n8n"
  container_id = 502

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.n8n}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores          = 2
  memory         = 2048
  swap           = 1024
  rootfs_size    = 8
  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir = "${path.module}/deploy"

  # SSH
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Container options - unprivileged for security
  unprivileged = true
  template     = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox notes
  service_description = "Workflow automation platform"
  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://n8n.${var.domain_internal}/"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.n8n}:5678/"
  }
  services = [
    { name = "n8n", port = 5678, info = "Web UI and API" }
  ]
  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Docker Deployment

**Compose file:** `/config/docker-compose.yml`
**Data volume:** `n8n_data`

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f n8n
```

**Restart n8n:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart n8n
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=n8n` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["n8n", "automation"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.n8n.container_id
  container_ip   = module.n8n.ip_address
  container_name = "n8n"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-502"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "SQLite backup"
      command = "cp /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite /var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data/database.sqlite.backup"
      timeout = 60
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes/config_n8n_data/_data"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,n8n"
  }

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "n8n_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "n8n"
  backend_url = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "n8n.${var.domain_internal}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.n8n]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.n8n.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.n8n.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.n8n.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.n8n_route.internal_url
    direct   = "http://${module.n8n.ip_address}:5678/"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.n8n_route.remote_config_path
}

---
# =============================================================================
# Configure Arcane Remote Agent in LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
# It deploys the Arcane headless agent for remote container management.
# =============================================================================

- name: Configure Arcane agent for ${container_name}
  hosts: ${container_name}
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    container_id: ${container_id}
    container_name: ${container_name}
    manager_url: ${manager_url}
    bootstrap_token: ${bootstrap_token}

    agent_compose_dir: /config/sidecars
    agent_compose_file: /config/sidecars/arcane-agent.yml

  tasks:
    # =========================================================================
    # Create Sidecar Directory
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create sidecars directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ agent_compose_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Arcane Agent Docker Compose
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Deploy Arcane agent docker-compose
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          services:
            arcane-agent:
              image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest
              container_name: arcane-agent
              ports:
                - "3553:3553"
              environment:
                - AGENT_MODE=true
                - AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN={{ bootstrap_token }}
              volumes:
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
                - arcane_agent_data:/app/data
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 256m
                    cpus: '0.5'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
              healthcheck:
                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3553/ || exit 1"]
                interval: 30s
                timeout: 10s
                retries: 3
                start_period: 30s

          volumes:
            arcane_agent_data:
        dest: "{{ agent_compose_file }}"
        mode: '0644'
      register: compose_file

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Agent Container
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Pull Arcane agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest
      changed_when: true

    - name: Deploy Arcane agent container
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker compose -f {{ agent_compose_file }} up -d --remove-orphans
      register: deploy_result
      changed_when: "'Started' in deploy_result.stderr or 'Creating' in deploy_result.stderr"

    # =========================================================================
    # Verify Deployment
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Wait for agent to start
      ansible.builtin.pause:
        seconds: 10

    - name: Check agent container status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=arcane-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: agent_status
      changed_when: false

    - name: Display deployment summary
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== Arcane Agent Deployed for ${container_name} ==="
          - ""
          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
          - "Agent Port: 3553"
          - "Agent Status: {{ agent_status.stdout }}"
          - ""
          - "To pair with Arcane manager:"
          - "  1. Go to Arcane UI -> Environments"
          - "  2. Add new environment: http://{{ ansible_host }}:3553"
          - "  3. Use bootstrap token for initial pairing"
          - ""
          - "View logs:"
          - "  docker logs -f arcane-agent"
          - ""
          - "Restart agent:"
          - "  docker compose -f {{ agent_compose_file }} restart"

Based on my search, here's what I found about Arcane headless agent environment variables for Docker remote setup:

## Arcane Headless Agent Configuration

Remote Environments let Arcane manage containers on other hosts through a stripped down version of Arcane itself. You run the Agent on a remote machine (with access to its Docker daemon), pair it to your Arcane manager using a one-time Bootstrap Token, and both sides store an Agent Token for all future requests.

### Docker Compose Configuration for the Agent

The agent uses the `ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest` image with these key environment variables:

**AGENT_MODE** (required): Set to `true` to run in Agent mode. **AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN** (pairing only): One-time secret used to mint the Agent Token.

### Example Docker Compose for the Agent

The agent compose configuration uses port 3553:3553, with environment variables `AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` and volume mounts for `/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock` and `agent-data:/app/data`.

### Additional Environment Variables

Optional environment variables include `AGENT_TOKEN` (generated-token) and `AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` (bootstrap-secret) for when the manager also acts as an agent.(no content)Note: The `GIN_MODE=release` environment variable is needed in this case due to it not being set via the dockerfile, unless you don't care if gin runs in development mode.

### Troubleshooting

- **401/403 during pairing**: Bootstrap token mismatch; ensure AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN equals the value provided in Arcane.
- **Connection errors**: Ensure port 3553 is reachable from the Manager to the Agent host.
- **Docker access issues**: Verify /var/run/docker.sock is mounted and the container user has permissions.

### Agent Pairing Process

The environment service implements agent pairing through a bootstrap token exchange mechanism. Remote agents expose their own Arcane API, and the manager pairs by calling `POST /api/environments/0/agent/pair` with the bootstrap token in the `X-Arcane-Agent-Bootstrap` header. The agent responds with a permanent access token that is stored in the environments table.

Based on the documentation, the agent configuration looks correct. The issue is that the **manager needs to initiate pairing to the agent**, not the other way around. The agent exposes port 3553 and waits for the manager to connect to it.

The workflow is:
1. Agent runs with `AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN` set
2. In Arcane UI, you add a new environment pointing to `http://<agent-ip>:3553`
3. Arcane manager calls the agent's pairing endpoint with the bootstrap token
4. Agent returns a permanent token that Arcane stores

So the agent is waiting correctly - you need to add it in the Arcane UI:

1. Go to https://arcane.homelab.rambtech.dev
2. Navigate to **Environments** or **Settings → Environments**
3. Add new environment with URL: `http://10.100.5.102:3553`
4. Enter the bootstrap token you put in 1Password

The agent should then pair and appear in the dashboard.

Sources:
- [Remote Environments](https://arcane.ofkm.dev/docs/features/environments)
- [Environment Service | DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/getarcaneapp/arcane/7.3-environment-service)

# =============================================================================
# OpenWebUI LXC - AI Chat Interface with Ollama
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 501
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Features AMD GPU passthrough for Ollama LLM acceleration.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with Ollama backend (AMD GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.openwebui}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "Ollama", port = 11434, info = "LLM backend (ROCM GPU)" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M passed through for Ollama LLM acceleration:
- `/dev/kfd`, `/dev/dri` devices
- ROCM backend

**Check GPU:**
```
docker exec ollama rocminfo
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f openwebui
cd /config && docker compose logs -f ollama
```

**List models:**
```
docker exec ollama ollama list
```

**Pull new model:**
```
docker exec ollama ollama pull llama3.2
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "ollama", "llm"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.openwebui.container_id
  container_ip   = module.openwebui.ip_address
  container_name = "openwebui"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-501"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database dump needed - SQLite file backup is sufficient

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2", "/root/.ollama/**"]  # Exclude 32GB of Ollama models

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,openwebui"
  }

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal and public routes (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "ai.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.openwebui_route.internal_url
    public   = module.openwebui_route.public_url
    direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.openwebui_route.remote_config_path
}

# =============================================================================
# OpenWebUI LXC - AI Chat Interface with Ollama
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 501
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Features AMD GPU passthrough for Ollama LLM acceleration.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with Ollama backend (AMD GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.openwebui}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "Ollama", port = 11434, info = "LLM backend (ROCM GPU)" },
    { name = "Portainer Agent", port = 9001, info = "Container management agent" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M passed through for Ollama LLM acceleration:
- `/dev/kfd`, `/dev/dri` devices
- ROCM backend

**Check GPU:**
```
docker exec ollama rocminfo
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f openwebui
cd /config && docker compose logs -f ollama
```

**List models:**
```
docker exec ollama ollama list
```

**Pull new model:**
```
docker exec ollama ollama pull llama3.2
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "ollama", "llm"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.openwebui.container_id
  container_ip   = module.openwebui.ip_address
  container_name = "openwebui"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-501"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database dump needed - SQLite file backup is sufficient

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2", "/root/.ollama/**"]  # Exclude 32GB of Ollama models

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,openwebui"
  }

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal and public routes (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "ai.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.openwebui_route.internal_url
    public   = module.openwebui_route.public_url
    direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.openwebui_route.remote_config_path
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate combined .env file with Jellystat + Edge credentials
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# NOTE: We generate a combined .env file here instead of using the docker-lxc
# module's portainer_edge_id/key because Jellyfin needs additional env vars
# for Jellystat (DB password, JWT secret). The module would overwrite these.

resource "local_sensitive_file" "jellyfin_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
# Jellyfin Stack Environment Variables
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# Jellystat PostgreSQL credentials
JELLYSTAT_DB_PASSWORD=st4dnS0X75gJTlATNXYBWQawJ4OzYQ
JELLYSTAT_JWT_SECRET=69z87jUXLPJxIkao3EGXW8QF51ZTM5uSSucwJaw6I

# Portainer Edge Agent credentials (from 1Password: portainer-edge-jellyfin)
PORTAINER_EDGE_ID=${local.portainer_edge["jellyfin"].edge_id}
PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY=${local.portainer_edge["jellyfin"].edge_key}
EOT

  file_permission = "0600"
}

module "jellyfin" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "jellyfin"
  container_id = 401
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for DLNA/casting)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.media.jellyfin}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.jellyfin}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  cores  = 4
  memory = 8192
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = 32

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Enable AMD GPU passthrough for hardware transcoding
  enable_gpu = true

  # NOTE: We don't set portainer_edge_id/key here because this app generates
  # its own .env file that includes both Jellystat and Edge credentials.
  # Setting them here would cause the docker-lxc module to create a separate
  # .env that would overwrite our combined one.

  # Mount point for media library
  # This is configured via SSH (null_resource.configure_mount_points) since
  # the API token doesn't have permission for bind mounts (requires root@pam)
  mount_points = [
    {
      slot   = 0
      path   = "/data/library"
      volume = "/tank/data/library"
    }
  ]

  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

## Quick Commands

**Restart:** cd /config && docker compose restart jellyfin
EOT

}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Homepage API Keys
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "homepage" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "homepage"
}

locals {
  # Flatten all section fields from homepage item
  _homepage_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.homepage.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  # Homepage widget API keys
  homepage_env = {
    portainer_key  = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "portainer_key", "")
    adguard_user   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "adguard_user", "admin")
    adguard_pass   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "adguard_pass", "")
    immich_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "immich_key", "")
    jellyfin_key   = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "jellyfin_key", "")
    jellyseerr_key = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "jellyseerr_key", "")
    sonarr_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "sonarr_key", "")
    radarr_key     = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "radarr_key", "")
    sabnzbd_key    = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "sabnzbd_key", "")
    qbit_user      = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "qbit_user", "admin")
    qbit_pass      = lookup(local._homepage_fields, "qbit_pass", "")
  }
}

# Generate the homepage.env file from 1Password secrets
resource "local_sensitive_file" "homepage_env" {

# Homepage Widget API Keys
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password

HOMEPAGE_VAR_ADGUARD_USER=${local.homepage_env.adguard_user}

# Immich: Account Settings > API Keys
HOMEPAGE_VAR_IMMICH_KEY=${local.homepage_env.immich_key}

# Jellyfin: Dashboard > API Keys

# =============================================================================
# Traefik LXC - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 200
#
# This deployment uses the docker-lxc module which handles:
#   1. LXC container creation with Docker pre-installed
#   2. File sync via rsync (file-sync module)
#   3. Docker Compose deployment
#   4. Proxmox notes generation
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# App-specific Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  description = "Container ID for Traefik LXC"
  type        = number
  default     = 200
}

variable "cores" {
  description = "CPU cores"
  type        = number
  default     = 2
}

variable "memory" {
  description = "Memory in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 2048
}

variable "swap" {
  description = "Swap in MB"
  type        = number
  default     = 1024
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  description = "Root filesystem size in GB"
  type        = number
  default     = 8
}

variable "rootfs_storage" {
  description = "Storage pool for root filesystem"
  type        = string
  default     = "nvme-containers"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "traefik" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "traefik"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (dual-NIC: container network + LAN for external access)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.dashboards.traefik}${local.network.container_netmask}"
  lan_ip       = "${local.lan_ips.traefik}${local.network.lan_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = var.rootfs_storage
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # MUST be privileged for binding to ports 80/443
  unprivileged = false

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Exclude migrated routes (managed by traefik-route module) and env templates (env is generated)
  exclude_patterns = ["^migrated-dynamic/", "^\\.env"]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Traefik"
  service_description = "Reverse proxy and ingress controller for all homelab services"

  service_urls = {
    dashboard_internal = "https://traefik.${var.domain_internal}/dashboard/"
    direct             = "http://${local.traefik_ip}:8080/dashboard/"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "HTTP", port = 80, info = "HTTP entrypoint (redirects to HTTPS)" },
    { name = "HTTPS", port = 443, info = "HTTPS entrypoint with Let's Encrypt" },
    { name = "Metrics", port = 8082, info = "Prometheus metrics endpoint" },
    { name = "Portainer Edge Agent", port = 0, info = "Outbound tunnel to Portainer" }
  ]

  custom_notes = file("${path.module}/notes.md")

  tags = ["traefik", "ingress", "reverse-proxy"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Create .env file with secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Generate .env file locally with secrets from 1Password, then sync to container

resource "local_sensitive_file" "traefik_env" {
  content = templatefile("${path.module}/deploy/.env.tpl", {
    cf_api_token       = local.op.cloudflare_api_token
    cf_api_email       = local.op.cloudflare_email
    portainer_edge_id  = local.portainer_edge["traefik"].edge_id
    portainer_edge_key = local.portainer_edge["traefik"].edge_key
  })

}

  container_ip   = module.traefik.ip_address

  value = module.traefik.ssh_command
}

    - name: Manage Tailscale service on network-services

      gather_facts: no

        app_name: network-services

        # Tailscale Service Management
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Ensure Tailscale daemon is running
          ansible.builtin.systemd:
            name: tailscaled
            state: started
            enabled: true
          register: tailscale_service

        - name: Wait for Tailscale to initialize
          ansible.builtin.pause:
            seconds: 3
          when: tailscale_service.changed

        # =====================================================================
        # Verify Tailscale Status
        # =====================================================================
        - name: Check Tailscale connection status
          ansible.builtin.command:
            cmd: tailscale status --json
          register: tailscale_status
          changed_when: false
          failed_when: false

        - name: Parse Tailscale status
          ansible.builtin.set_fact:
            tailscale_info: "{{ tailscale_status.stdout | from_json }}"
          when: tailscale_status.rc == 0

        - name: Display Tailscale connection info

              Hostname: {{ tailscale_info.Self.HostName | default('N/A') }}
          when: tailscale_status.rc == 0

        - name: Warn if Tailscale not connected
          ansible.builtin.debug:
            msg: "WARNING: Tailscale is not connected. Check authentication status with 'tailscale status'"
          when: tailscale_status.rc != 0 or (tailscale_info.BackendState | default('')) != 'Running'

# =============================================================================
# Configure Pulse Docker Agent in LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
# It deploys the Pulse Docker agent for container monitoring.
# =============================================================================

- name: Configure Pulse agent for ${container_name}
  hosts: ${container_name}
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    container_id: ${container_id}
    container_name: ${container_name}
    pulse_url: ${pulse_url}
    pulse_token: ${pulse_token}

    agent_compose_dir: /config/sidecars
    agent_compose_file: /config/sidecars/pulse-agent.yml

  tasks:
    # =========================================================================
    # Create Sidecar Directory
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create sidecars directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ agent_compose_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Pulse Agent Docker Compose
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Deploy Pulse agent docker-compose
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          services:
            pulse-agent:
              image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
              container_name: pulse-agent
              pid: host
              uts: host
              environment:
                - PULSE_URL={{ pulse_url }}
                - PULSE_TOKEN={{ pulse_token }}
              volumes:
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.25'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 64m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
              healthcheck:
                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep pulse-docker-agent || exit 1"]
                interval: 30s
                timeout: 10s
                retries: 3
                start_period: 30s
        dest: "{{ agent_compose_file }}"
        mode: '0644'
      register: compose_file

    # =========================================================================

    # =========================================================================
    - name: Pull Pulse agent image

## Pulse Docker Agent (ghcr.io/rcourtman)

Pulse is a modern, unified dashboard for monitoring your infrastructure across Proxmox, Docker, and Kubernetes. It consolidates metrics, alerts, and AI-powered insights from all your systems into a single, beautiful interface.

### Docker Agent Image

The Pulse Docker agent is available on GitHub Container Registry at:
- **`ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest`**

### Running the Docker Agent

To run the agent as a container:
```bash
docker run -d \
  --name pulse-agent \
  --pid=host --uts=host \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -e PULSE_URL="http://pulse:7655" \
  -e PULSE_TOKEN="<token>" \
  ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
```

### Unified Agent Updates (2025)

As of version v4.36.1, there's a unified agent for host and Docker monitoring.(no content)Recent releases include fixes for unified agent installation, deploying install.sh, install.ps1, and pulse-agent binaries during installation.

### Known Issues

With the new unified agent, some users reported being unable to add a "docker only" agent like before. Even when adding the parameter `--disable-host` to the command line, users only get host monitoring (and no docker monitoring at all).

### Main Pulse Server Image

The main Pulse server is available on Docker Hub: `rcourtman/pulse:latest` and can be run with:
```bash
docker run -d \
  --name pulse \
  -p 7655:7655 \
  -v pulse_data:/data \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  rcourtman/pulse:latest
```

---
# =============================================================================
# Configure Container Management Agents in LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
# It deploys all enabled agents in a single docker-compose file to avoid
# conflicts from separate compose projects removing each other's containers.
#
# Agents:
#   - Pulse Docker Agent: Container monitoring (pushes metrics to Pulse server)
#   - Arcane Agent: Remote container management (manager initiates pairing)
# =============================================================================

- name: Configure container agents for ${container_name}
  hosts: ${container_name}
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    container_id: "${container_id}"
    container_name: "${container_name}"

    # Pulse agent config
    pulse_enabled: ${pulse_enabled}
    pulse_url: "${pulse_url}"
    pulse_token: "${pulse_token}"

    # Arcane agent config
    arcane_enabled: ${arcane_enabled}
    manager_url: "${manager_url}"
    bootstrap_token: "${bootstrap_token}"

    # Shared paths
    sidecars_dir: /config/sidecars
    compose_file: /config/sidecars/docker-compose.yml

  tasks:
    # =========================================================================
    # Create Sidecar Directory
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create sidecars directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ sidecars_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Unified Docker Compose
    # =========================================================================
    # Single compose file with all enabled agents to prevent --remove-orphans
    # from removing the "other" agent when updating just one.

    - name: Deploy unified agents docker-compose
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          # =============================================================================
          # Container Management Agents - ${container_name}
          # =============================================================================
          # Generated by OpenTofu lxc-sidecars module
          # DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY - changes will be overwritten
          # =============================================================================

          services:
%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            # Pulse Docker Agent - Container Monitoring
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            # NOTE: pulse-docker-agent is deprecated. Pulse v5.0+ introduces a unified
            # agent (binary install). Until v5.0 is stable, continue using this image.
            pulse-agent:
              image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
              container_name: pulse-agent
              pid: host
              uts: host
              environment:
                - PULSE_URL=${pulse_url}
                - PULSE_TOKEN=${pulse_token}
              volumes:
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.25'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 64m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
              healthcheck:
                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep pulse-docker-agent || exit 1"]
                interval: 30s
                timeout: 10s
                retries: 3
                start_period: 30s

%{ endif ~}
%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            # Arcane Agent - Remote Container Management
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            arcane-agent:
              image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest
              container_name: arcane-agent
              ports:
                - "3553:3553"
              environment:
                - AGENT_MODE=true
                - AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=${bootstrap_token}
              volumes:
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
                - arcane_agent_data:/app/data
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 256m
                    cpus: '0.5'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
              healthcheck:
                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3553/api/health || exit 1"]
                interval: 30s
                timeout: 10s
                retries: 3
                start_period: 30s

%{ endif ~}
%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
          volumes:
            arcane_agent_data:
%{ endif ~}
        dest: "{{ compose_file }}"
        mode: '0644'
      register: compose_file_result

    # =========================================================================
    # Pull Latest Images
    # =========================================================================
%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
    - name: Pull Pulse agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
      changed_when: true
%{ endif ~}

%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
    - name: Pull Arcane agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest
      changed_when: true
%{ endif ~}

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Agent Containers
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Deploy agent containers
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} up -d --remove-orphans
      register: deploy_result
      changed_when: "'Started' in deploy_result.stderr or 'Creating' in deploy_result.stderr"

    # =========================================================================
    # Verify Deployment
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Wait for agents to start
      ansible.builtin.pause:
        seconds: 10

%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
    - name: Check Pulse agent status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=pulse-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: pulse_status
      changed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
    - name: Check Arcane agent status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=arcane-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: arcane_status
      changed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

    - name: Display deployment summary
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== Container Agents Deployed for ${container_name} ==="
          - ""
          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
          - "Pulse Agent: {{ pulse_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"
          - "  → Pulse URL: ${pulse_url}"
%{ endif ~}
%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
          - "Arcane Agent: {{ arcane_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"
          - "  → Agent Port: 3553"
          - "  → Pair in Arcane UI: http://{{ ansible_host }}:3553"
%{ endif ~}
          - ""
          - "Compose file: {{ compose_file }}"
          - ""
          - "Commands:"
          - "  View logs:  docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} logs -f"
          - "  Restart:    docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} restart"
          - "  Status:     docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} ps"

## Pulse Sensor Proxy - Allowed Nodes Configuration

**Pulse** is a responsive monitoring platform for Proxmox VE, PBS, and Docker with real-time metrics across nodes and containers, developed by rcourtman.

### Allowed Nodes Configuration

The sensor proxy uses a file-based allowlist system. The configuration involves:
- `CONFIG_FILE="/etc/pulse-sensor-proxy/config.yaml"` 
- `ALLOWED_NODES_FILE="/etc/pulse-sensor-proxy/allowed_nodes.yaml"`
- The minimum allowed nodes file version required is `v4.31.1`
- The system uses `ALLOWLIST_MODE="file"`

### "Source IP Not Allowed" Error Context

This error likely occurs when a node tries to connect to the sensor proxy but isn't listed in the `allowed_nodes.yaml` file. The proxy has been hardened so it "never drops into a permissive mode; localhost-only access is enforced during degraded scenarios."

### Version Requirements

If you see an error like "pulse-sensor-proxy v4.31.0 is too old (< v4.31.1)" with "File-based allowlist is now required," you need to upgrade the proxy binary first.

### Resolution Steps

To resolve allowed nodes issues, "re-run the sensor-proxy installer to switch existing deployments to HTTP mode; the installer now auto-registers allowed nodes and enforces localhost-only fallbacks."

### Security Model

The proxy includes context deadlines so local temperature collectors cannot hang the proxy when a node stops responding. It has hardened security fallback so the proxy never drops into a permissive mode, with localhost-only access enforced during degraded scenarios.

If you're experiencing the "source IP not allowed" error, you likely need to:
1. Ensure your Pulse and sensor-proxy versions are at least v4.31.1
2. Check that the `/etc/pulse-sensor-proxy/allowed_nodes.yaml` file contains the IP addresses of your nodes
3. Re-run the sensor-proxy installer which will auto-register allowed nodes

# Traefik - Reverse Proxy & Ingress Controller
# https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/

name: traefik

services:
  traefik:
    container_name: traefik
    image: traefik:v3.6.5
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"        # HTTP
      - "443:443"      # HTTPS
      - "8082:8082"    # Metrics
    environment:
      - CF_DNS_API_TOKEN=${CF_DNS_API_TOKEN}
      - CF_API_EMAIL=${CF_API_EMAIL}
    volumes:
      # Static config (synced by docker-host module to /config/static/)
      - /config/static/traefik.yml:/etc/traefik/traefik.yml:ro
      # Dynamic configs (synced by docker-host module to /config/dynamic/)
      - /config/dynamic:/config/dynamic:ro
      # Certificates (Docker volume for persistence across restarts)
      - certs:/config/certs
      # Logs (Docker volume)
      - logs:/config/logs
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "traefik", "healthcheck", "--ping"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-traefik
  portainer-edge-agent:
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    image: portainer/agent:2.33.6
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  certs:
  logs:
  portainer_agent_data:

# Media Management Stack
# VPN-protected download clients + library managers
# Following TRaSH Guides best practices

name: media-management

networks:
  media-net:
    driver: bridge

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Gluetun - VPN Gateway (NordVPN WireGuard)
  # ==========================================================================
  gluetun:
    image: qmcgaw/gluetun:v3.40.3
    container_name: gluetun
    cap_add:
      - NET_ADMIN
    devices:
      - /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun
    networks:
      - media-net
    environment:
      - VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER=nordvpn
      - VPN_TYPE=wireguard
      - WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY=${NORDVPN_WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY}
      - SERVER_COUNTRIES=Netherlands
      - TZ=America/New_York
      # Allow access to container network for inter-service communication
      - FIREWALL_OUTBOUND_SUBNETS=192.168.1.0/24
      # Health check settings
      - HEALTH_VPN_DURATION_INITIAL=30s
      - HEALTH_VPN_DURATION_ADDITION=10s
    ports:
      # qBittorrent
      - "8080:8080"
      - "6881:6881"
      - "6881:6881/udp"
      # SABnzbd
      - "8085:8085"
      # Prowlarr
      - "9696:9696"
      # FlareSolverr
      - "8191:8191"
    volumes:
      - gluetun-data:/gluetun
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- ifconfig.me || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # qBittorrent - BitTorrent Client (via VPN)
  # ==========================================================================
  qbittorrent:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/qbittorrent:5.1.4
    container_name: qbittorrent
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - WEBUI_PORT=8080
    volumes:
      - qbittorrent-config:/config
      - /data/torrents:/data/torrents
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prowlarr - Indexer Manager (via VPN)
  # ==========================================================================
  prowlarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/prowlarr:2.3.0
    container_name: prowlarr
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - prowlarr-config:/config
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9696/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # FlareSolverr - Cloudflare Bypass (via VPN, optional)
  # ==========================================================================
  flaresolverr:
    image: ghcr.io/flaresolverr/flaresolverr:v3.4.6
    container_name: flaresolverr
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - LOG_LEVEL=info
      - LOG_HTML=false
      - CAPTCHA_SOLVER=none
      - TZ=America/New_York
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8191/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Sonarr - TV Show Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # NOTE: After switching from host network, update Sonarr's download client
  # settings to use container names (e.g., gluetun:8080 for qBittorrent)
  sonarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/sonarr:4.0.16
    container_name: sonarr
    networks:
      - media-net
    ports:
      - "8989:8989"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - sonarr-config:/config
      - /data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8989/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Radarr - Movie Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # NOTE: After switching from host network, update Radarr's download client
  # settings to use container names (e.g., gluetun:8080 for qBittorrent)
  radarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/radarr:6.0.4
    container_name: radarr
    networks:
      - media-net
    ports:
      - "7878:7878"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - radarr-config:/config
      - /data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7878/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Lidarr - Music Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # NOTE: After switching from host network, update Lidarr's download client
  # settings to use container names (e.g., gluetun:8080 for qBittorrent)
  lidarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/lidarr:3.1.0
    container_name: lidarr
    networks:
      - media-net
    ports:
      - "8686:8686"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - lidarr-config:/config
      - /data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8686/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Bazarr - Subtitle Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # NOTE: After switching from host network, update Bazarr's Sonarr/Radarr
  # settings to use container names (e.g., sonarr:8989, radarr:7878)
  bazarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/bazarr:1.5.3
    container_name: bazarr
    networks:
      - media-net
    ports:
      - "6767:6767"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - bazarr-config:/config
      - /data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:6767/ping || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # SABnzbd - Usenet Download Client (via VPN)
  # ==========================================================================
  sabnzbd:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/sabnzbd:4.5.5
    container_name: sabnzbd
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
    volumes:
      - sabnzbd-config:/config
      - /data/usenet:/data/usenet
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8085/api?mode=version || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s
    restart: unless-stopped
    labels:
      - "com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true"

  # ==========================================================================
  # Recyclarr - TRaSH Guides Sync
  # ==========================================================================
  # NOTE: Update recyclarr.yml to use container names for Sonarr/Radarr/Lidarr
  # (e.g., sonarr:8989, radarr:7878, lidarr:8686)
  recyclarr:
    image: ghcr.io/recyclarr/recyclarr:7.5.2
    container_name: recyclarr
    networks:
      - media-net
    user: 1000:1000
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - RECYCLARR_CREATE_CONFIG=true
    volumes:
      - ./recyclarr:/config
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep recyclarr || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # Portainer Edge Agent - Container Management (Outbound Connection)
  # ==========================================================================
  # Edge Agent initiates outbound connection to Portainer (no inbound port exposure)
  # Credentials stored in 1Password: portainer-edge-media-management
  portainer-edge-agent:
    container_name: portainer_edge_agent
    image: portainer/agent:2.33.6
    environment:
      EDGE: 1
      EDGE_ID: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_ID}
      EDGE_KEY: ${PORTAINER_EDGE_KEY}
      EDGE_INSECURE_POLL: 1
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
      - /var/lib/docker/volumes:/var/lib/docker/volumes
      - /:/host
      - portainer_agent_data:/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    # No ports exposed - Edge Agent initiates outbound connection

volumes:
  gluetun-data:
  qbittorrent-config:
  prowlarr-config:
  sonarr-config:
  radarr-config:
  lidarr-config:
  bazarr-config:
  sabnzbd-config:
  portainer_agent_data:
