# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery (PBS - Recommended)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Fix SSH Host Key

The new LXC has a different SSH host key. Update your known_hosts:

```bash
# Get IP from tofu output
IP=$(cd tofu/apps/<APP> && tofu output -raw ip_address)

# Remove old key and add new one
ssh-keygen -R $IP
ssh-keyscan -H $IP >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts
```

#### Step 4: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 5: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state
task tofu:state APP=<APP> > /tmp/new.txt
task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old > /tmp/old.txt
diff /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt  # Should show no differences
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm tofu/apps/<APP>/terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
# 1. Rename state
mv tofu/apps/n8n/terraform.tfstate tofu/apps/n8n/terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Fix SSH (IP: 10.100.5.102)
ssh-keygen -R 10.100.5.102
ssh-keyscan -H 10.100.5.102 >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

# 4. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 5. Verify
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 6. Cleanup
rm tofu/apps/n8n/terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Single Container Recovery (vzdump - Legacy)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses full vzdump container backups (older method).

1. **Identify the failed container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct list"
   ```

2. **Check available backups**

   ```bash
   task backup:list APP=<app-name>
   # Example: task backup:list APP=immich
   ```

3. **Restore to a new container ID** (safer - allows verification)

   ```bash
   task backup:restore BACKUP=<backup-file> TARGET_ID=<new-id>
   # Example: task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-304-2025_12_07-02_00_00.tar.zst TARGET_ID=350
   ```

4. **Verify the restored container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"
   # Check services are running
   ssh root@<container-ip> "docker ps"
   ```

5. **Swap containers** (if verification passes)

   ```bash
   # Stop original
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct stop <original-id>"

   # Update network config on new container to use original IP
   # Then start new container
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"

   # If using OpenTofu, update state:
   task tofu:state:rm APP=<app> RESOURCE="module.<app>.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc"
   ```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<user>/homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2:

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes
   ```

2. Download backups:

   ```bash
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/
   ```

3. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working
- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

ssh-keygen -R 10.100.5.102
ssh-keyscan -H 10.100.5.102 >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

# 4. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 5. Verify
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 6. Cleanup
rm tofu/apps/n8n/terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Single Container Recovery (vzdump - Legacy)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses full vzdump container backups (older method).

1. **Identify the failed container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct list"
   ```

2. **Check available backups**

   ```bash
   task backup:list APP=<app-name>
   # Example: task backup:list APP=immich
   ```

3. **Restore to a new container ID** (safer - allows verification)

   ```bash
   task backup:restore BACKUP=<backup-file> TARGET_ID=<new-id>
   # Example: task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-304-2025_12_07-02_00_00.tar.zst TARGET_ID=350
   ```

4. **Verify the restored container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"
   # Check services are running
   ssh root@<container-ip> "docker ps"
   ```

5. **Swap containers** (if verification passes)

   ```bash
   # Stop original
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct stop <original-id>"

   # Update network config on new container to use original IP
   # Then start new container
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"

   # If using OpenTofu, update state:
   task tofu:state:rm APP=<app> RESOURCE="module.<app>.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc"
   ```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<user>/homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2:

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes
   ```

2. Download backups:

   ```bash
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/
   ```

3. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working
- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery (PBS - Recommended)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state
task tofu:state APP=<APP> > /tmp/new.txt
task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old > /tmp/old.txt
diff /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt  # Should show no differences
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm tofu/apps/<APP>/terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
# 1. Rename state
mv tofu/apps/n8n/terraform.tfstate tofu/apps/n8n/terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Fix SSH (IP: 10.100.5.102)
ssh-keygen -R 10.100.5.102
ssh-keyscan -H 10.100.5.102 >> ~/.ssh/known_hosts

# 4. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 5. Verify
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 6. Cleanup
rm tofu/apps/n8n/terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Single Container Recovery (vzdump - Legacy)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses full vzdump container backups (older method).

1. **Identify the failed container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct list"
   ```

2. **Check available backups**

   ```bash
   task backup:list APP=<app-name>
   # Example: task backup:list APP=immich
   ```

3. **Restore to a new container ID** (safer - allows verification)

   ```bash
   task backup:restore BACKUP=<backup-file> TARGET_ID=<new-id>
   # Example: task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-304-2025_12_07-02_00_00.tar.zst TARGET_ID=350
   ```

4. **Verify the restored container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"
   # Check services are running
   ssh root@<container-ip> "docker ps"
   ```

5. **Swap containers** (if verification passes)

   ```bash
   # Stop original
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct stop <original-id>"

   # Update network config on new container to use original IP
   # Then start new container
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"

   # If using OpenTofu, update state:
   task tofu:state:rm APP=<app> RESOURCE="module.<app>.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc"
   ```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<user>/homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2:

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes
   ```

2. Download backups:

   ```bash
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/
   ```

3. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working
- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery (PBS - Recommended)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state
task tofu:state APP=<APP> > /tmp/new.txt
task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old > /tmp/old.txt
diff /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt  # Should show no differences
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm tofu/apps/<APP>/terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Single Container Recovery (vzdump - Legacy)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses full vzdump container backups (older method).

1. **Identify the failed container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct list"
   ```

2. **Check available backups**

   ```bash
   task backup:list APP=<app-name>
   # Example: task backup:list APP=immich
   ```

3. **Restore to a new container ID** (safer - allows verification)

   ```bash
   task backup:restore BACKUP=<backup-file> TARGET_ID=<new-id>
   # Example: task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-304-2025_12_07-02_00_00.tar.zst TARGET_ID=350
   ```

4. **Verify the restored container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"
   # Check services are running
   ssh root@<container-ip> "docker ps"
   ```

5. **Swap containers** (if verification passes)

   ```bash
   # Stop original
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct stop <original-id>"

   # Update network config on new container to use original IP
   # Then start new container
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"

   # If using OpenTofu, update state:
   task tofu:state:rm APP=<app> RESOURCE="module.<app>.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc"
   ```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<user>/homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2:

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes
   ```

2. Download backups:

   ```bash
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/
   ```

3. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working
- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery (PBS - Recommended)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state
task tofu:state APP=<APP> > /tmp/new.txt
task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old > /tmp/old.txt
diff /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt  # Should show no differences
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm tofu/apps/<APP>/terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Single Container Recovery (vzdump - Legacy)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses full vzdump container backups (older method).

1. **Identify the failed container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct list"
   ```

2. **Check available backups**

   ```bash
   task backup:list APP=<app-name>
   # Example: task backup:list APP=immich
   ```

3. **Restore to a new container ID** (safer - allows verification)

   ```bash
   task backup:restore BACKUP=<backup-file> TARGET_ID=<new-id>
   # Example: task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-304-2025_12_07-02_00_00.tar.zst TARGET_ID=350
   ```

4. **Verify the restored container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"
   # Check services are running
   ssh root@<container-ip> "docker ps"
   ```

5. **Swap containers** (if verification passes)

   ```bash
   # Stop original
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct stop <original-id>"

   # Update network config on new container to use original IP
   # Then start new container
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"

   # If using OpenTofu, update state:
   task tofu:state:rm APP=<app> RESOURCE="module.<app>.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc"
   ```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<user>/homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2:

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes
   ```

2. Download backups:

   ```bash
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/
   ```

3. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working
- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery-pbs---recommended) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery (PBS - Recommended)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state
task tofu:state APP=<APP> > /tmp/new.txt
task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old > /tmp/old.txt
diff /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt  # Should show no differences
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Single Container Recovery (vzdump - Legacy)

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses full vzdump container backups (older method).

1. **Identify the failed container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct list"
   ```

2. **Check available backups**

   ```bash
   task backup:list APP=<app-name>
   # Example: task backup:list APP=immich
   ```

3. **Restore to a new container ID** (safer - allows verification)

   ```bash
   task backup:restore BACKUP=<backup-file> TARGET_ID=<new-id>
   # Example: task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-304-2025_12_07-02_00_00.tar.zst TARGET_ID=350
   ```

4. **Verify the restored container**

   ```bash
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"
   # Check services are running
   ssh root@<container-ip> "docker ps"
   ```

5. **Swap containers** (if verification passes)

   ```bash
   # Stop original
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct stop <original-id>"

   # Update network config on new container to use original IP
   # Then start new container
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start <new-id>"

   # If using OpenTofu, update state:
   task tofu:state:rm APP=<app> RESOURCE="module.<app>.module.lxc.proxmox_virtual_environment_container.lxc"
   ```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<user>/homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2:

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes
   ```

2. Download backups:

   ```bash
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/
   ```

3. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working
- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

## Overview

## Quick Reference

| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery-pbs---recommended) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |

### Single Container Recovery

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old > /tmp/old.txt

```bash
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state
task tofu:state APP=<APP> > /tmp/new.txt
task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old > /tmp/old.txt
diff /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt  # Should show no differences
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/<user>/homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2:

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes
   ```

2. Download backups:

   ```bash
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/
   ```

3. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working
- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>

Here's my SRE review with identified gaps:

## DR Runbook Gaps & Issues

### Critical Gaps

1. **PBS LXC (102) is missing from recovery tiers** - The PBS server itself needs to be recovered before you can restore any app data. It should be Tier 1.

2. **Full Host Recovery still references vzdump** (lines 251-261) - We removed vzdump for single container recovery but Full Host Recovery still uses `pct restore` from vzdump backups. Should this use PBS too? Or is vzdump still needed for full LXC restoration?

3. **No procedure for PBS server failure** - If PBS (LXC 102) fails, how do you recover it? It's a circular dependency - you need PBS to restore PBS.

4. **Database dumps location unclear** - Lines 161, 171, 184 reference `/tank/backups/database-dumps/` but are these dumps created by PBS or a separate process? How often are they created?

5. **1Password/secrets recovery not addressed** - The tofu commands require `TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase` from 1Password. If you lose access to 1Password, you can't decrypt state files or access secrets.

6. **Rclone credentials for B2 recovery** - Line 271 says "Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes" but where are these credentials stored? If they're only in 1Password and you've lost access...

### Medium Gaps

7. **No rollback procedure** - What if a restore makes things worse? No documented rollback.

8. **Missing: Multiple container failure** - What if 3-4 containers fail at once? Serial recovery or parallel?

9. **RPO claims not validated** - "< 24 hrs" RPO, but what's the actual backup frequency? PBS timers are weekly per the plan file.

10. **No pre-flight checks** - Before starting recovery, should verify: disk space, network connectivity, credentials available.

11. **Traefik certificates** - Are Let's Encrypt certs backed up? Will they auto-renew after recovery or will there be downtime?

12. **VPN (gluetun) credentials** - Media Management depends on VPN. Where are those credentials stored/restored from?

### Minor Gaps

13. **GitHub repo URL placeholder** - Line 241 has `<user>` placeholder instead of actual repo URL.

14. **Verification checklist incomplete** - Missing: n8n healthcheck, Jellyfin, Documents, Obsidian Sync verification.

15. **No communication plan** - Who gets notified during DR? Any status page to update?

16. **Immich-importer (303) not mentioned** - Excluded from backups but not mentioned if it auto-recovers or needs manual restart.

---

Would you like me to address any of these gaps in the document?

# Disaster Recovery Runbook

## Overview

This document outlines procedures for recovering the homelab from various failure scenarios. For detailed backup information, see [backups.md](./backups.md).

## Quick Reference

| Scenario | RTO | RPO | Procedure |
| -------- | --- | --- | --------- |
| Single container failure | 15 min | < 24 hrs | [Container Recovery](#single-container-recovery) |
| Proxmox host failure | 2-4 hrs | < 24 hrs | [Full Host Recovery](#full-host-recovery) |
| Database corruption | 30 min | < 24 hrs | [Database Recovery](#database-recovery) |
| Network services down | 5 min | N/A | [Network Recovery](#network-services-recovery) |

## Service Dependencies

### Recovery Order (Critical Path)

Recovery must follow this order due to service dependencies:

```text
1. Proxmox VE host
   └── 2. Network Services (LXC 101) - AdGuard DNS
       └── 3. Traefik (LXC 200) - Reverse proxy
           └── 4. Authelia (LXC 202) - SSO/Auth
               └── 5. All other services
```

### Tier 1: Infrastructure (Recover First)

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies | Critical For |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ | ------------ |
| - | Proxmox VE | 192.168.1.215 | None | Everything |
| 101 | Network Services | 10.100.1.101 / 192.168.1.196 | Proxmox | DNS resolution |
| 200 | Traefik | 10.100.2.200 / 192.168.1.235 | DNS | HTTPS access to all services |
| 202 | Authelia | 10.100.2.202 | Traefik | Protected service access |

### Tier 2: Core Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 500 | Monitoring | 10.100.5.100 | Traefik |
| 201 | Dashboards | 10.100.2.201 | Traefik |

### Tier 3: Application Services

| ID | Service | IP | Dependencies |
| -- | ------- | -- | ------------ |
| 304 | Immich | 10.100.3.104 / 192.168.1.222 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 401 | Jellyfin | 10.100.4.101 / 192.168.1.226 | Traefik |
| 402 | Media Management | 10.100.4.102 | Traefik, Authelia, VPN (gluetun) |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | 10.100.5.101 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 502 | n8n | 10.100.5.102 | Traefik, Authelia |
| 503 | Obsidian Sync | 10.100.5.103 | Traefik |
| 504 | Documents | 10.100.5.104 | Traefik, Authelia |

## Recovery Procedures

### Single Container Recovery

*Time estimate: 15-30 minutes*
This uses PBS (Proxmox Backup Server) incremental backups with OpenTofu for infrastructure recreation.

#### Step 1: Prepare for Recreation

Get the IP address, remove the old SSH host key, and rename the state file. This ensures OpenTofu recreates all resources and can connect to the new LXC without mid-apply failures.

```bash
cd tofu/apps/<APP>

# Get IP before renaming state (so tofu output still works)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address 2>/dev/null || echo "")

# Remove old SSH key (prevents host key mismatch during apply)
[ -n "$IP" ] && ssh-keygen -R $IP

# Rename state to force full recreation
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Step 2: Recreate Infrastructure

```bash
task tofu:init APP=<APP>
task tofu:apply APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Create new LXC container with same VMID
- Run Ansible to configure base system
- Deploy docker-compose and config files
- Start Docker containers (with empty/fresh data)
- Configure PBS backup client
- Deploy Pulse/Arcane agents

#### Step 3: Restore Data from PBS

```bash
task pbs:backup:restore APP=<APP>
```

This will:

- Stop Docker containers
- Restore `/config` directory from PBS backup
- Restore Docker volume data from PBS backup
- Start Docker containers

#### Step 4: Verify and Cleanup

1. Check the app is working at its URL
1. Verify data is restored correctly
1. (Optional) Compare state files to verify same resources are tracked:

```bash
# Compare resource lists between old and new state
task tofu:state APP=<APP> > /tmp/new.txt
task tofu:state APP=<APP> -- -state=terraform.tfstate.old > /tmp/old.txt
diff /tmp/old.txt /tmp/new.txt  # Should show no differences
```

1. Clean up old state file:

```bash
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

#### Example: Recovering n8n

```bash
cd tofu/apps/n8n

# 1. Prepare (get IP, remove SSH key, rename state)
IP=$(tofu output -raw ip_address)
ssh-keygen -R $IP
mv terraform.tfstate terraform.tfstate.old

# 2. Recreate
task tofu:init APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# 3. Restore data
task pbs:backup:restore APP=n8n

# 4. Verify
curl -s http://10.100.5.102:5678/healthz
# Should return: {"status":"ok"}

# 5. Cleanup
rm terraform.tfstate.old
```

### Database Recovery

#### Immich (PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs)

```bash
# 1. List available dumps
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "ls -lh /tank/backups/database-dumps/immich-postgres-*"

# 2. Restore using task
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

#### Jellystat (PostgreSQL)

```bash
# 1. Copy dump to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 401 /tank/backups/database-dumps/jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz /tmp/"

# 2. SSH to Jellyfin container
ssh root@10.100.4.101

# 3. Restore
docker exec -i jellystat-db psql -U jellystat -d jellystat < /tmp/jellystat-postgres-*.sql
```

#### SQLite Databases (OpenWebUI, n8n)

```bash
# Copy from backup dump directory to container
ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct push 501 /tank/backups/database-dumps/openwebui-*.db /config/openwebui/webui.db"

# Restart the service
ssh root@10.100.5.101 "cd /config && docker compose restart"
```

### Network Services Recovery

If DNS (AdGuard) is down, LAN devices cannot resolve homelab domains.

1. **Temporary workaround** - Use direct IPs:
   - Proxmox: <https://192.168.1.215:8006>
   - Traefik: <http://192.168.1.235:8080> (dashboard)

2. **Recover AdGuard container**

   ```bash
   # Check container status
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct status 101"

   # Start if stopped
   ssh root@192.168.1.215 "pct start 101"

   # Check AdGuard service
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "docker ps"
   ssh root@10.100.1.101 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   ```

3. **Verify DNS resolution**

   ```bash
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

### Full Host Recovery

This procedure assumes complete Proxmox host failure requiring reinstall.

#### Phase 1: Proxmox Installation (30 min)

1. Boot from Proxmox ISO
2. Install to boot drive
3. Configure network:
   - IP: 192.168.1.215/24
   - Gateway: 192.168.1.1
   - DNS: 1.1.1.1 (temporarily)
4. Import ZFS pool:

   ```bash
   zpool import tank
   ```

#### Phase 2: Restore Configuration (30 min)

1. Clone the homelab repo:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/darshan-rambhia/proxmox-homelab.git
   cd homelab
   ```

2. Sync backup configuration:

   ```bash
   task backup:sync
   ```

3. Restore containers from local backups (if ZFS pool survived):

   ```bash
   # List available backups
   ls /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/

   # Restore each container - start with Tier 1
   pct restore 101 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
   pct restore 200 /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-200-*.tar.zst
   # ... continue for all containers
   ```

#### Phase 3: Cloud Recovery (if local backups lost)

If ZFS pool is lost, restore from Backblaze B2:

1. Install rclone and configure with existing credentials:

   ```bash
   apt install rclone
   # Configure b2 and b2-crypt remotes
   ```

2. Download backups:

   ```bash
   rclone copy b2-crypt:vzdump /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/
   rclone copy b2-crypt:database-dumps /tank/backups/database-dumps/
   ```

3. Restore containers as in Phase 2

#### Phase 4: Verification (30 min)

1. Start containers in dependency order:

   ```bash
   pct start 101  # Network Services
   pct start 200  # Traefik
   pct start 202  # Authelia
   # ... rest of containers
   ```

2. Verify services:

   ```bash
   # DNS
   dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev

   # Web services
   curl -k https://homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev
   ```

3. Re-apply OpenTofu if needed:

   ```bash
   task tofu:init APP=traefik
   task tofu:plan APP=traefik
   # Review and apply if needed
   ```

## Verification Checklist

After any recovery, verify:

- [ ] DNS resolution working (`dig @192.168.1.196 homepage.homelab.rambtech.dev`)
- [ ] Traefik dashboard accessible (<https://traefik.homelab.rambtech.dev>)
- [ ] Authelia login working
- [ ] Homepage loads and shows service status
- [ ] Immich accessible and photos loading
- [ ] Monitoring (Grafana) showing metrics
- [ ] Backups scheduled (`cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg`)

## Preventive Measures

### Regular Testing

- Monthly: Test restore of one container to verify backups
- Quarterly: Full DR drill - document actual recovery time

### Monitoring Gaps to Address

- [ ] Add backup failure alerting (see proxmox-homelab-v9t)
- [ ] Add Prometheus scrape targets for all services (see proxmox-homelab-30m)

## Contact & Escalation

For issues beyond this runbook:

- Proxmox Forums: <https://forum.proxmox.com/>
- Backblaze Support: <https://www.backblaze.com/help/>
