services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Loki - Log aggregation
  # ==========================================================================
  loki:
    image: grafana/loki:3.3.2
    container_name: loki
    command: -config.file=/etc/loki/local-config.yaml
    ports:
      - "3100:3100"
    volumes:
      - ./loki/config.yaml:/etc/loki/local-config.yaml:ro
      - loki_data:/loki
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3100/ready || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana Alloy - Unified telemetry collector (replaces OTEL Collector)
  # ==========================================================================
  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.5.1
    container_name: alloy
    command:
      - run
      - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
      - --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy/data
      - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver (backwards compat)
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver (backwards compat)
      - "12345:12345" # Alloy UI
    volumes:
      - ./alloy/config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /var/log:/var/log/host:ro
      - alloy_data:/var/lib/alloy/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
      - loki
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:12345/-/ready"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
      - '--web.external-url=https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
      - '--web.external-url=https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9093/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.4.0
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.11.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # alertmanager-ntfy-formatter - Format Alertmanager webhooks for ntfy
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager-ntfy-formatter:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: alertmanager-ntfy-formatter
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir flask requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        from flask import Flask, request
        import requests
        import json

        app = Flask(__name__)

        @app.route("/webhook", methods=["POST"])
        def webhook():
            data = request.json
            status = data.get("status", "unknown")
            receiver = data.get("receiver", "unknown")
            alerts = data.get("alerts", [])

            if not alerts:
                return "No alerts", 200

            # Format title
            first_alert = alerts[0]
            alertname = first_alert.get("labels", {}).get("alertname", "Unknown")
            if status == "firing":
                title = f"🚨 Alert: {alertname}"
                priority = first_alert.get("labels", {}).get("severity") == "critical" and "urgent" or "default"
                tags = "critical,rotating_light" if priority == "urgent" else "warning,homelab"
            else:
                title = f"✅ Resolved: {alertname}"
                priority = "default"
                tags = "resolved,homelab"

            # Format message body
            message_lines = [f"Status: {status.title()}", f"Receiver: {receiver}", ""]
            for alert in alerts:
                labels = alert.get("labels", {})
                annotations = alert.get("annotations", {})
                message_lines.append(f"Alert: {labels.get('alertname', 'Unknown')}")
                message_lines.append(f"Instance: {labels.get('instance', 'N/A')}")
                message_lines.append(f"Severity: {labels.get('severity', 'N/A')}")
                message_lines.append(f"Starts at: {alert.get('startsAt', 'N/A')}")
                if alert.get("endsAt") and alert["endsAt"] != "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z":
                    message_lines.append(f"Ends at: {alert['endsAt']}")
                if annotations.get("summary"):
                    message_lines.append(f"Summary: {annotations['summary']}")
                if annotations.get("description"):
                    message_lines.append(f"Description: {annotations['description']}")
                if alert.get("generatorURL"):
                    message_lines.append(f"Source: {alert['generatorURL']}")
                message_lines.append("")

            message = "\n".join(message_lines)

            # Send to ntfy
            ntfy_url = f"http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?priority={priority}&tags={tags}"
            headers = {"Title": title}
            resp = requests.post(ntfy_url, data=message.encode('utf-8'), headers=headers)
            print(f"Formatted alert: {title} -> ntfy (status: {resp.status_code})")

            return "OK", 200

        app.run(host="0.0.0.0", port=5001)
        ENDSCRIPT
    ports:
      - "5001:5001"
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:5001/ || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  alloy_data:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:

Based on the search results, I found several resources for ntfy alertmanager templates and examples. Here's what I found:

## Official ntfy Alertmanager Template

ntfy has a pre-defined alertmanager template that formats Alertmanager webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts), which can be found in alertmanager.yml. You can use this template by setting the X-Template header or query parameter to "alertmanager" (such as ?template=alertmanager).

## Third-Party Integration Examples

There are several GitHub projects providing alertmanager-to-ntfy integration with template examples:

### 1. **alexbakker/alertmanager-ntfy** (Most Featured)
An example configuration is available in config.example.yml. This project supports:
- Customizing the title and description of the notification using Go's templating engine
- Dynamic priority based on alert status
- Tags with conditional display based on alert state

Example template from this project:
```yaml
templates:
  title: | 
    {{ if eq .Status "resolved" }}Resolved: {{ end }}{{ index .Annotations "summary" }}
  description: |
    {{ index .Annotations "description" }}
```

### 2. **xenrox/ntfy-alertmanager**
You can optionally provide a path for a rendering template to fine-tune the notification body, and the format uses scfg with an example configuration file in the repo.

### 3. **Other Bridges**
- **pinpox/alertmanager-ntfy**: Listens for webhooks from Alertmanager and sends them to ntfy push notifications, with configuration done via environment variables
- **aTable/ntfy_alertmanager_bridge**: A basic JavaScript-based bridge with jq selector support

For the most comprehensive and actively maintained solution with template examples, I'd recommend checking out the **alexbakker/alertmanager-ntfy** repository on GitHub.

# Alertmanager Configuration
# Routes alerts to ntfy for centralized notification aggregation

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# Route tree
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'severity']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: 'ntfy'

  routes:
    # Critical alerts - immediate notification with high priority
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: 'ntfy-critical'
      group_wait: 10s
      repeat_interval: 1h

    # Warning alerts - batched notifications with default priority
    - match:
        severity: warning
      receiver: 'ntfy'
      group_wait: 1m
      repeat_interval: 4h

# Inhibition rules
inhibit_rules:
  # Inhibit warning if critical is firing for same alertname
  - source_match:
      severity: 'critical'
    target_match:
      severity: 'warning'
    equal: ['alertname', 'instance']

# Receivers
receivers:
  # ntfy receiver for warnings
  - name: 'ntfy'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with X-Template header to use server-side template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?priority=default&tags=warning,homelab'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          http_headers:
            X-Template:
              values: ['alertmanager']
          follow_redirects: true

  # ntfy receiver for critical alerts

    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with X-Template header to use server-side template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?priority=urgent&tags=rotating_light,critical'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          http_headers:
            X-Template:
              values: ['alertmanager']
          follow_redirects: true

# Templates for message formatting
templates:
  - '/etc/alertmanager/templates/*.tmpl'

# Alertmanager Configuration
# Routes alerts to ntfy for centralized notification aggregation

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# Route tree
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'severity']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: 'ntfy'

  routes:
    # Critical alerts - immediate notification with high priority
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: 'ntfy-critical'
      group_wait: 10s
      repeat_interval: 1h

    # Warning alerts - batched notifications with default priority
    - match:
        severity: warning
      receiver: 'ntfy'
      group_wait: 1m
      repeat_interval: 4h

# Inhibition rules
inhibit_rules:
  # Inhibit warning if critical is firing for same alertname
  - source_match:
      severity: 'critical'
    target_match:
      severity: 'warning'
    equal: ['alertname', 'instance']

# Receivers
receivers:
  # ntfy receiver for warnings
  - name: 'ntfy'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with built-in alertmanager template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=yes&priority=default&tags=warning,homelab'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          follow_redirects: true

  # ntfy receiver for critical alerts
  - name: 'ntfy-critical'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with built-in alertmanager template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=yes&priority=urgent&tags=rotating_light,critical'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          follow_redirects: true

# Templates for message formatting
templates:
  - '/etc/alertmanager/templates/*.tmpl'

content.content:
# Message Templating in ntfy

## Triggering Templates

Templates are activated via the `X-Template` header or its aliases (`Template`, `Tpl`) or the `?template=` query parameter. You can set it to:

- A **pre-defined template name** like `github`, `grafana`, or `alertmanager`
- A **custom template name** (loads from template directory)
- `yes` or `1` for **inline templating**

## Available Fields

Templates can define two key sections:

- **`title`**: Populates the notification title
- **`message`**: Populates the notification body

Both are processed as Go templates that parse the incoming JSON payload.

## JSON Request Structure

When sending templated messages, POST JSON to your topic with the payload data. The server transforms it according to template rules. Basic example:

```json
{
  "status": "firing",
  "type": "cpu",
  "server": "example.com",
  "percent": 99
}
```

## Template Files

Custom templates go in the template directory (default: `/etc/ntfy/templates/`) with `.yml` extension. A sample structure:

```yaml
title: |
  {{- if eq .status "firing" }}
    Alert
  {{- else }}
    Resolved
  {{- end }}
message: |
  Status: {{ .status }}
  Type: {{ .type }}
```

## Accessible Variables

Templates receive the entire incoming JSON object. Access fields using dot notation: `{{ .fieldname }}` or nested fields like `{{ .error.level }}`. The documentation mentions supporting "String Functions," "Math Functions," and "Date Functions" from Sprig, plus type conversion utilities.

# Alertmanager Configuration
# Routes alerts to ntfy for centralized notification aggregation

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m

# Route tree
route:
  group_by: ['alertname', 'severity']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 4h
  receiver: 'ntfy'

  routes:
    # Critical alerts - immediate notification with high priority
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: 'ntfy-critical'
      group_wait: 10s
      repeat_interval: 1h

    # Warning alerts - batched notifications with default priority
    - match:
        severity: warning
      receiver: 'ntfy'
      group_wait: 1m
      repeat_interval: 4h

# Inhibition rules
inhibit_rules:
  # Inhibit warning if critical is firing for same alertname
  - source_match:
      severity: 'critical'
    target_match:
      severity: 'warning'
    equal: ['alertname', 'instance']

# Receivers
receivers:
  # ntfy receiver for warnings
  - name: 'ntfy'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with alertmanager template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=alertmanager&priority=default&tags=warning,homelab'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          follow_redirects: true

  # ntfy receiver for critical alerts
  - name: 'ntfy-critical'
    webhook_configs:
      # ntfy with alertmanager template
      - url: 'http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts?template=alertmanager&priority=urgent&tags=rotating_light,critical'
        send_resolved: true
        max_alerts: 10
        http_config:
          follow_redirects: true

# Templates for message formatting
templates:
  - '/etc/alertmanager/templates/*.tmpl'

## ntfy v2.15.0 Built-in Templates for Alertmanager and Grafana

The following pre-defined templates are available in ntfy: **github**, **grafana**, and **alertmanager**.

### Available Built-in Templates:

1. **github** - Formats a subset of GitHub webhook payloads (PRs, issues, new star, new watcher, new comment). See github.yml.

2. **grafana** - Formats Grafana webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts). See grafana.yml.

3. **alertmanager** - Formats Alertmanager webhook payloads (firing/resolved alerts). See alertmanager.yml.

### Key Features:

Pre-defined templates and custom templates for enhanced JSON webhook support were introduced in v2.14.0, along with support of advanced template functions based on the Sprig library.

### Usage:

When X-Template: <n> (aliases: Template: <n>, Tpl: <n>) or ?template=<n> is set, ntfy will transform the message and/or title based on one of the built-in pre-defined templates.

Setting the X-Template header or query parameter to a pre-defined template name (one of github, grafana, or alertmanager, such as ?template=github) will use the built-in template with that name.

### Template Customization:

To override the pre-defined templates, you can place a file with the same name in the template directory (defaults to /etc/ntfy/templates, can be overridden with template-dir). See custom templates for more details.

### Template Functions:

ntfy supports a subset of the Sprig template functions (originally copied from Sprig, thank you to the Sprig developers 🙏). Great findings! ntfy v2.15.0 has three built-in templates: `github`, `grafana`, and `alertmanager`.

For your backup notifications use case, you have two options:

**Option 1: Use existing `alertmanager` template**
- Keep using Prometheus/Alertmanager for backup failure/success alerts
- The built-in `alertmanager` template will format them nicely
- This is the most consistent approach since you're already using Alertmanager

**Option 2: Create custom template for backups**
- Create a custom template specifically for backup notifications (e.g., `backup.yml`)
- Place it in `/etc/ntfy/templates/` directory
- This gives you full control over formatting backup-specific fields (job name, retention, size, duration, etc.)
- Your backup scripts would POST directly to ntfy with `?template=backup`

I'd recommend **Option 2** if your backup scripts (PBS, Proxmox backups) can POST directly to ntfy, because:
- Backup events are operational events, not metric-based alerts
- You can format backup-specific details exactly how you want
- Direct notification = faster feedback
- Keeps Prometheus/Alertmanager focused on metric-based monitoring

## Uptime Kuma Webhook Payload Format

The standard webhook payload from Uptime Kuma has the structure: `{ heartbeat: heartbeatJSON, monitor: monitorJSON, msg, }`

### Detailed JSON Example

Here's a complete example of the JSON payload sent by Uptime Kuma:

```json
{
  "heartbeat": {
    "monitorID": 1,
    "status": 0,
    "time": "2023-03-26 10:07:50.153",
    "msg": "Request failed with status code 526",
    "important": true,
    "duration": 30
  },
  "monitor": {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Password Pusher",
    "description": null,
    "url": "https://xxx.xxx.net/",
    "method": "GET",
    "hostname": null,
    "port": null,
    "maxretries": 2,
    "weight": 2000,
    "active": 1,
    "type": "http",
    "interval": 30,
    "retryInterval": 30,
    "resendInterval": 0,
    "keyword": null,
    "expiryNotification": false,
    "ignoreTls": false,
    "upsideDown": false,
    "packetSize": 56,
    "maxredirects": 10,
    "accepted_statuscodes": ["200-299"],
    "dns_resolve_type": "A",
    "dns_resolve_server": "1.1.1.1",
    "dns_last_result": null,
    "docker_container": "",
    "docker_host": null,
    "proxyId": null,
    "notificationIDList": {
      "1": true
    },
    "tags": [],
    "maintenance": false,
    "mqttTopic": "",
    "mqttSuccessMessage": "",
    "databaseQuery": null,
    "authMethod": null
  }
}
```

### Key Points

- The payload is accessed using `trigger.json` when you're using the application/json Content Type in Uptime Kuma's notification
- The `heartbeat` object contains status information about the monitor check
- The `monitor` object contains configuration details about the monitored service
- Uptime Kuma also supports custom body webhooks where you can define your own JSON structure with template variables

## Uptime Kuma Webhook Payload Format

The standard webhook payload from Uptime Kuma has the structure: `{ heartbeat: heartbeatJSON, monitor: monitorJSON, msg, }`

    "type": "http",

## Webhook Notification Configuration

Webhook notification targets perform HTTP requests to a configurable URL, with the URL supporting templating to inject message contents, metadata and secrets.

## Available Fields for JSON Payloads

For configuration options that support templating, the Handlebars syntax can be used to access properties including {{ fields.<n> }} for any metadata fields of the notification.

The webhook body configuration should be sent and supports templating to inject message contents, metadata and secrets.

## Example JSON Payload Formats

Here are some example JSON payload formats found in the documentation:

**Basic Format:**
```json
{
  "title": "{{ escape title }}",
  "message": "{{ escape message }}"
}
```

**Discord Example:**
Method: POST with Body: { "content": "``` {{ escape message }}```" }

**Pushover Example:**
{ "token": "{{ secrets.apikey }}", "user": "{{ secrets.userkey }}", "title": "{{ title }}", "message": "{{ escape message }}", "priority": "0", "timestamp": "{{ timestamp }}" }

**Mattermost Example:**
{ "text": "```\nField | Value\n-----------|----------------\nTitle | {{ title }}\nMessage | {{ message }}\nLogs | {{ logs }}\nSeverity | {{ severity }}\nTimestamp | {{ timestamp }}\n```"

## Available Template Variables

The following variables can be used in webhook JSON payloads:
- `{{ title }}` - Notification title
- `{{ message }}` - Notification message
- `{{ escape message }}` - Escaped message (recommended for JSON)
- `{{ timestamp }}` - Timestamp of the notification
- `{{ severity }}` - Severity level
- `{{ logs }}` - Log information
- `{{ fields }}` - Metadata fields namespace
- `{{ secrets.<key> }}` - Access to secret values

{{ json <value/property> }}: Render a value as JSON, which can be useful to pass a whole sub-namespace (e.g. fields) as a part of a JSON payload (e.g. {{ json fields }}).

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# PBS Backup Script for ${container_name} (Container ${container_id})
# =============================================================================
# Generated by lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module
# Namespace: ${namespace}
# Schedule: ${schedule}
# Retention: ${retention} backups
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# =============================================================================
# Configuration
# =============================================================================

CONTAINER_ID="${container_id}"
NAMESPACE="${namespace}"
RETENTION="${retention}"
LOG_FILE="/var/log/pbs-backups/$${NAMESPACE}.log"

# PBS repository from environment (set by systemd service)
# PBS_REPOSITORY, PBS_NAMESPACE, PBS_PASSWORD, PBS_FINGERPRINT

# Backup paths
INCLUDE_PATHS=(
%{ for path in include_paths ~}
  "${path}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

EXCLUDE_PATTERNS=(
%{ for pattern in exclude_paths ~}
  "${pattern}"
%{ endfor ~}
)

# Alert configuration
NTFY_URL="${ntfy_url}"
NTFY_PRIORITY="${ntfy_priority}"
NTFY_TAGS="${ntfy_tags}"

# =============================================================================
# Helper Functions
# =============================================================================

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*"
}

send_alert() {
    local title="$1"
    local message="$2"
    local priority="$${3:-$${NTFY_PRIORITY}}"

    curl -sf \
        -H "Title: $${title}" \
        -H "Priority: $${priority}" \
        -H "Tags: $${NTFY_TAGS}" \
        -d "$${message}" \
        "$${NTFY_URL}" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# =============================================================================
# Pre-Backup Commands (Database Dumps, etc.)
# =============================================================================

run_pre_backup_hooks() {
    log "Running pre-backup hooks..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
%{ for cmd in pre_backup_commands ~}
    # ${cmd.name}
    log "  - ${cmd.name}"
    if timeout ${cmd.timeout} bash -c '${cmd.command}'; then
        log "    ✓ Success"
    else
        local hook_exit_code=$$?
        log "    ✗ Failed (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})"
        send_alert "Backup Hook Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "Pre-backup hook failed: ${cmd.name} (exit code: $${hook_exit_code})" \
            "high"
        return 1
    fi

%{ endfor ~}
%{ else ~}
    log "  (No pre-backup hooks configured)"
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Cleanup Functions
# =============================================================================

cleanup_temp_files() {
    log "Cleaning up temporary dump files..."

%{ if length(pre_backup_commands) > 0 ~}
    # Remove database dumps after successful backup
    find /config -type f \( -name "*.sql.gz" -o -name "*.db.backup" \) -mmin +60 -delete 2>/dev/null || true
%{ endif ~}
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Backup Function
# =============================================================================

run_backup() {
    local backup_id="lxc-$${CONTAINER_ID}"
    local backup_time=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
    local start_time=$(date +%s)

    log "=== Starting PBS Backup for ${container_name} ==="
    log "Repository: $${PBS_REPOSITORY}"
    log "Namespace: $${PBS_NAMESPACE}"
    log "Backup ID: $${backup_id}"
    log "Backup time: $${backup_time}"

    # Build exclude arguments
    local exclude_args=""
    for pattern in "$${EXCLUDE_PATTERNS[@]}"; do
        exclude_args="$${exclude_args} --exclude '$${pattern}'"
    done

    # Build backup command
    local backup_cmd="proxmox-backup-client backup"

    for path in "$${INCLUDE_PATHS[@]}"; do
        local archive_name=$(basename "$${path}")
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} '$${archive_name}.pxar:$${path}'"
    done

    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --repository \$PBS_REPOSITORY"
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --ns \$PBS_NAMESPACE"
%{ endif ~}
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-id '$${backup_id}'"
    backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} --backup-time $(date +%s)"

    if [ -n "$${exclude_args}" ]; then
        backup_cmd="$${backup_cmd} $${exclude_args}"
    fi

    # Set PBS fingerprint environment variable for certificate verification
    export PBS_FINGERPRINT

    log "Command: $${backup_cmd}"

    # Run backup
    local backup_exit_code=0
    eval "$${backup_cmd}" || backup_exit_code=$$?

    if [ "$${backup_exit_code}" -eq 0 ]; then
        local end_time=$(date +%s)
        local duration=$((end_time - start_time))

        log "✓ Backup completed successfully in $${duration}s"

        # Prune old backups
        log "Pruning old backups (keep $${RETENTION})..."
        proxmox-backup-client prune "host/$${backup_id}" \
            --repository "$PBS_REPOSITORY" \
%{ if namespace != "" ~}
            --ns "$PBS_NAMESPACE" \
%{ endif ~}
            --keep-last "$${RETENTION}"

        log "✓ Prune completed"

        # Cleanup temporary files
        cleanup_temp_files

        log "=== Backup Completed Successfully ==="
        return 0
    else
        log "✗ Backup failed with exit code: $${backup_exit_code}"

        send_alert "Backup Failed: ${container_name}" \
            "PBS backup failed for ${container_name} (exit code: $${backup_exit_code})" \
            "high"

        return 1
    fi
}

# =============================================================================
# Main Execution
# =============================================================================

main() {
    log "========================================"
    log "PBS Backup: ${container_name}"
    log "Container ID: ${container_id}"
    log "Namespace: ${namespace}"
    log "========================================"

    # Run pre-backup hooks
    if ! run_pre_backup_hooks; then
        log "Pre-backup hooks failed, aborting backup"
        exit 1
    fi

    # Run backup
    if ! run_backup; then
        log "Backup failed"
        exit 1
    fi

    log "All tasks completed successfully"
    exit 0
}

# Run main function
main

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Loki - Log aggregation
  # ==========================================================================
  loki:
    image: grafana/loki:3.3.2
    container_name: loki
    command: -config.file=/etc/loki/local-config.yaml
    ports:
      - "3100:3100"
    volumes:
      - ./loki/config.yaml:/etc/loki/local-config.yaml:ro
      - loki_data:/loki
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3100/ready || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana Alloy - Unified telemetry collector (replaces OTEL Collector)
  # ==========================================================================
  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.5.1
    container_name: alloy
    command:
      - run
      - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
      - --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy/data
      - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver (backwards compat)
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver (backwards compat)
      - "12345:12345" # Alloy UI
    volumes:
      - ./alloy/config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /var/log:/var/log/host:ro
      - alloy_data:/var/lib/alloy/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
      - loki
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:12345/-/ready"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
      - '--web.external-url=https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
      - '--web.external-url=https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9093/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.4.0
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.15.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  alloy_data:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:

## Uptime Kuma v2 Upgrade Research Report

Based on my comprehensive research of your current setup and Uptime Kuma v2, here's what I found:

---

### CURRENT SETUP ANALYSIS

**File:** `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab/tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/docker-compose.yml`

**Current Version:** `louislam/uptime-kuma:1` (tag `1` - latest v1)
**AutoKuma Version:** `ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0`

Your setup includes:
- 15 monitors configured in autokuma/monitors.json (HTTP, port, and internal service checks)
- Webhook notifications to ntfy
- Discord notification forwarding through ntfy
- Health checks enabled on the container

---

### LATEST UPTIME KUMA V2 RELEASE

**Latest Stable Version:** v2.0.2 (released October 2024)

**Key v2.0 Features:**
- MariaDB database support alongside SQLite
- New monitor types: Manual (static/fixed), SMTP, SNMP, RabbitMQ
- Nextcloud Talk, Brevo, Evolution API notification integrations
- Force IPv4/IPv6 selection for HTTP monitors
- Markdown rendering in monitor descriptions
- Enhanced interval display

---

### BREAKING CHANGES BETWEEN V1 AND V2

**Critical API Changes:**
- Badge duration parameters now only accept: `24`, `24h`, `30d`, `1y` (no other formats)
- Monitor retry default changed from `1` to `0`
- Email notification templating switched from custom-regex to **LiquidJS** (variables now case-sensitive, all non-matching variables ignored)
- JSON backup/restore functionality removed
- DNS cache for HTTP monitors eliminated

**Docker Changes:**
- Alpine-based images no longer supported (uses Debian)
- Debian Buster (Raspberry Pi) incompatible due to libseccomp2 library bug
- Rootless images NOT recommended for v1-to-v2 upgrade (startup issues likely)

**System Requirements:**
- Node.js 20.4+ required (versions 14, 16, 18 no longer supported)

---

### WEBHOOK & NTFY INTEGRATION COMPATIBILITY

**Good News:** Your ntfy webhook integration is compatible with v2.

**Important Details:**
- Uptime Kuma v2 has native ntfy support built-in (recommended over webhooks)
- Email notification template engine changed to LiquidJS
- Webhook payload structure remains: `{ heartbeat: heartbeatJSON, monitor: monitorJSON, msg }`
- Variable syntax changed (case-sensitive in LiquidJS)

**Your Current Setup:**
- Using webhooks to ntfy (still works in v2)
- Discord forwarding via ntfy listener (still works in v2)

---

### AUTOKUMA COMPATIBILITY WITH V2

**Critical Issue:** Your version `ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0` is outdated.

**AutoKuma v2.0.0 Changes:**
- **Uptime Kuma v2 support enabled by default** in latest releases
- v1-compatible images available with `uptime-kuma-v1-` prefix
- Latest AutoKuma (v2.0.0) requires persistent storage for its own database
- Improved connection handling with keep-alive between syncs

**Migration Path:** You'll need to update AutoKuma to `ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:2.0.0` or `latest` when upgrading Uptime Kuma to v2 (it's backward incompatible).

---

### DATABASE MIGRATION REQUIREMENTS

**Process Overview:**
The v1-to-v2 migration aggregates the heartbeat table into a more optimized format.

**Time Estimates:**
- Small setup (20 monitors, 90 days data): ~7 minutes
- Medium setup (~1.5GB data): 20-30 minutes
- Large setup with more data: Can take hours or even 24+ hours

**Critical Safety Requirements:**
1. **Backup your data directory multiple times before starting**
2. **NEVER interrupt the migration** - if interrupted, must restore from backup and restart
3. Monitor logs during the entire migration process
4. Plan for downtime (service will be unavailable during migration)

**Supported Migration Path:**
- SQLite → SQLite in v2 (fully supported)
- SQLite → MariaDB (NOT supported directly; requires 3rd party tools)
- Current setup uses SQLite (safe to migrate)

---

### PERFORMANCE & KNOWN ISSUES

**Performance Improvements in v2:**
- External MariaDB support for large deployments
- Aggregated heartbeat storage reduces table scans
- Server-side pagination for events
- Improved async operations

**Known Migration Issues (v2.0.2):**
- Database migration locks can occur if process is interrupted
- SQLite transaction errors reported in some cases
- False positive for Google Chrome during migration (fixed in v2.0.2)
- Some slower systems report extended migration times

**Performance Optimization Tips:**
- Reduce data retention period
- Lower monitor check frequency
- Reduce total number of active monitors
- Use VACUUM function to clean up database history

Based on my comprehensive research of your current setup and Uptime Kuma v2, here's what I found:

### LATEST UPTIME KUMA V2 RELEASE

**Latest Stable Version:** v2.0.2 (released October 2024)

**Key v2.0 Features:**
- MariaDB database support alongside SQLite
- New monitor types: Manual (static/fixed), SMTP, SNMP, RabbitMQ
- Nextcloud Talk, Brevo, Evolution API notification integrations
- Force IPv4/IPv6 selection for HTTP monitors
- Markdown rendering in monitor descriptions

---

### BREAKING CHANGES BETWEEN V1 AND V2

**Critical API Changes:**
- Badge duration parameters now only accept: `24`, `24h`, `30d`, `1y` (no other formats)
- Monitor retry default changed from `1` to `0`
- Email notification templating switched from custom-regex to **LiquidJS** (variables now case-sensitive, all non-matching variables ignored)
- JSON backup/restore functionality removed
- DNS cache for HTTP monitors eliminated

**Docker Changes:**
- Alpine-based images no longer supported (uses Debian)
- Debian Buster (Raspberry Pi) incompatible due to libseccomp2 library bug
- Rootless images NOT recommended for v1-to-v2 upgrade (startup issues likely)

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Loki - Log aggregation
  # ==========================================================================
  loki:
    image: grafana/loki:3.3.2
    container_name: loki
    command: -config.file=/etc/loki/local-config.yaml
    ports:
      - "3100:3100"
    volumes:
      - ./loki/config.yaml:/etc/loki/local-config.yaml:ro
      - loki_data:/loki
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3100/ready || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana Alloy - Unified telemetry collector (replaces OTEL Collector)
  # ==========================================================================
  alloy:
    image: grafana/alloy:v1.5.1
    container_name: alloy
    command:
      - run
      - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
      - --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy/data
      - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC receiver (backwards compat)
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver (backwards compat)
      - "12345:12345" # Alloy UI
    volumes:
      - ./alloy/config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /var/log:/var/log/host:ro
      - alloy_data:/var/lib/alloy/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
      - loki
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "-qO-", "http://localhost:12345/-/ready"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.1.0
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
      - '--web.external-url=https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.28.1
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
      - '--web.external-url=https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9093/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:11.4.0
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.15.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ./ntfy/templates:/etc/ntfy/templates:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m

bd create \
  --title="Upgrade Uptime Kuma to v2.0.0 and AutoKuma to v2.0.0" \
  --type=task \
  --priority=2 \
  --body="## Overview
Upgrade Uptime Kuma from v1 to v2.0.0 and AutoKuma from v1.0.0 to v2.0.0 to gain new features and improvements.

## Current Versions
- Uptime Kuma: \`louislam/uptime-kuma:1\` (v1.x)
- AutoKuma: \`ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0\`

## Target Versions
- Uptime Kuma: \`louislam/uptime-kuma:2.0.0\`
- AutoKuma: \`ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:2.0.0\`

## Breaking Changes to Address

### Critical Changes
1. **AutoKuma Compatibility**: Must upgrade AutoKuma to v2.0.0 (v1.0.0 incompatible with Uptime Kuma v2)
2. **Database Migration**: SQLite auto-migrates but takes 20 mins to 2+ hours
   - **NEVER interrupt migration** - must restore from backup and restart if interrupted
   - Migration aggregates heartbeat table for better performance
3. **Docker Image**: Now Debian-based (was Alpine)
4. **Monitor Retry Default**: Changed from 1 to 0

### Compatible (No Changes Needed)
- ✅ ntfy webhook integration (payload format unchanged)
- ✅ Monitor definitions in autokuma/monitors.json
- ✅ Discord forwarding via ntfy

## Migration Steps

### 1. Pre-Migration (CRITICAL)
- [ ] Backup \`uptime_kuma_data\` Docker volume multiple times
- [ ] Document current state (15 monitors in autokuma/monitors.json)
- [ ] Schedule maintenance window (expect 20 mins to 2 hours downtime)

### 2. Update Configuration
File: \`tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/docker-compose.yml\`

\`\`\`yaml
uptime-kuma:
  image: louislam/uptime-kuma:2.0.0  # was: :1

autokuma:
  image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:2.0.0  # was: :1.0.0
\`\`\`

### 3. Apply Changes
\`\`\`bash
cd /Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/homelab
task tofu:plan APP=monitoring
task tofu:apply APP=monitoring
\`\`\`

### 4. Monitor Migration
\`\`\`bash
# Watch migration logs (DO NOT INTERRUPT)
ssh root@10.100.5.100
docker logs -f uptime-kuma
\`\`\`

### 5. Post-Migration Verification
- [ ] Verify all 15 monitors are running
- [ ] Test ntfy webhook notifications
- [ ] Test Discord alert forwarding via ntfy
- [ ] Check Uptime Kuma UI is accessible: https://status.homelab.rambtech.dev
- [ ] Verify AutoKuma sync completed successfully

## Known Issues & Mitigations
- **Long migration time**: Can take hours for large databases - plan accordingly
- **Database locks**: If interrupted, must restore from backup
- **False positive Chrome detection**: Fixed in v2.0.2 (using v2.0.0, shouldn't affect us)

## New Features in v2.0
- MariaDB support (optional, currently using SQLite)
- New monitor types: Manual, SMTP, SNMP, RabbitMQ
- Force IPv4/IPv6 selection for HTTP monitors
- Markdown rendering in monitor descriptions
- Improved performance with aggregated heartbeat storage

## References
- Migration Guide: https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/wiki/Migration-From-v1-To-v2
- v2.0.0 Release Notes: https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/releases
- AutoKuma GitHub: https://github.com/BigBoot/AutoKuma
- Performance Discussion: https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/issues/4500
- v2.0.0 Beta Notes: https://github.com/louislam/uptime-kuma/wiki/2.0.0-beta.0

## Risk Assessment
- **Impact**: Medium (15 monitors, webhook integrations)
- **Downtime**: 20 minutes to 2 hours
- **Rollback**: Restore from backup if migration fails
- **Compatibility Risk**: Low (webhook format unchanged)"

        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"

  --title="Update PBS backup scripts to use ntfy pbs-backup template" \
  --type=task \
  --priority=2 \
  --body="## Overview
Update PBS backup scripts to send structured JSON notifications to ntfy using the new \`pbs-backup\` template instead of plain text alerts.

## Current State
PBS backup scripts in \`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl\` currently send simple text notifications via curl:

\`\`\`bash
send_alert() {
    local title=\"\$1\"
    local message=\"\$2\"
    local priority=\"\${3:-\${NTFY_PRIORITY}}\"

    curl -sf \\
        -H \"Title: \${title}\" \\
        -H \"Priority: \${priority}\" \\
        -H \"Tags: \${NTFY_TAGS}\" \\
        -d \"\${message}\" \\
        \"\${NTFY_URL}\" 2>/dev/null || true
}
\`\`\`

## New Template Available
Custom ntfy template created at \`tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ntfy/templates/pbs-backup.yml\` that formats:
- Container name and ID
- Backup status (success/failure)
- Duration
- Backup size
- Retention settings
- Error messages (for failures)

### Expected JSON Payload Format
\`\`\`json
{
  \"status\": \"success|failure\",
  \"container_name\": \"n8n\",
  \"container_id\": \"502\",
  \"namespace\": \"lxc-containers\",
  \"duration\": 120,
  \"backup_size\": \"1.2 GB\",
  \"retention\": 7,
  \"error_message\": \"...\" (optional, for failures),
  \"timestamp\": \"2025-12-19 23:30:00\"
}
\`\`\`

## Tasks

### 1. Update send_alert Function
File: \`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/pbs-backup.sh.tftpl\`

Replace simple text alerts with JSON payload:
\`\`\`bash
send_backup_notification() {
    local status=\"\$1\"
    local duration=\"\${2:-0}\"
    local backup_size=\"\${3:-unknown}\"
    local error_msg=\"\${4:-}\"
    
    local json_payload
    json_payload=\$(cat <<EOF
{
  \"status\": \"\${status}\",
  \"container_name\": \"${container_name}\",
  \"container_id\": \"${container_id}\",
  \"namespace\": \"\${NAMESPACE}\",
  \"duration\": \${duration},
  \"backup_size\": \"\${backup_size}\",
  \"retention\": \${RETENTION},
  \"timestamp\": \"\$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')\"
  \${error_msg:+, \"error_message\": \"\${error_msg}\"}
}
EOF
    )
    
    curl -sf \\
        -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
        -d \"\${json_payload}\" \\
        \"\${NTFY_URL}?template=pbs-backup&priority=\${NTFY_PRIORITY}&tags=\${NTFY_TAGS}\" \\
        2>/dev/null || true
}
\`\`\`

### 2. Capture Backup Metrics
Update \`run_backup()\` function to capture:
- [ ] Backup completion duration
- [ ] Backup size from PBS client output
- [ ] Parse PBS client output for size information
- [ ] Call new notification function with metrics

### 3. Update Success Notifications
Replace current success log with:
\`\`\`bash
send_backup_notification \"success\" \"\${duration}\" \"\${backup_size}\"
\`\`\`

### 4. Update Failure Notifications
Replace current failure alerts with:
\`\`\`bash
send_backup_notification \"failure\" \"\${duration}\" \"unknown\" \"\${error_message}\"
\`\`\`

### 5. Update Pre-Backup Hook Failures
Update pre-backup hook failure notifications to use new format.

### 6. Test Notifications
- [ ] Test successful backup notification
- [ ] Test failed backup notification  
- [ ] Test pre-backup hook failure notification
- [ ] Verify ntfy template renders correctly
- [ ] Verify Discord forwarding still works

## Implementation Notes

### Parsing PBS Output for Size
PBS client outputs backup size in the summary. Example parsing:

# Capture PBS output

\`\`\`

Ensure proper JSON escaping for error messages:

# Escape quotes and newlines in error messages
error_msg=\$(echo \"\${error_msg}\" | sed 's/\"/\\\\\"/g' | tr '\\n' ' ')
\`\`\`

Consider keeping old \`send_alert()\` function temporarily in case any custom scripts use it, mark as deprecated.

# Proxmox Backup Server S3 Backend Datastore Support

## Overview
PBS supports "S3 compatible object stores as storage backend for datastores," though this remains "currently a technology preview."

## Requirements & Prerequisites

**Setup Prerequisites:**
- S3 endpoint configuration under "Configuration" > "Remotes" > "S3 Endpoints"
- Pre-existing bucket with appropriate access permissions
- Access credentials (key pair) established in your S3 provider
- "permissions to get, put list and delete objects in the bucket"

**Local Cache Requirement:**
A persistent local filesystem cache is mandatory. The documentation recommends "64 GiB to 128 GiB are recommended given that cached datastore contents include also data chunks." You cannot repurpose existing datastores for this cache layer.

## Configuration Steps

**1. Create S3 Endpoint:**
```
proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create my-s3-ep \
  --access-key 'key' \
  --secret-key 'secret' \
  --endpoint '{{bucket}}.s3.{{region}}.amazonaws.com' \
  --region eu-central-1
```

**2. Create Datastore:**
```
proxmox-backup-manager datastore create my-s3-store \
  /mnt/datastore/cache-path \
  --backend type=s3,client=my-s3-ep,bucket=pbs-bucket
```

## S3-Compatible Provider Support

The platform supports templated endpoint configuration: "{{bucket}}.s3.{{region}}.amazonaws.com will be expanded to my-pbs-bucket.s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com."

**Documented Examples Include:**
- AWS S3 (vhost-style addressing)
- Ceph RADOS Gateway (path-style, custom ports)
- Cloudflare R2 (path-style with `region=auto`)

Both vhost and path-style bucket addressing are supported, with vhost-style favored by default.

## Performance & Operational Considerations

**Cost Implications:**
Users should understand that "operating as S3 backed object store might cause additional costs. Providers might charge you for storage space and API requests performed to the buckets, egress and bandwidth fees might be charged as well."

**Monitoring Required:**
"monitoring of these values and eventual costs is highly recommended."

## Key Limitations

- **Single Instance Requirement:** "A datastore cannot be shared between multiple Proxmox Backup Server instances, only one instance can operate on the datastore at a time"
- **HTTPS Only:** "Proxmox Backup Server does not support plain text communication with the S3 API, all communication is encrypted using HTTPS in transit"
- **Self-Signed Certificate Support:** For self-hosted stores, "the matching fingerprint has to be provided to the endpoint configuration"
- **Storage Failure Handling:** "If your S3 object store runs out of space while performing write operation to it, most likely cleanup operations such as cleaning up of contents within a snapshot directory will fail as well"

## Data Reuse on Fresh Installations

When recovering a datastore on a new instance, use specific flags:
```
proxmox-backup-manager datastore create my-s3-store /cache-path \
  --backend type=s3,client=endpoint,bucket=bucket \
  --reuse-datastore true \
  --overwrite-in-use true
```

The datastore name must remain identical since "the datastore name is used as prefix."

# Homelab Backup Strategy

## Overview

Two-tier backup system with daily backups for user data services and weekly backups for infrastructure. All backups are synced to Backblaze B2 (encrypted) for off-site redundancy.

## Backup Tiers

### Daily Backups (2:00 AM)

User data that changes frequently - kept for 7 days.

| ID | Service | Pre-Backup Hook |
|----|---------|-----------------|
| 304 | Immich | PostgreSQL dump |
| 501 | OpenWebUI | SQLite copy |
| 502 | n8n | SQLite copy |

### Weekly Backups (Sunday 3:00 AM)

Infrastructure services that rarely change - kept for 4 weeks.

| ID | Service | Pre-Backup Hook |
|----|---------|-----------------|
| 101 | Network Services (AdGuard) | None |
| 200 | Traefik | None |
| 201 | Dashboards | None |
| 202 | Authelia | None |
| 401 | Jellyfin | Jellystat PostgreSQL dump |
| 402 | Media Management | None |
| 500 | Monitoring | None |

### Excluded Containers

- **303 (immich-importer)** - Stateless, runs cron jobs only
- **600 (desktop-tmp)** - Temporary GUI container

## Cloud Backup (Backblaze B2)

All local backups are synced to Backblaze B2 with rclone crypt encryption.

| Sync | Schedule | Source | Destination |
|------|----------|--------|-------------|
| Photos | Daily 3:00 AM | LXC 303 `/photos` | `b2-crypt:` |
| Vzdump | Daily 4:00 AM | `/tank/backups/vzdump` | `b2-crypt:vzdump` |
| DB Dumps | Daily 4:00 AM | `/tank/backups/database-dumps` | `b2-crypt:database-dumps` |

### Daily Timeline

```text
2:00 AM - Daily vzdump backups (immich, openwebui, n8n)
3:00 AM - Photos cloud sync to B2
4:00 AM - Vzdump + DB dumps cloud sync to B2
```

## Storage Layout

```text
/tank/backups/
├── vzdump/dump/           # Proxmox vzdump backups
│   ├── vzdump-lxc-100-*.tar.zst
│   ├── vzdump-lxc-101-*.tar.zst
│   └── ...
└── database-dumps/        # Pre-backup database dumps
    ├── immich-postgres-*.sql.gz
    ├── jellystat-postgres-*.sql.gz
    ├── openwebui-*.db
    └── n8n-*.db
```

## Taskfile Commands

### Local Backups

```bash
# Sync backup config to Proxmox
task backup:sync

# View status
task backup:status

# Manual backups
task backup:now APP=openwebui    # Single container
task backup:all                   # All containers

# List backups for an app
task backup:list APP=immich

# Restore container
task backup:restore BACKUP=vzdump-lxc-304-2025_12_07-02_00_00.tar.zst TARGET_ID=305

# Immich database operations
task backup:immich:db              # Manual dump
task backup:immich:db:restore DUMP=immich-postgres-20251207_020000.sql.gz
```

### Cloud Backups

```bash
# Trigger cloud sync
task cloud:sync              # Both vzdump + photos
task cloud:sync:vzdump       # Vzdump only
task cloud:sync:photos       # Photos only

# Check status
task cloud:status            # B2 bucket sizes
task cloud:status:photos     # Photos backup status
task cloud:progress          # Check if sync is running
task cloud:dry-run           # Preview what would sync

# View logs
task cloud:logs              # Vzdump sync logs
task cloud:logs:photos       # Photos sync logs
```

## Restore Procedures

### Full Container Restore

```bash
# 1. List available backups
task backup:list APP=openwebui

# 2. Restore to new container ID (recommended for testing)

tar -xf /tank/backups/vzdump/dump/vzdump-lxc-501-2025_12_10-19_28_32.tar.zst

```

## Monitoring

### Check Backup Status

```bash
# View scheduled jobs
ssh root@homelab "cat /etc/pve/jobs.cfg"

# View hook script logs
ssh root@homelab "tail -50 /var/log/vzdump-hooks.log"

# Check local storage usage
task backup:status

# Check cloud backup status
task cloud:status
```

### Proxmox UI

Backup jobs visible at: **Datacenter > Backup**

## Files Reference

| File | Location | Purpose |
|------|----------|---------|
| Job config (source) | `scripts/backup/jobs.cfg` | Scheduled vzdump job definitions |

- PostgreSQL with pgvecto-rs extension (ML embeddings)
- Container: `immich_postgres`

- Dumps kept 4 weeks

### OpenWebUI (501)

- SQLite at `/config/openwebui/webui.db`
- Contains chat history, users, settings
- Copied directly (no sqlite3 in container)

### n8n (502)

- SQLite at `/config/n8n/database.sqlite`
- Contains workflows, credentials, execution history
