input.command:
bd create \
  --title="Migrate Backblaze B2 from rclone to PBS native S3 datastore" \
  --type=feature \
  --priority=2 \
  --body="## Overview
Replace current rclone-based Backblaze B2 sync with Proxmox Backup Server's native S3 datastore backend. This eliminates the rclone wrapper layer and integrates B2 directly into PBS.

## Current Architecture

### Backblaze B2 Setup (rclone-based)
- **Method**: Daily rclone sync jobs from Proxmox host
- **Encryption**: rclone crypt layer
- **Storage paths**:
  - \`b2-crypt:vzdump\` - PBS local backups synced daily at 4:00 AM
  - \`b2-crypt:database-dumps\` - Database dumps synced daily at 4:00 AM
  - \`b2-crypt:\` - Photos synced daily at 3:00 AM from LXC 303
- **Configuration**: rclone config in 1Password vault \"homelab\"

### Current PBS Setup
- **Location**: LXC 102 (10.100.1.102)
- **Local datastore**: Local filesystem
- **Backup targets**: 12 LXC containers (daily/weekly schedules)
- **Pre-backup hooks**: PostgreSQL dumps (Immich, Jellystat), SQLite copies (OpenWebUI, n8n)

## New Architecture (PBS S3 Native)

### PBS S3 Datastore
PBS now supports S3-compatible object stores as native datastores (technology preview feature).

**Benefits**:
- ✅ No rclone wrapper/sync delay
- ✅ Direct backup to cloud (no local-then-sync workflow)
- ✅ PBS handles encryption/deduplication natively
- ✅ Unified backup management in PBS UI
- ✅ Reduced disk I/O on Proxmox host

**Considerations**:
- ⚠️ Technology preview (not production-ready per PBS docs)
- ⚠️ Requires local cache layer (64-128 GB recommended)
- ⚠️ API costs (Backblaze charges for API requests, egress)
- ⚠️ Single PBS instance per S3 datastore (no sharing)
- ⚠️ HTTPS required (no plain HTTP)

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Research & Planning

#### 1.1 Backblaze B2 S3 API Research
- [ ] Verify Backblaze B2 S3 API endpoint format
- [ ] Document required credentials format
- [ ] Check B2 pricing for API requests vs download bandwidth
- [ ] Compare costs: current (daily rclone sync) vs native (per-backup API calls)
- [ ] Understand B2 S3 compatibility limitations (if any)

**Backblaze B2 S3 Endpoint Format:**
\`\`\`
https://s3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com
\`\`\`
(Region varies by bucket)

#### 1.2 PBS S3 Feature Testing
- [ ] Test PBS S3 datastore creation on test bucket
- [ ] Verify encryption works with S3 backend
- [ ] Test backup/restore cycle
- [ ] Measure cache size requirements for our backup set
- [ ] Test failure scenarios (network loss, API rate limits)

### Phase 2: S3 Endpoint Configuration

**File**: PBS configuration (via CLI on LXC 102)

\`\`\`bash
# Create S3 endpoint for Backblaze B2
proxmox-backup-manager s3 endpoint create backblaze-b2 \\
  --access-key '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID>' \\
  --secret-key '<B2_APPLICATION_KEY>' \\
  --endpoint 's3.us-west-004.backblazeb2.com' \\
  --region 'us-west-004'
\`\`\`

**Credentials Source**: 1Password vault \"homelab\" - rclone B2 config

### Phase 3: S3 Datastore Creation

#### 3.1 Prepare Cache Storage
- [ ] Allocate 128 GB for S3 cache on LXC 102
- [ ] Create filesystem at \`/mnt/pbs-s3-cache\` or similar
- [ ] Verify disk space available

#### 3.2 Create S3 Datastore
\`\`\`bash
# Create S3-backed datastore with local cache
proxmox-backup-manager datastore create backblaze-s3 \\
  /mnt/pbs-s3-cache \\
  --backend type=s3,client=backblaze-b2,bucket=<B2_BUCKET_NAME>
\`\`\`

### Phase 4: Migration Strategy

**Option A: Parallel Operation (Safer)**
1. Keep existing local PBS datastore + rclone sync
2. Add new S3 datastore alongside
3. Configure NEW backup jobs to use S3 datastore
4. Run both systems in parallel for 30 days
5. Verify S3 backups are reliable
6. Decommission rclone sync jobs
7. Archive old local backups

**Option B: Direct Migration (Riskier)**
1. Stop local backup jobs
2. Create S3 datastore
3. Migrate existing backups to S3 (if possible)
4. Point all jobs to S3 datastore
5. Remove rclone sync

**Recommendation**: Use **Option A** for safety

### Phase 5: Backup Job Updates

Update all PBS backup jobs to target new S3 datastore:
- 12 LXC containers (daily: 304, 501, 502; weekly: 101, 200, 201, 202, 401, 402, 500)
- Keep pre-backup hooks unchanged (database dumps still needed)

### Phase 6: Cost Monitoring

- [ ] Set up Backblaze B2 cost alerts
- [ ] Monitor API request counts
- [ ] Monitor egress bandwidth (if applicable)
- [ ] Compare monthly costs: before (storage + download) vs after (storage + API calls)

### Phase 7: Decommission rclone

After 30 days of verified S3 backups:
- [ ] Disable rclone cron jobs on Proxmox host
- [ ] Archive rclone config to 1Password (keep for recovery)
- [ ] Document S3 datastore configuration for DR
- [ ] Update disaster recovery runbook

## Technical Details

### PBS S3 Datastore Limitations

**From PBS Documentation:**
- Technology preview status (not production-ready)
- No datastore sharing between PBS instances
- HTTPS only (encrypted in transit)
- Requires persistent local filesystem cache (64-128 GB recommended)
- Storage failure handling: cleanup operations may fail if bucket runs out of space

### Cache Sizing Calculation

**Current Backup Set:**
- 12 LXC containers
- Daily backups: 3 containers × 7 days = 21 backups
- Weekly backups: 9 containers × 4 weeks = 36 backups
- Total: ~57 backup snapshots active at any time

**Estimated cache needs:**
- PBS docs recommend 64-128 GB
- Our backup set likely fits in 128 GB cache
- Monitor actual cache usage after deployment

### Cost Comparison

**Current (rclone sync):**
- B2 Storage: \$X/month
- B2 Download: \$Y/month (for disaster recovery only)
- No API charges (bulk sync)

**Future (PBS S3 native):**
- B2 Storage: \$X/month (same)
- B2 API Requests: Class B (write/delete), Class C (read/list)
- B2 Download: Minimal (only cache misses)

**Action**: Calculate expected API request volume before migration

## Testing Checklist

### Pre-Migration Tests (on test bucket)
- [ ] Create test S3 endpoint
- [ ] Create test datastore with S3 backend
- [ ] Run manual backup to S3
- [ ] Verify backup appears in B2 bucket
- [ ] Test restore from S3 backup
- [ ] Simulate network failure during backup
- [ ] Test cache behavior (eviction, refill)

### Post-Migration Tests
- [ ] Verify all 12 containers backup successfully to S3
- [ ] Test restore from S3 datastore
- [ ] Verify pre-backup hooks still execute
- [ ] Check PBS logs for S3 errors
- [ ] Monitor Backblaze B2 dashboard for costs

## Rollback Plan

If S3 datastore proves unreliable:
1. Re-enable local PBS datastore
2. Re-enable rclone sync jobs
3. Keep S3 datastore as secondary/archive
4. Document issues encountered

## Documentation Updates

After successful migration:
- [ ] Update \`docs/backups.md\` - replace rclone references
- [ ] Update \`docs/disaster-recovery.md\` - update recovery procedures
- [ ] Update \`tasks/cloud.yml\` - remove rclone task definitions
- [ ] Document PBS S3 endpoint configuration in runbook
- [ ] Add S3 datastore to PBS monitoring alerts

## References

### PBS S3 Documentation
- PBS Storage S3 Backend: https://pbs.homelab.rambtech.dev/docs/storage.html#datastore-s3-backend
- PBS S3 Endpoint Config: https://pbs.proxmox.com/docs/storage.html#datastore-s3-backend

### Backblaze B2 S3 API
- B2 S3 Compatible API: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/docs/s3_compatible_api.html
- B2 S3 Endpoint Regions: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/docs/s3_compatible_api.html#regions
- B2 Pricing: https://www.backblaze.com/b2/cloud-storage-pricing.html

### Current Implementation
- Backup strategy: \`docs/backups.md\`
- Disaster recovery: \`docs/disaster-recovery.md\`
- Cloud sync scripts: \`scripts/backup/cloud-sync.sh\`
- rclone config: 1Password vault \"homelab\"

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| S3 feature instability | High | Use parallel operation (Option A) |
| API cost overrun | Medium | Monitor costs, set alerts |
| Backup failures | High | Keep local backups during transition |
| Cache exhaustion | Medium | Provision 128 GB cache, monitor usage |
| B2 API rate limits | Low | PBS should handle retries |

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 12 containers backup successfully to S3 datastore
- [ ] Restore operations work from S3
- [ ] Monthly B2 costs are acceptable (document threshold)
- [ ] No backup failures for 30 consecutive days
- [ ] Cache performance is adequate (no slowdowns)
- [ ] PBS UI shows healthy S3 datastore status"

### 1. Identify Scope
- [ ] List all LXCs and check Alloy container status
  \`\`\`bash
  # On each LXC
  docker ps -a | grep alloy
  docker logs alloy-<container-name>
  \`\`\`

- [ ] Identify which LXCs are affected
- [ ] Check if monitoring LXC (500) Alloy is also affected

### 2. Check Common Failure Modes

#### Configuration Issues
- [ ] Review Alloy config template: \`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/configure-alloy-playbook.yml.tftpl\`
- [ ] Check for recent changes to Alloy configuration
- [ ] Verify Loki/Prometheus endpoints are reachable

#### Network Issues
- [ ] Test connectivity to Loki: \`http://10.100.5.100:3100\`
- [ ] Test connectivity to Prometheus: \`http://10.100.5.100:9090\`
- [ ] Check Traefik auth endpoints (loki-push, prometheus-push)

#### Docker Issues
- [ ] Check Docker socket permissions
- [ ] Verify Alloy image version consistency
- [ ] Check for OOM kills: \`dmesg | grep -i oom\`

#### Resource Constraints
- [ ] Check memory usage on affected LXCs
- [ ] Verify Alloy memory limits (currently 128m)
- [ ] Check disk space on LXCs

### 3. Review Logs

Collect logs from affected containers:
\`\`\`bash
# For each failing LXC
ssh root@10.100.X.XXX
docker logs alloy-<name> --tail 100
journalctl -u docker -n 100
\`\`\`

Common error patterns to look for:
- Authentication failures (Traefik basic auth)
- Connection refused (Loki/Prometheus down)
- Configuration syntax errors
- Permission denied (Docker socket)

### 4. Check Recent Changes

- [ ] Review recent commits to lxc-sidecars module
- [ ] Check if monitoring stack was restarted
- [ ] Verify Loki/Prometheus are healthy
- [ ] Check if Traefik routes changed

## Quick Verification

### Check Monitoring Stack Health
\`\`\`bash
ssh root@10.100.5.100
docker ps | grep -E 'loki|prometheus|alloy'
docker logs loki --tail 50
docker logs prometheus --tail 50
\`\`\`

### Check Traefik Auth Endpoints
\`\`\`bash
# Test from an LXC that should have access
curl -u alloy:<password> https://loki-push.homelab.rambtech.dev/loki/api/v1/push
curl -u alloy:<password> https://prometheus-push.homelab.rambtech.dev/api/v1/write
\`\`\`

## Potential Root Causes

1. **Authentication change**: Alloy basic auth credentials rotated/changed
2. **Monitoring stack restart**: Loki/Prometheus IP changed or restarted
3. **Traefik configuration**: Routes changed or middleware broken
4. **Config deployment**: Recent Ansible/OpenTofu run broke configs
5. **Resource exhaustion**: LXCs running out of memory
6. **Docker issue**: Docker daemon problems on multiple LXCs

## Immediate Mitigation

If urgent:
1. Identify one working LXC (if any)
2. Compare working vs failing configurations
3. Manual restart of Alloy containers: \`docker restart alloy-<name>\`
4. Check if restart resolves issue

## Files to Review
- \`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/main.tf\` - Alloy deployment logic
- \`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/configure-alloy-playbook.yml.tftpl\` - Alloy config template
- \`tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/docker-compose.yml\` - Loki/Prometheus/Alloy (monitoring LXC)
- \`tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/alloy-auth.yml.tpl\` - Traefik auth middleware

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All Alloy sidecars running and healthy
- [ ] Logs flowing to Loki
- [ ] Metrics flowing to Prometheus
- [ ] No error logs in Alloy containers
- [ ] Grafana showing recent data from all LXCs

## Follow-up Actions
After fix:
- Document root cause
- Add monitoring/alerting for Alloy sidecar health
- Consider adding health checks to Alloy containers
- Update runbooks with troubleshooting steps"

bd create \
  --title="Expose Ollama API via Traefik with authentication" \
  --type=task \
  --priority=1 \
  --body="## Overview
Expose Ollama API publicly via Traefik with proper authentication to enable AI integrations from external services (Pulse 5.0, other tools).

## Current State
- Ollama running on LXC 501 (OpenWebUI)
- Internal access only at \`http://10.100.5.101:11434\`
- OpenWebUI uses Ollama internally
- No external/authenticated API access

## Requirements

### Security
- **MUST**: Authentication layer (basic auth or API key)
- **MUST**: HTTPS only (via Traefik)
- **SHOULD**: Rate limiting to prevent abuse
- **SHOULD**: Logging/monitoring of API usage

### Access Control Options

**Option 1: Basic Auth (Simplest)**
- Traefik basicauth middleware
- Single shared credential for all AI integrations
- Easy to implement with existing patterns

**Option 2: API Key Headers**
- Custom header-based auth (\`X-API-Key\`)
- Traefik forwardauth middleware
- More flexible, per-service keys

**Option 3: OAuth2/OIDC via Authelia**
- Most secure, SSO integration
- Complex setup
- Overkill for API access

**Recommendation**: Start with **Option 1** (Basic Auth)

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Traefik Route Configuration

Create new Traefik route: \`ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev\`

**File**: \`tofu/apps/openwebui/traefik-routes.tf\` (new file)

\`\`\`hcl
module \"ollama_route\" {
  source = \"../../modules/traefik-route\"

  service_name = \"ollama\"
  host         = \"ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev\"
  target_ip    = \"10.100.5.101\"
  target_port  = 11434
  
  middlewares = [
    \"ollama-auth@file\",
    \"rate-limit@file\"  # Optional
  ]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}
\`\`\`

### Phase 2: Authentication Middleware

**File**: \`tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/ollama-auth.yml\` (new)

\`\`\`yaml
http:
  middlewares:
    ollama-auth:
      basicAuth:
        users:
          # Username: ollama-api
          # Password: Generated via htpasswd, stored in 1Password
          - \"ollama-api:\$apr1\$...\"  # htpasswd hash
        realm: \"Ollama API\"
\`\`\`

**Credential Storage**: 1Password vault \"homelab\" > \"Ollama API\" item

### Phase 3: Rate Limiting (Optional but Recommended)

**File**: \`tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/common.yml\` (add to existing)

\`\`\`yaml
http:
  middlewares:
    rate-limit:
      rateLimit:
        average: 100  # requests per second
        burst: 50
        period: 1m
\`\`\`

### Phase 4: Testing

Test external API access:
\`\`\`bash
# Test authentication
curl -u ollama-api:<password> https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev/api/tags

# Test model generation
curl -u ollama-api:<password> https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev/api/generate \\
  -d '{
    \"model\": \"llama3.2:3b\",
    \"prompt\": \"Why is the sky blue?\"
  }'

# Test without auth (should fail)
curl https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev/api/tags
\`\`\`

## Configuration Reference

### Ollama API Endpoints
- \`GET /api/tags\` - List models
- \`POST /api/generate\` - Generate completion
- \`POST /api/chat\` - Chat completion
- \`POST /api/embeddings\` - Generate embeddings
- \`POST /api/pull\` - Pull model (should be disabled publicly)
- \`POST /api/push\` - Push model (should be disabled publicly)

### Endpoint Access Control

Consider restricting dangerous endpoints:
\`\`\`yaml
# In Traefik route config
http:
  routers:
    ollama:
      rule: \"Host(\`ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev\`) && !PathPrefix(\`/api/pull\`, \`/api/push\`)\"
\`\`\`

## Security Considerations

### Risks
- **Model abuse**: External users could consume GPU resources
- **Cost**: Large model inference can be expensive (GPU time)
- **Data leakage**: Prompts might contain sensitive info (logged)

### Mitigations
- Strong authentication (rotate credentials regularly)
- Rate limiting (prevent abuse)
- Monitor GPU usage on LXC 501
- Set up Prometheus alerts for high Ollama usage
- Consider IP whitelisting if only specific services need access

## Monitoring

Add Prometheus metrics for Ollama API:
- Request count by endpoint
- Authentication failures
- Response times
- GPU utilization correlation

Alert on:
- Authentication failure spikes
- Unusual request patterns
- GPU exhaustion

## Documentation Updates

After implementation:
- [ ] Document Ollama API access in runbook
- [ ] Add credentials to 1Password with usage notes
- [ ] Update service map with new route
- [ ] Document rate limits and usage expectations

## Testing Checklist
- [ ] Traefik route resolves correctly
- [ ] HTTPS certificate valid
- [ ] Basic auth required and working
- [ ] Unauthorized requests rejected (401)
- [ ] Rate limiting triggers correctly
- [ ] Ollama API responses as expected
- [ ] GPU utilization monitored in Grafana

## Dependencies
None - can be implemented independently

## Follow-up Tasks
After this is complete:
- Pulse 5.0 upgrade can use authenticated Ollama endpoint
- Other AI integrations can be added
- Consider adding more granular access controls if needed

## References
- Ollama API docs: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md
- Traefik basicauth: https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/middlewares/http/basicauth/
- Traefik rate limit: https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/middlewares/http/ratelimit/"

bd create \
  --title="Upgrade Pulse to 5.0 with Ollama AI monitoring integration" \
  --type=feature \
  --priority=1 \
  --body="## Overview
Upgrade Pulse from current version to 5.0 to enable AI-powered monitoring capabilities using Ollama integration.

## Current State
- Pulse agents deployed on all LXCs via \`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars\`
- Pulse server version: TBD (check current deployment)
- Manual monitoring and alerting
- No AI-assisted diagnostics

## Pulse 5.0 New Features

### AI Assistant Capabilities
**Powered by Ollama (local AI)**:
- **Natural Language Queries**: Ask questions about infrastructure in plain English
- **Patrol Service**: Automated health checks with configurable schedules
- **Auto-Fix Capability**: AI can diagnose and remediate issues (opt-in)
- **Predictive Intelligence**: Failure pattern detection and anomaly identification
- **Multi-Resource Correlation**: Detect cascading issues across infrastructure
- **Baseline Learning**: Learns normal behavior to identify deviations
- **Cost Tracking**: Monitor AI API usage with budget controls

### Additional Features
- Native Kubernetes cluster monitoring (not needed for our setup)
- Improved AI settings UX
- Ollama model configuration improvements
- Better provider configuration flow

## Prerequisites

### Completed First
- **MUST**: \`proxmox-homelab-tkw\` - Expose Ollama API via Traefik with auth
  - Ollama must be accessible at \`https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev\`
  - Basic auth configured
  - Rate limiting in place

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Pre-Upgrade Preparation

#### 1.1 Document Current State
- [ ] Check current Pulse version on all agents
- [ ] Document current Pulse server version
- [ ] Export current Pulse configuration/settings
- [ ] Verify all Pulse agents are healthy
- [ ] Backup Pulse database/configuration

#### 1.2 Test Ollama Integration
- [ ] Verify Ollama API accessible via Traefik
- [ ] Test model availability (\`llama3.2:3b\` or similar)
- [ ] Confirm authentication works
- [ ] Test basic generation request

### Phase 2: Pulse Server Upgrade

#### 2.1 Update Docker Image
**File**: \`tofu/apps/container-mgmt/deploy/docker-compose.yml\` (or wherever Pulse server is)

Update Pulse server to v5.0:
\`\`\`yaml
pulse-server:
  image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:5.0  # Update from current version
\`\`\`

#### 2.2 Configure Ollama Integration
Add Ollama configuration to Pulse:
- Provider: Ollama
- Endpoint: \`https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev\`
- Auth: Basic Auth (username: \`ollama-api\`, password from 1Password)
- Default model: \`llama3.2:3b\` (or best available model)

### Phase 3: Agent Upgrades

#### 3.1 Update Agent Version
**File**: \`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/variables.tf\` or \`main.tf\`

Update Pulse agent image version:
\`\`\`hcl
pulse_agent = {
  enabled = true
  version = \"5.0\"  # Update from current version
}
\`\`\`

#### 3.2 Rolling Deployment
Apply agent upgrades via OpenTofu:
\`\`\`bash
# Update one LXC at a time to test
task tofu:plan APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# If successful, roll out to all
task tofu:plan-all
task tofu:apply-all
\`\`\`

### Phase 4: AI Feature Configuration

#### 4.1 Enable AI Features
In Pulse UI/config:
- [ ] Enable AI assistant
- [ ] Configure Ollama provider settings
- [ ] Set patrol service schedule
- [ ] Configure baseline learning period
- [ ] Set up cost tracking alerts

#### 4.2 AI Settings
- **Auto-Fix**: Disabled initially (enable after testing)
- **Patrol Schedule**: Every 6 hours (adjust based on needs)
- **Baseline Period**: 7 days (let it learn normal patterns)
- **Budget Alerts**: Set conservative thresholds

### Phase 5: Testing & Validation

#### 5.1 Test AI Queries
Test natural language monitoring:
- \"Which containers are using the most memory?\"
- \"Are there any unhealthy services?\"
- \"Show me network traffic anomalies\"
- \"What failed recently?\"

#### 5.2 Test Patrol Service
- [ ] Verify patrol runs on schedule
- [ ] Check patrol findings/reports
- [ ] Review AI-generated insights

#### 5.3 Test Correlation
- [ ] Trigger a cascading failure scenario
- [ ] Verify AI detects correlation
- [ ] Check root cause analysis accuracy

### Phase 6: Monitoring & Optimization

#### 6.1 Monitor Ollama Usage
- [ ] GPU utilization on LXC 501 (Ollama host)
- [ ] Ollama API request counts
- [ ] Response times
- [ ] Model inference times

#### 6.2 Cost Tracking
- [ ] Monitor AI API call volume
- [ ] Track GPU hours used
- [ ] Set up budget alerts in Pulse
- [ ] Optimize query frequency if needed

## Configuration Details

### Ollama Endpoint Configuration
\`\`\`yaml
# In Pulse AI settings
provider: ollama
endpoint: https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev
auth:
  type: basic
  username: ollama-api
  password: <from-1password>
model: llama3.2:3b
timeout: 30s
\`\`\`

### Recommended Models
Based on GPU capacity (LXC 501 has GPU passthrough):
- **llama3.2:3b** - Fastest, good for quick queries
- **llama3.2:7b** - Better accuracy, slower
- **qwen2.5:7b** - Alternative, strong reasoning

Test different models and choose based on:
- Response time
- Accuracy of insights
- GPU memory usage

## Rollback Plan

If 5.0 causes issues:
1. Revert Pulse server image to previous version
2. Revert agent images via OpenTofu
3. Document issues encountered
4. Wait for bug fixes or next release

## Breaking Changes

Check release notes for:
- [ ] Configuration format changes
- [ ] API compatibility with agents
- [ ] Database migrations
- [ ] Feature deprecations

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Pulse server 5.0 running and healthy
- [ ] All agents upgraded to 5.0
- [ ] AI assistant responding to queries
- [ ] Ollama integration working
- [ ] Patrol service running on schedule
- [ ] No degradation in existing monitoring
- [ ] AI insights providing value

## Documentation Updates

After successful upgrade:
- [ ] Document AI features and usage
- [ ] Add AI query examples to runbook
- [ ] Document Ollama endpoint configuration
- [ ] Update Pulse troubleshooting guide
- [ ] Add AI-specific monitoring/alerts

## References

### Pulse 5.0 Documentation
- Release notes: https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse/releases
- Pulse GitHub: https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse
- Pulse README: https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse/blob/main/README.md

### Ollama Integration
- Ollama API: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md
- Model library: https://ollama.com/library

### Current Implementation
- Pulse agents: \`tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars\`
- Pulse configuration: TBD (locate current config)

## Dependencies

**Blocks**:
- \`proxmox-homelab-tkw\` - Expose Ollama API via Traefik

**Related**:
- \`proxmox-homelab-m63\` - Fix Alloy failures (should be resolved first for clean monitoring)

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Upgrade breaks existing monitoring | High | Test on one LXC first, keep rollback ready |
| Ollama API overload | Medium | Rate limiting, monitor GPU usage |
| AI false positives/negatives | Medium | Start with patrol disabled, validate insights |
| Version incompatibility (server/agents) | High | Upgrade server first, test before agent rollout |

## Expected Benefits

- **Faster incident response**: AI correlates issues automatically
- **Predictive maintenance**: Catch problems before they become critical
- **Reduced manual work**: Patrol service automates routine checks
- **Better insights**: Natural language queries simplify troubleshooting
- **Learning system**: Baseline detection improves over time"

      retries: 3

  # ==========================================================================

    restart: unless-stopped

  # ntfy - Push notifications

    container_name: ntfy

      - ./ntfy/templates:/etc/ntfy/templates:ro

    environment:

    deploy:

          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'

      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}

    environment:

    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.15.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ./ntfy/templates:/etc/ntfy/templates:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  loki_data:
  alloy_data:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:

      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP receiver (backwards compat)
      - "12345:12345" # Alloy UI
    volumes:
      - ./alloy/config.alloy:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - /var/log:/var/log/host:ro
      - alloy_data:/var/lib/alloy/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
      - loki
    # Healthcheck removed: Alloy is a minimal container without curl/wget
    # Monitor via Prometheus metrics at :12345/metrics instead

  # ==========================================================================
  # Prometheus - Metrics storage and alerting
  # ==========================================================================
  prometheus:
    image: prom/prometheus:v3.8.1
    container_name: prometheus
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml'
      - '--storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus'
      - '--storage.tsdb.retention.time=30d'
      - '--web.enable-lifecycle'
      - '--web.enable-remote-write-receiver'
      - '--web.external-url=https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9090:9090"
    volumes:
      - ./prometheus/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro
      - ./prometheus/alerts:/etc/prometheus/alerts:ro
      - prometheus_data:/prometheus
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 4096m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9090/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Alertmanager - Alert routing and notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  alertmanager:
    image: prom/alertmanager:v0.30.0
    container_name: alertmanager
    command:
      - '--config.file=/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml'
      - '--storage.path=/alertmanager'
      - '--web.external-url=https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev'
    ports:
      - "9093:9093"
    volumes:
      - ./alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:/etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml:ro
      - ./alertmanager/templates:/etc/alertmanager/templates:ro
      - alertmanager_data:/alertmanager
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:9093/-/healthy || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Grafana - Visualization and dashboards
  # ==========================================================================
  grafana:
    image: grafana/grafana:12.3.1
    container_name: grafana
    environment:
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - GF_SECURITY_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${GRAFANA_ADMIN_PASSWORD:-admin}
      - GF_USERS_ALLOW_SIGN_UP=false
      - GF_SERVER_ROOT_URL=https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=false
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    volumes:
      - ./grafana/provisioning:/etc/grafana/provisioning:ro
      - ./grafana/dashboards:/var/lib/grafana/dashboards:ro
      - grafana_data:/var/lib/grafana
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 2048m
          cpus: '2.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      - prometheus
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:3000/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Uptime Kuma - HTTP endpoint monitoring and status page
  # ==========================================================================
  uptime-kuma:
    image: louislam/uptime-kuma:1
    container_name: uptime-kuma
    ports:
      - "3001:3001"
    volumes:
      - uptime_kuma_data:/app/data
    dns:
      - 192.168.1.196  # AdGuard DNS for local domain resolution
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 1024m
          cpus: '1.0'
        reservations:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3001/ > /dev/null || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

  # ==========================================================================
  # AutoKuma - Declarative monitor management for Uptime Kuma
  # Monitors defined in ./autokuma/monitors.json
  # ==========================================================================
  autokuma:
    image: ghcr.io/bigboot/autokuma:1.0.0
    container_name: autokuma
    environment:
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__URL=http://uptime-kuma:3001
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__USERNAME=${UPTIME_KUMA_USERNAME:-admin}
      - AUTOKUMA__KUMA__PASSWORD=${UPTIME_KUMA_PASSWORD}
      - AUTOKUMA__STATIC_MONITORS=/monitors/monitors.json
      - AUTOKUMA__DOCKER__ENABLED=false
    volumes:
      - ./autokuma/monitors.json:/monitors/monitors.json:ro
    depends_on:
      - uptime-kuma
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    # Healthcheck removed: AutoKuma is distroless Rust binary with no health endpoint
    # Container health monitored via Docker restart policy
    restart: unless-stopped

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy - Push notifications
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy:
    image: binwiederhier/ntfy:v2.15.0
    container_name: ntfy
    command:
      - serve
      - --cache-file=/var/cache/ntfy/cache.db
      - --attachment-cache-dir=/var/cache/ntfy/attachments
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    volumes:
      - ./ntfy/server.yml:/etc/ntfy/server.yml:ro
      - ./ntfy/templates:/etc/ntfy/templates:ro
      - ntfy_cache:/var/cache/ntfy
      - ntfy_data:/var/lib/ntfy
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:80/v1/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # ntfy-discord-forwarder - Forward ntfy notifications to Discord
  # ==========================================================================
  ntfy-discord-forwarder:
    image: python:3.12-alpine
    container_name: ntfy-discord-forwarder
    command:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        pip install --no-cache-dir requests &&
        python3 -u << 'ENDSCRIPT'
        import requests
        import json
        import os

        NTFY_URL = "http://ntfy:80/homelab-alerts/json"
        DISCORD_WEBHOOK = os.environ["DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL"]

        print(f"Starting ntfy->Discord forwarder. Listening to {NTFY_URL}")
        for line in requests.get(NTFY_URL, stream=True).iter_lines():
            if line:
                data = json.loads(line)
                msg = data.get("message", "")
                if msg:
                    print(f"Forwarding: {msg}")
                    requests.post(DISCORD_WEBHOOK, json={"content": msg})
        ENDSCRIPT
    environment:
      - DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL=${DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL}
    depends_on:
      - ntfy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
        reservations:
          memory: 128m
          cpus: '0.25'
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep -f python3 || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  loki_data:
  alloy_data:
  prometheus_data:
  alertmanager_data:
  grafana_data:
  uptime_kuma_data:
  ntfy_cache:
  ntfy_data:

     2→# =============================================================================
     3→# Configure Container Management Agents in LXC Container
     4→# =============================================================================
     5→# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
     6→# It deploys all enabled agents in a single docker-compose file to avoid
     7→# conflicts from separate compose projects removing each other's containers.

     9→# Agents:
    10→#   - Pulse Docker Agent: Container monitoring (pushes metrics to Pulse server)
    11→#   - Arcane Agent: Remote container management (manager initiates pairing)
    12→#   - Alloy Agent: Grafana Alloy for log collection to Loki
    13→# =============================================================================
    14→
    15→- name: Configure container agents for ${container_name}
    16→  hosts: ${container_name}
    17→  gather_facts: true
    18→
    19→  vars:
    20→    container_id: "${container_id}"
    21→    container_name: "${container_name}"
    22→
    23→    # Pulse agent config

    25→    pulse_url: "${pulse_url}"

    40→    # Shared paths
    41→    sidecars_dir: /config/sidecars
    42→    compose_file: /config/sidecars/docker-compose.yml

    44→  tasks:
    45→    # =========================================================================

    53→
    54→    # =========================================================================
    55→    # Deploy Unified Docker Compose
    56→    # =========================================================================
    57→    # Single compose file with all enabled agents to prevent --remove-orphans
    58→    # from removing the "other" agent when updating just one.
    59→
    60→    - name: Deploy unified agents docker-compose

    63→          # =============================================================================

    65→          # =============================================================================

    68→          # =============================================================================

    71→%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
    72→            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    73→            # Pulse Docker Agent - Container Monitoring
    74→            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    75→            # NOTE: pulse-docker-agent is deprecated. Pulse v5.0+ introduces a unified
    76→            # agent (binary install). Until v5.0 is stable, continue using this image.
    77→            pulse-agent:
    78→              image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
    79→              container_name: pulse-agent
    80→              pid: host
    81→              uts: host
    82→              environment:
    83→                - PULSE_URL=${pulse_url}
    84→                - PULSE_TOKEN=${pulse_token}
    85→              volumes:
    86→                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    87→              deploy:

    90→                    memory: 128m

    92→                  reservations:
    93→                    memory: 64m
    94→                    cpus: '0.1'

    97→                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep pulse-docker-agent || exit 1"]
    98→                interval: 30s
    99→                timeout: 10s
   100→                retries: 3

   103→%{ endif ~}

   174→    - name: Deploy Alloy River configuration
   175→      ansible.builtin.copy:
   176→        content: |
   177→          // =============================================================================
   178→          // Grafana Alloy Configuration - ${container_name} (LXC ${container_id})
   179→          // =============================================================================
   180→          // Generated by OpenTofu lxc-sidecars module
   181→          // DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY - changes will be overwritten
   182→          // Config version: 2 (auth + metrics)
   183→          // =============================================================================
   184→
   185→          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   186→          // Docker Log Discovery
   187→          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   188→          discovery.docker "containers" {
   189→            host = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
   190→          }
   191→
   192→          discovery.relabel "docker_logs" {
   193→            targets = discovery.docker.containers.targets
   194→
   195→            // Keep container name as label
   196→            rule {
   197→              source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_name"]
   198→              regex         = "/(.*)"
   199→              target_label  = "container"
   200→            }
   201→
   202→            // Add compose service name if available
   203→            rule {
   204→              source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_com_docker_compose_service"]
   205→              target_label  = "service"
   206→            }
   207→
   208→            // Add LXC identifier
   209→            rule {
   210→              target_label = "lxc"
   211→              replacement  = "${container_name}"
   212→            }
   213→
   214→            rule {
   215→              target_label = "lxc_id"
   216→              replacement  = "${container_id}"
   217→            }
   218→          }
   219→
   220→          loki.source.docker "containers" {
   221→            host       = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
   222→            targets    = discovery.relabel.docker_logs.output
   223→            forward_to = [loki.write.default.receiver]
   224→          }
   225→
   226→          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   227→          // Journal Logs (systemd)
   228→          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   229→          loki.source.journal "systemd" {
   230→            forward_to = [loki.process.journal.receiver]
   231→            labels = {

   304→    - name: Restart Alloy if config changed

   312→    # =========================================================================
   313→    # Pull Latest Images

   315→%{ if pulse_enabled ~}

   372→      register: alloy_status

   374→%{ endif ~}
   375→
   376→    - name: Display deployment summary
   377→      ansible.builtin.debug:
   378→        msg:
   379→          - "=== Container Agents Deployed for ${container_name} ==="
   380→          - ""
   381→          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
   382→%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
   383→          - "Pulse Agent: {{ pulse_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"

   390→%{ endif ~}

   401→          - "  Restart:    docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} restart"

---
# =============================================================================
# Configure Container Management Agents in LXC Container
# =============================================================================
# This playbook is generated by the lxc-sidecars OpenTofu module.
# It deploys all enabled agents in a single docker-compose file to avoid
# conflicts from separate compose projects removing each other's containers.
#
# Agents:
#   - Pulse Docker Agent: Container monitoring (pushes metrics to Pulse server)
#   - Arcane Agent: Remote container management (manager initiates pairing)
#   - Alloy Agent: Grafana Alloy for log collection to Loki
# =============================================================================

- name: Configure container agents for ${container_name}
  hosts: ${container_name}
  gather_facts: true

  vars:
    container_id: "${container_id}"
    container_name: "${container_name}"

    # Pulse agent config
    pulse_enabled: ${pulse_enabled}
    pulse_url: "${pulse_url}"
    pulse_token: "${pulse_token}"

    # Arcane agent config
    arcane_enabled: ${arcane_enabled}
    manager_url: "${manager_url}"
    bootstrap_token: "${bootstrap_token}"

    # Alloy agent config
    alloy_enabled: ${alloy_enabled}
    loki_url: "${loki_url}"
    prometheus_url: "${prometheus_url}"
    alloy_username: "${alloy_username}"
    alloy_password: "${alloy_password}"

    # Shared paths
    sidecars_dir: /config/sidecars
    compose_file: /config/sidecars/docker-compose.yml

  tasks:
    # =========================================================================
    # Create Sidecar Directory
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Create sidecars directory
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: "{{ sidecars_dir }}"
        state: directory
        mode: '0755'

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Unified Docker Compose
    # =========================================================================
    # Single compose file with all enabled agents to prevent --remove-orphans
    # from removing the "other" agent when updating just one.

    - name: Deploy unified agents docker-compose
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          # =============================================================================
          # Container Management Agents - ${container_name}
          # =============================================================================
          # Generated by OpenTofu lxc-sidecars module
          # DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY - changes will be overwritten
          # =============================================================================

          services:
%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            # Pulse Docker Agent - Container Monitoring
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            # NOTE: pulse-docker-agent is deprecated. Pulse v5.0+ introduces a unified
            # agent (binary install). Until v5.0 is stable, continue using this image.
            pulse-agent:
              image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
              container_name: pulse-agent
              pid: host
              uts: host
              environment:
                - PULSE_URL=${pulse_url}
                - PULSE_TOKEN=${pulse_token}
              volumes:
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.25'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 64m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
              healthcheck:
                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pgrep pulse-docker-agent || exit 1"]
                interval: 30s
                timeout: 10s
                retries: 3
                start_period: 30s

%{ endif ~}
%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            # Arcane Agent - Remote Container Management
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            arcane-agent:
              image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest
              container_name: arcane-agent
              ports:
                - "3553:3553"
              environment:
                - AGENT_MODE=true
                - AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN=${bootstrap_token}
              volumes:
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
                - arcane_agent_data:/app/data
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 256m
                    cpus: '0.5'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
              healthcheck:
                test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3553/api/health || exit 1"]
                interval: 30s
                timeout: 10s
                retries: 3
                start_period: 30s

%{ endif ~}
%{ if alloy_enabled ~}
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            # Alloy Agent - Log Collection to Loki
            # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
            alloy:
              image: grafana/alloy:v1.5.1
              container_name: alloy
              command:
                - run
                - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
                - --disable-reporting=true
                - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
              volumes:
                - /config/sidecars/alloy.river:/etc/alloy/config.alloy:ro
                - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
                - /var/log:/var/log/host:ro
              deploy:
                resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: 128m
                    cpus: '0.25'
                  reservations:
                    memory: 64m
                    cpus: '0.1'
              restart: unless-stopped
%{ endif ~}
%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
          volumes:
            arcane_agent_data:
%{ endif ~}
        dest: "{{ compose_file }}"
        mode: '0644'
      register: compose_file_result

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Alloy Configuration
    # =========================================================================
%{ if alloy_enabled ~}
    - name: Deploy Alloy River configuration
      ansible.builtin.copy:
        content: |
          // =============================================================================
          // Grafana Alloy Configuration - ${container_name} (LXC ${container_id})
          // =============================================================================
          // Generated by OpenTofu lxc-sidecars module
          // DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY - changes will be overwritten
          // Config version: 2 (auth + metrics)
          // =============================================================================

          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          // Docker Log Discovery
          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          discovery.docker "containers" {
            host = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
          }

          discovery.relabel "docker_logs" {
            targets = discovery.docker.containers.targets

            // Keep container name as label
            rule {
              source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_name"]
              regex         = "/(.*)"
              target_label  = "container"
            }

            // Add compose service name if available
            rule {
              source_labels = ["__meta_docker_container_label_com_docker_compose_service"]
              target_label  = "service"
            }

            // Add LXC identifier
            rule {
              target_label = "lxc"
              replacement  = "${container_name}"
            }

            rule {
              target_label = "lxc_id"
              replacement  = "${container_id}"
            }
          }

          loki.source.docker "containers" {
            host       = "unix:///var/run/docker.sock"
            targets    = discovery.relabel.docker_logs.output
            forward_to = [loki.write.default.receiver]
          }

          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          // Journal Logs (systemd)
          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          loki.source.journal "systemd" {
            forward_to = [loki.process.journal.receiver]
            labels = {
              job    = "journal",
              lxc    = "${container_name}",
              lxc_id = "${container_id}",
            }
          }

          loki.process "journal" {
            forward_to = [loki.write.default.receiver]

            stage.static_labels {
              values = {
                source = "journal",
              }
            }
          }

          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          // Loki Write Endpoint (with Basic Auth)
          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          loki.write "default" {
            endpoint {
              url = "${loki_url}/loki/api/v1/push"

              basic_auth {
                username = "${alloy_username}"
                password = "${alloy_password}"
              }
            }
          }

          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          // Prometheus Remote Write (with Basic Auth)
          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          // Collect host metrics and forward to Prometheus
          prometheus.exporter.unix "node" {
            disable_collectors = ["arp", "bonding", "btrfs", "infiniband", "ipvs", "mdadm", "nfs", "nfsd", "nvme", "rapl", "tapestats", "zfs"]
          }

          prometheus.scrape "node" {
            targets    = prometheus.exporter.unix.node.targets
            forward_to = [prometheus.relabel.add_labels.receiver]
            job_name   = "node"
          }

          prometheus.relabel "add_labels" {
            forward_to = [prometheus.remote_write.default.receiver]

            rule {
              target_label = "lxc"
              replacement  = "${container_name}"
            }

            rule {
              target_label = "lxc_id"
              replacement  = "${container_id}"
            }
          }

          prometheus.remote_write "default" {
            endpoint {
              url = "${prometheus_url}/api/v1/write"

              basic_auth {
                username = "${alloy_username}"
                password = "${alloy_password}"
              }
            }
          }
        dest: "{{ sidecars_dir }}/alloy.river"
        mode: '0644'
      register: alloy_config_result

    - name: Restart Alloy if config changed
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker restart alloy
      when: alloy_config_result.changed
      register: alloy_restart_result
      failed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

    # =========================================================================
    # Pull Latest Images
    # =========================================================================
%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
    - name: Pull Pulse agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
      changed_when: true
%{ endif ~}

%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
    - name: Pull Arcane agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest
      changed_when: true
%{ endif ~}

%{ if alloy_enabled ~}
    - name: Pull Alloy image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull grafana/alloy:v1.5.1
      changed_when: true
%{ endif ~}

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Agent Containers
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Deploy agent containers
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} up -d --remove-orphans
      register: deploy_result
      changed_when: "'Started' in deploy_result.stderr or 'Creating' in deploy_result.stderr"

    # =========================================================================
    # Verify Deployment
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Wait for agents to start
      ansible.builtin.pause:
        seconds: 10

%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
    - name: Check Pulse agent status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=pulse-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: pulse_status
      changed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
    - name: Check Arcane agent status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=arcane-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: arcane_status
      changed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

%{ if alloy_enabled ~}
    - name: Check Alloy agent status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=alloy --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: alloy_status
      changed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

    - name: Display deployment summary
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== Container Agents Deployed for ${container_name} ==="
          - ""
          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
          - "Pulse Agent: {{ pulse_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"
          - "  → Pulse URL: ${pulse_url}"
%{ endif ~}
%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
          - "Arcane Agent: {{ arcane_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"
          - "  → Agent Port: 3553"
          - "  → Pair in Arcane UI: http://{{ ansible_host }}:3553"
%{ endif ~}
%{ if alloy_enabled ~}
          - "Alloy Agent: {{ alloy_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"
          - "  → Loki URL: ${loki_url}"
          - "  → Alloy UI: http://{{ ansible_host }}:12345"
%{ endif ~}
          - ""
          - "Compose file: {{ compose_file }}"
          - ""
          - "Commands:"
          - "  View logs:  docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} logs -f"
          - "  Restart:    docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} restart"
          - "  Status:     docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} ps"

              url = "${loki_url}/loki/api/v1/push"

              basic_auth {
                username = "${alloy_username}"
                password = "${alloy_password}"
              }
            }
          }

          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          // Prometheus Remote Write (with Basic Auth)
          // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
          // Collect host metrics and forward to Prometheus
          prometheus.exporter.unix "node" {
            disable_collectors = ["arp", "bonding", "btrfs", "infiniband", "ipvs", "mdadm", "nfs", "nfsd", "nvme", "rapl", "tapestats", "zfs"]
          }

          prometheus.scrape "node" {
            targets    = prometheus.exporter.unix.node.targets
            forward_to = [prometheus.relabel.add_labels.receiver]
            job_name   = "node"
          }

          prometheus.relabel "add_labels" {
            forward_to = [prometheus.remote_write.default.receiver]

            rule {
              target_label = "lxc"
              replacement  = "${container_name}"
            }

            rule {
              target_label = "lxc_id"
              replacement  = "${container_id}"
            }
          }

          prometheus.remote_write "default" {
            endpoint {
              url = "${prometheus_url}/api/v1/write"

              basic_auth {
                username = "${alloy_username}"
                password = "${alloy_password}"
              }
            }
          }
        dest: "{{ sidecars_dir }}/alloy.river"
        mode: '0644'
      register: alloy_config_result

    - name: Restart Alloy if config changed
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker restart alloy
      when: alloy_config_result.changed
      register: alloy_restart_result
      failed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

    # =========================================================================
    # Pull Latest Images
    # =========================================================================
%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
    - name: Pull Pulse agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse-docker-agent:latest
      changed_when: true
%{ endif ~}

%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
    - name: Pull Arcane agent image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane-headless:latest
      changed_when: true
%{ endif ~}

%{ if alloy_enabled ~}
    - name: Pull Alloy image
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker pull grafana/alloy:v1.5.1
      changed_when: true
%{ endif ~}

    # =========================================================================
    # Deploy Agent Containers
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Deploy agent containers
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} up -d --remove-orphans
      register: deploy_result
      changed_when: "'Started' in deploy_result.stderr or 'Creating' in deploy_result.stderr"

    # =========================================================================
    # Verify Deployment
    # =========================================================================
    - name: Wait for agents to start
      ansible.builtin.pause:
        seconds: 10

%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
    - name: Check Pulse agent status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=pulse-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: pulse_status
      changed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
    - name: Check Arcane agent status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=arcane-agent --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: arcane_status
      changed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

%{ if alloy_enabled ~}
    - name: Check Alloy agent status
      ansible.builtin.command:
        cmd: docker ps --filter name=alloy --format "{{ '{{' }}.Status{{ '}}' }}"
      register: alloy_status
      changed_when: false
%{ endif ~}

    - name: Display deployment summary
      ansible.builtin.debug:
        msg:
          - "=== Container Agents Deployed for ${container_name} ==="
          - ""
          - "Container ID: ${container_id}"
%{ if pulse_enabled ~}
          - "Pulse Agent: {{ pulse_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"
          - "  → Pulse URL: ${pulse_url}"
%{ endif ~}
%{ if arcane_enabled ~}
          - "Arcane Agent: {{ arcane_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"
          - "  → Agent Port: 3553"
          - "  → Pair in Arcane UI: http://{{ ansible_host }}:3553"
%{ endif ~}
%{ if alloy_enabled ~}
          - "Alloy Agent: {{ alloy_status.stdout | default('not running') }}"
          - "  → Loki URL: ${loki_url}"
          - "  → Alloy UI: http://{{ ansible_host }}:12345"
%{ endif ~}
          - ""
          - "Compose file: {{ compose_file }}"
          - ""
          - "Commands:"
          - "  View logs:  docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} logs -f"
          - "  Restart:    docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} restart"
          - "  Status:     docker compose -f {{ compose_file }} ps"

Perfect! I've added the bash-based healthcheck to both:
1. The monitoring stack's Alloy container in [docker-compose.yml](tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/docker-compose.yml)
2. The Alloy sidecar template in [configure-agents-playbook.yml.tftpl](tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/templates/configure-agents-playbook.yml.tftpl)

This healthcheck uses bash's built-in `/dev/tcp` feature to:
- Open a TCP connection to localhost:12345 (file descriptor 42)
- Send an HTTP GET request to `/-/healthy`
- Check that the response starts with HTTP 200
- Close the connection

Note: I used `$$` in the template file to escape the `$` character properly for Terraform templating.

# =============================================================================
# Documents LXC - Paperless-ngx + Stirling-PDF
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 504
# IP: 10.100.5.104
#
# Document management stack:
# - Paperless-ngx: OCR, full-text search, auto-tagging, email consumption
# - Stirling-PDF: PDF manipulation (merge, split, compress, convert, etc.)
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1Password - Paperless Secrets
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data "onepassword_item" "paperless" {
  vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
  title = "paperless"
}

locals {
  # Flatten paperless section fields into a map by label
  _paperless_section_fields = merge([
    for s in try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.section, []) : {
      for f in try(s.field, []) : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)

  paperless = {
    admin_user     = try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.username, "admin")
    admin_password = try(data.onepassword_item.paperless.password, "")
    db_password    = lookup(local._paperless_section_fields, "db_password", "")
    secret_key     = lookup(local._paperless_section_fields, "secret_key", "")
  }
}

# Generate the .env file from 1Password secrets
resource "local_sensitive_file" "documents_env" {
  filename = "${path.module}/deploy/.env"
  content  = <<-EOT
# Documents Stack Environment
# Auto-generated by OpenTofu from 1Password
# DO NOT EDIT - changes will be overwritten

# Paperless-ngx
PAPERLESS_ADMIN_USER=${local.paperless.admin_user}
PAPERLESS_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${local.paperless.admin_password}
PAPERLESS_DB_PASSWORD=${local.paperless.db_password}
PAPERLESS_SECRET_KEY=${local.paperless.secret_key}
EOT

  file_permission = "0600"
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 504
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 4  # OCR is CPU intensive
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 8192  # OCR needs memory
}

variable "swap" {
  type    = number
  default = 2048
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64  # Documents can grow large
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Documents Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "documents" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "documents"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.documents}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = var.swap

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged container (security hardened)
  unprivileged = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # Ensure .env is generated before file sync
  depends_on = [local_sensitive_file.documents_env]

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "Documents"
  service_description = "Document management with Paperless-ngx (OCR) and Stirling-PDF (utilities)"

  service_urls = {
    paperless_internal    = "https://docs.${var.domain_internal}"
    paperless_public      = "https://docs.${var.domain_public}"
    stirling_pdf_internal = "https://pdf.${var.domain_internal}"
    stirling_pdf_public   = "https://pdf.${var.domain_public}"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "Paperless-ngx", port = 8000, info = "Document management with OCR" },
    { name = "Stirling-PDF", port = 8080, info = "PDF manipulation tools" },
    { name = "PostgreSQL", port = 5432, info = "Paperless database (internal)" },
    { name = "Redis", port = 6379, info = "Paperless cache (internal)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f paperless
cd /config && docker compose logs -f stirling-pdf
```

**Restart services:**
```
cd /config && docker compose restart paperless
cd /config && docker compose restart stirling-pdf
```

**Import documents:**
Place files in `/config/consume/` - they'll be automatically imported.

**Export all documents:**
```
cd /config && docker compose exec paperless document_exporter ../export/
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=documents` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["documents", "paperless", "pdf", "ocr"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "documents_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.documents.container_id
  container_ip   = module.documents.ip_address
  container_name = "documents"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-504"

    pre_backup_commands = [{
      name    = "PostgreSQL dump (Paperless)"
      command = "docker exec paperless-db pg_dump -U paperless -d paperless --clean --if-exists | gzip > /config/paperless-db-backup.sql.gz"
      timeout = 300
    }]

    include_paths = ["/config", "/var/lib/docker/volumes"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2"]

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,documents,paperless"
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.documents]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Routes - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Paperless-ngx route (internal only)
module "paperless_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "docs"
  backend_url = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8000"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "docs.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "docs.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Authelia protected
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.documents]
}

# Stirling-PDF route (internal only)
module "stirling_pdf_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "pdf"
  backend_url = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8080"

  # Internal route (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "pdf.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "pdf.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares - Authelia protected
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers", "authelia"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.documents]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.documents.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.documents.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.documents.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    direct_paperless      = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8000"
    paperless_internal    = module.paperless_route.internal_url
    paperless_public      = module.paperless_route.public_url

    direct_stirling_pdf   = "http://${module.documents.ip_address}:8080"
    stirling_pdf_internal = module.stirling_pdf_route.internal_url
    stirling_pdf_public   = module.stirling_pdf_route.public_url
  }
}

output "traefik_config_paths" {
  description = "Paths to Traefik configs on Traefik LXC"
  value = {
    paperless    = module.paperless_route.remote_config_path
    stirling_pdf = module.stirling_pdf_route.remote_config_path
  }
}
