proxmox-homelab-tkw: Expose Ollama API via Traefik with authentication
Status: open
Priority: P1
Type: task
Created: 2025-12-19 23:34
Updated: 2025-12-19 23:34

Description:
## Overview
Expose Ollama API publicly via Traefik with proper authentication to enable AI integrations from external services (Pulse 5.0, other tools).

## Current State
- Ollama running on LXC 501 (OpenWebUI)
- Internal access only at `http://10.100.5.101:11434`
- OpenWebUI uses Ollama internally
- No external/authenticated API access

## Requirements

### Security
- **MUST**: Authentication layer (basic auth or API key)
- **MUST**: HTTPS only (via Traefik)
- **SHOULD**: Rate limiting to prevent abuse
- **SHOULD**: Logging/monitoring of API usage

### Access Control Options

**Option 1: Basic Auth (Simplest)**
- Traefik basicauth middleware
- Single shared credential for all AI integrations
- Easy to implement with existing patterns

**Option 2: API Key Headers**
- Custom header-based auth (`X-API-Key`)
- Traefik forwardauth middleware
- More flexible, per-service keys

**Option 3: OAuth2/OIDC via Authelia**
- Most secure, SSO integration
- Complex setup
- Overkill for API access

**Recommendation**: Start with **Option 1** (Basic Auth)

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Traefik Route Configuration

Create new Traefik route: `ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev`

**File**: `tofu/apps/openwebui/traefik-routes.tf` (new file)

```hcl
module "ollama_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  service_name = "ollama"
  host         = "ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev"
  target_ip    = "10.100.5.101"
  target_port  = 11434
  
  middlewares = [
    "ollama-auth@file",
    "rate-limit@file"  # Optional
  ]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}
```

### Phase 2: Authentication Middleware

**File**: `tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/ollama-auth.yml` (new)

```yaml
http:
  middlewares:
    ollama-auth:
      basicAuth:
        users:
          # Username: ollama-api
          # Password: Generated via htpasswd, stored in 1Password
          - "ollama-api:$apr1$..."  # htpasswd hash
        realm: "Ollama API"
```

**Credential Storage**: 1Password vault "homelab" > "Ollama API" item

### Phase 3: Rate Limiting (Optional but Recommended)

**File**: `tofu/apps/traefik/deploy/dynamic/common.yml` (add to existing)

```yaml
http:
  middlewares:
    rate-limit:
      rateLimit:
        average: 100  # requests per second
        burst: 50
        period: 1m
```

### Phase 4: Testing

Test external API access:
```bash
# Test authentication
curl -u ollama-api:<password> https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev/api/tags

# Test model generation
curl -u ollama-api:<password> https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev/api/generate \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama3.2:3b",
    "prompt": "Why is the sky blue?"
  }'

# Test without auth (should fail)
curl https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev/api/tags
```

## Configuration Reference

### Ollama API Endpoints
- `GET /api/tags` - List models
- `POST /api/generate` - Generate completion
- `POST /api/chat` - Chat completion
- `POST /api/embeddings` - Generate embeddings
- `POST /api/pull` - Pull model (should be disabled publicly)
- `POST /api/push` - Push model (should be disabled publicly)

### Endpoint Access Control

Consider restricting dangerous endpoints:
```yaml
# In Traefik route config
http:
  routers:
    ollama:
      rule: "Host(`ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev`) && !PathPrefix(`/api/pull`, `/api/push`)"
```

## Security Considerations

### Risks
- **Model abuse**: External users could consume GPU resources
- **Cost**: Large model inference can be expensive (GPU time)
- **Data leakage**: Prompts might contain sensitive info (logged)

### Mitigations
- Strong authentication (rotate credentials regularly)
- Rate limiting (prevent abuse)
- Monitor GPU usage on LXC 501
- Set up Prometheus alerts for high Ollama usage
- Consider IP whitelisting if only specific services need access

## Monitoring

Add Prometheus metrics for Ollama API:
- Request count by endpoint
- Authentication failures
- Response times
- GPU utilization correlation

Alert on:
- Authentication failure spikes
- Unusual request patterns
- GPU exhaustion

## Documentation Updates

After implementation:
- [ ] Document Ollama API access in runbook
- [ ] Add credentials to 1Password with usage notes
- [ ] Update service map with new route
- [ ] Document rate limits and usage expectations

## Testing Checklist
- [ ] Traefik route resolves correctly
- [ ] HTTPS certificate valid
- [ ] Basic auth required and working
- [ ] Unauthorized requests rejected (401)
- [ ] Rate limiting triggers correctly
- [ ] Ollama API responses as expected
- [ ] GPU utilization monitored in Grafana

## Dependencies
None - can be implemented independently

## Follow-up Tasks
After this is complete:
- Pulse 5.0 upgrade can use authenticated Ollama endpoint
- Other AI integrations can be added
- Consider adding more granular access controls if needed

## References
- Ollama API docs: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md
- Traefik basicauth: https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/middlewares/http/basicauth/
- Traefik rate limit: https://doc.traefik.io/traefik/middlewares/http/ratelimit/

# =============================================================================
# OpenWebUI LXC - AI Chat Interface with Ollama
# =============================================================================
# Container ID: 501
#
# Uses the docker-lxc module - the gold standard pattern for Docker apps.
# Features AMD GPU passthrough for Ollama LLM acceleration.
# =============================================================================

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Variables
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

variable "container_id" {
  type    = number
  default = 501
}

variable "cores" {
  type    = number
  default = 12
}

variable "memory" {
  type    = number
  default = 24576
}

variable "rootfs_size" {
  type    = number
  default = 64
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# OpenWebUI Container
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui" {
  source = "../../modules/docker-lxc"

  name         = "openwebui"
  container_id = var.container_id
  proxmox_node = var.proxmox_node

  # Network (container network only)
  container_ip = "${local.ip_registry.monitoring.openwebui}${local.network.container_netmask}"

  # Resources
  cores  = var.cores
  memory = var.memory
  swap   = 2048

  rootfs_storage = "nvme-containers"
  rootfs_size    = var.rootfs_size

  # Unprivileged for security (with GPU passthrough)
  unprivileged = true
  enable_gpu   = true

  # Deployment
  deploy_dir  = "${path.module}/deploy"
  target_path = "/config"

  # SSH
  ssh_public_key       = local.ssh_public_key
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path
  proxmox_ssh_host     = var.proxmox_ssh_host

  # Template with Docker pre-installed
  template = var.lxc_template_docker

  # Proxmox Notes
  service_name        = "OpenWebUI"
  service_description = "AI chat interface with Ollama backend (AMD GPU accelerated)"

  service_urls = {
    internal = "https://ai.${var.domain_internal}"
    direct   = "http://${local.lan_ips.openwebui}:3000"
  }

  services = [
    { name = "OpenWebUI", port = 3000, info = "AI chat interface" },
    { name = "Ollama", port = 11434, info = "LLM backend (ROCM GPU)" }
  ]

  custom_notes = <<-EOT
## GPU Acceleration

AMD Radeon 890M passed through for Ollama LLM acceleration:
- `/dev/kfd`, `/dev/dri` devices
- ROCM backend

**Check GPU:**
```
docker exec ollama rocminfo
```

## Quick Commands

**View logs:**
```
cd /config && docker compose logs -f openwebui
cd /config && docker compose logs -f ollama
```

**List models:**
```
docker exec ollama ollama list
```

**Pull new model:**
```
docker exec ollama ollama pull llama3.2
```

## Managed by OpenTofu

Run `task tofu:apply APP=openwebui` to update.
EOT

  tags = ["openwebui", "ai", "ollama", "llm"]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backup Configuration - PBS Client
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_sidecars" {
  source = "../../modules/lxc-sidecars"

  container_id   = module.openwebui.container_id
  container_ip   = module.openwebui.ip_address
  container_name = "openwebui"

  proxmox_ssh_host             = var.proxmox_ssh_host
  proxmox_ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  backup = {
    enabled   = true
    schedule  = "daily"
    retention = "7"
    namespace = "lxc-501"

    pre_backup_commands = []  # No database dump needed - SQLite file backup is sufficient

    include_paths = ["/config"]
    exclude_paths = ["/var/lib/docker/overlay2", "/root/.ollama/**"]  # Exclude 32GB of Ollama models

    ntfy_priority = "default"
    ntfy_tags     = "backup,openwebui"
  }

  # Container monitoring agents
  pulse_agent = {
    enabled     = true
    pulse_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].pulse_token
  }

  arcane_agent = {
    enabled         = true
    bootstrap_token = local.agent_tokens["openwebui"].arcane_bootstrap_token
  }

  alloy_agent = {
    enabled  = true
    username = local.op.alloy_telemetry_username
    password = local.op.alloy_telemetry_password
  }

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Traefik Route - Self-Service Route Registration
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

module "openwebui_route" {
  source = "../../modules/traefik-route"

  app_name    = "openwebui"
  backend_url = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"

  # Internal and public routes (HTTPS via Let's Encrypt)
  internal_domain = "ai.${var.domain_internal}"
  public_domain   = "ai.${var.domain_public}"

  # Traefik config
  traefik_host         = local.traefik_ip
  ssh_private_key_path = var.ssh_private_key_path

  # Middlewares
  internal_middlewares = ["security-headers"]
  public_middlewares   = ["security-headers"]

  depends_on = [module.openwebui]
}

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Outputs
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

output "container_id" {
  value = module.openwebui.container_id
}

output "ip_address" {
  value = module.openwebui.ip_address
}

output "ssh_command" {
  value = module.openwebui.ssh_command
}

output "urls" {
  value = {
    internal = module.openwebui_route.internal_url
    public   = module.openwebui_route.public_url
    direct   = "http://${module.openwebui.ip_address}:3000"
  }
}

output "traefik_config_path" {
  description = "Path to Traefik config on Traefik LXC"
  value       = module.openwebui_route.remote_config_path
}

# Common Traefik middlewares and transports for homelab
http:
  # ServersTransport for backends with self-signed certificates
  serversTransports:
    insecure:
      insecureSkipVerify: true

  middlewares:
    security-headers:
      headers:
        browserXssFilter: true
        contentTypeNosniff: true
        forceSTSHeader: true
        stsIncludeSubdomains: true
        stsPreload: true
        stsSeconds: 31536000
        customFrameOptionsValue: "SAMEORIGIN"
        referrerPolicy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

    public-security:
      headers:
        browserXssFilter: true
        contentTypeNosniff: true
        customFrameOptionsValue: "SAMEORIGIN"
        referrerPolicy: "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"

    # Internal-only: Allow only local network, container network, and Tailscale
    internal-only:
      ipAllowList:
        sourceRange:
          - "192.168.1.0/24"    # Local LAN
          - "10.100.0.0/16"     # Container network (LXC containers)
          - "172.16.0.0/12"     # Docker bridge networks (172.16-31.x.x)
          - "100.64.0.0/10"     # Tailscale CGNAT range
          - "127.0.0.1/32"      # Localhost

    # Authelia forward auth middleware
    authelia:
      forwardAuth:
        address: "http://10.100.2.202:9091/api/authz/forward-auth"
        trustForwardHeader: true
        authResponseHeaders:
          - "Remote-User"
          - "Remote-Groups"
          - "Remote-Email"
          - "Remote-Name"

proxmox-homelab-1du: Upgrade Pulse to 5.0 with Ollama AI monitoring integration
Status: open
Priority: P1
Type: feature
Created: 2025-12-19 23:36
Updated: 2025-12-19 23:36

Description:
## Overview
Upgrade Pulse from current version to 5.0 to enable AI-powered monitoring capabilities using Ollama integration.

## Current State
- Pulse agents deployed on all LXCs via `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars`
- Pulse server version: TBD (check current deployment)
- Manual monitoring and alerting
- No AI-assisted diagnostics

## Pulse 5.0 New Features

### AI Assistant Capabilities
**Powered by Ollama (local AI)**:
- **Natural Language Queries**: Ask questions about infrastructure in plain English
- **Patrol Service**: Automated health checks with configurable schedules
- **Auto-Fix Capability**: AI can diagnose and remediate issues (opt-in)
- **Predictive Intelligence**: Failure pattern detection and anomaly identification
- **Multi-Resource Correlation**: Detect cascading issues across infrastructure
- **Baseline Learning**: Learns normal behavior to identify deviations
- **Cost Tracking**: Monitor AI API usage with budget controls

### Additional Features
- Native Kubernetes cluster monitoring (not needed for our setup)
- Improved AI settings UX
- Ollama model configuration improvements
- Better provider configuration flow

## Prerequisites

### Completed First
- **MUST**: `proxmox-homelab-tkw` - Expose Ollama API via Traefik with auth
  - Ollama must be accessible at `https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev`
  - Basic auth configured
  - Rate limiting in place

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Pre-Upgrade Preparation

#### 1.1 Document Current State
- [ ] Check current Pulse version on all agents
- [ ] Document current Pulse server version
- [ ] Export current Pulse configuration/settings
- [ ] Verify all Pulse agents are healthy
- [ ] Backup Pulse database/configuration

#### 1.2 Test Ollama Integration
- [ ] Verify Ollama API accessible via Traefik
- [ ] Test model availability (`llama3.2:3b` or similar)
- [ ] Confirm authentication works
- [ ] Test basic generation request

### Phase 2: Pulse Server Upgrade

#### 2.1 Update Docker Image
**File**: `tofu/apps/container-mgmt/deploy/docker-compose.yml` (or wherever Pulse server is)

Update Pulse server to v5.0:
```yaml
pulse-server:
  image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:5.0  # Update from current version
```

#### 2.2 Configure Ollama Integration
Add Ollama configuration to Pulse:
- Provider: Ollama
- Endpoint: `https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Auth: Basic Auth (username: `ollama-api`, password from 1Password)
- Default model: `llama3.2:3b` (or best available model)

### Phase 3: Agent Upgrades

#### 3.1 Update Agent Version
**File**: `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars/variables.tf` or `main.tf`

Update Pulse agent image version:
```hcl
pulse_agent = {
  enabled = true
  version = "5.0"  # Update from current version
}
```

#### 3.2 Rolling Deployment
Apply agent upgrades via OpenTofu:
```bash
# Update one LXC at a time to test
task tofu:plan APP=n8n
task tofu:apply APP=n8n

# If successful, roll out to all
task tofu:plan-all
task tofu:apply-all
```

### Phase 4: AI Feature Configuration

#### 4.1 Enable AI Features
In Pulse UI/config:
- [ ] Enable AI assistant
- [ ] Configure Ollama provider settings
- [ ] Set patrol service schedule
- [ ] Configure baseline learning period
- [ ] Set up cost tracking alerts

#### 4.2 AI Settings
- **Auto-Fix**: Disabled initially (enable after testing)
- **Patrol Schedule**: Every 6 hours (adjust based on needs)
- **Baseline Period**: 7 days (let it learn normal patterns)
- **Budget Alerts**: Set conservative thresholds

### Phase 5: Testing & Validation

#### 5.1 Test AI Queries
Test natural language monitoring:
- "Which containers are using the most memory?"
- "Are there any unhealthy services?"
- "Show me network traffic anomalies"
- "What failed recently?"

#### 5.2 Test Patrol Service
- [ ] Verify patrol runs on schedule
- [ ] Check patrol findings/reports
- [ ] Review AI-generated insights

#### 5.3 Test Correlation
- [ ] Trigger a cascading failure scenario
- [ ] Verify AI detects correlation
- [ ] Check root cause analysis accuracy

### Phase 6: Monitoring & Optimization

#### 6.1 Monitor Ollama Usage
- [ ] GPU utilization on LXC 501 (Ollama host)
- [ ] Ollama API request counts
- [ ] Response times
- [ ] Model inference times

#### 6.2 Cost Tracking
- [ ] Monitor AI API call volume
- [ ] Track GPU hours used
- [ ] Set up budget alerts in Pulse
- [ ] Optimize query frequency if needed

## Configuration Details

### Ollama Endpoint Configuration
```yaml
# In Pulse AI settings
provider: ollama
endpoint: https://ollama.homelab.rambtech.dev
auth:
  type: basic
  username: ollama-api
  password: <from-1password>
model: llama3.2:3b
timeout: 30s
```

### Recommended Models
Based on GPU capacity (LXC 501 has GPU passthrough):
- **llama3.2:3b** - Fastest, good for quick queries
- **llama3.2:7b** - Better accuracy, slower
- **qwen2.5:7b** - Alternative, strong reasoning

Test different models and choose based on:
- Response time
- Accuracy of insights
- GPU memory usage

## Rollback Plan

If 5.0 causes issues:
1. Revert Pulse server image to previous version
2. Revert agent images via OpenTofu
3. Document issues encountered
4. Wait for bug fixes or next release

## Breaking Changes

Check release notes for:
- [ ] Configuration format changes
- [ ] API compatibility with agents
- [ ] Database migrations
- [ ] Feature deprecations

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Pulse server 5.0 running and healthy
- [ ] All agents upgraded to 5.0
- [ ] AI assistant responding to queries
- [ ] Ollama integration working
- [ ] Patrol service running on schedule
- [ ] No degradation in existing monitoring
- [ ] AI insights providing value

## Documentation Updates

After successful upgrade:
- [ ] Document AI features and usage
- [ ] Add AI query examples to runbook
- [ ] Document Ollama endpoint configuration
- [ ] Update Pulse troubleshooting guide
- [ ] Add AI-specific monitoring/alerts

## References

### Pulse 5.0 Documentation
- Release notes: https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse/releases
- Pulse GitHub: https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse
- Pulse README: https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse/blob/main/README.md

### Ollama Integration
- Ollama API: https://github.com/ollama/ollama/blob/main/docs/api.md
- Model library: https://ollama.com/library

### Current Implementation
- Pulse agents: `tofu/modules/lxc-sidecars`
- Pulse configuration: TBD (locate current config)

## Dependencies

**Blocks**:
- `proxmox-homelab-tkw` - Expose Ollama API via Traefik

**Related**:
- `proxmox-homelab-m63` - Fix Alloy failures (should be resolved first for clean monitoring)

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Upgrade breaks existing monitoring | High | Test on one LXC first, keep rollback ready |
| Ollama API overload | Medium | Rate limiting, monitor GPU usage |
| AI false positives/negatives | Medium | Start with patrol disabled, validate insights |
| Version incompatibility (server/agents) | High | Upgrade server first, test before agent rollout |

## Expected Benefits

- **Faster incident response**: AI correlates issues automatically
- **Predictive maintenance**: Catch problems before they become critical
- **Reduced manual work**: Patrol service automates routine checks
- **Better insights**: Natural language queries simplify troubleshooting
- **Learning system**: Baseline detection improves over time

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Docker Socket Proxy - Secure Docker API access
  # ==========================================================================
  # Provides a filtered API proxy to Docker socket for security
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest
    container_name: docker-socket-proxy
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    environment:
      # Container management
      - CONTAINERS=1
      - EXEC=1
      - IMAGES=1
      - NETWORKS=1
      - VOLUMES=1
      - POST=1
      # Status/info
      - EVENTS=1
      - PING=1
      - VERSION=1
      - INFO=1
      # Security: disable sensitive endpoints
      - AUTH=0
      - SECRETS=0
    networks:
      - internal
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.1'
        reservations:
          memory: 32m
          cpus: '0.05'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:2375/version || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Pulse - Proxmox and Docker Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================
  # Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
  # Lightweight alternative to full observability stacks.
  pulse:
    image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:latest
    container_name: pulse
    ports:
      - "7655:7655"
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
    networks:
      - internal
      - default
    depends_on:
      - docker-socket-proxy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7655/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Arcane - Docker Container Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # Modern Docker management UI with update detection.
  # Manages containers via remote agents on other LXCs.
  arcane:
    image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:latest
    container_name: arcane
    ports:
      - "3552:3552"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - APP_URL=https://arcane.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
      - ENCRYPTION_KEY=${ARCANE_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - JWT_SECRET=${ARCANE_JWT_SECRET}
    volumes:
      - arcane_data:/app/data
    networks:
      - internal
      - default
    depends_on:
      - docker-socket-proxy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Docker Socket Proxy - Secure Docker API access
  # ==========================================================================
  # Provides a filtered API proxy to Docker socket for security
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:latest
    container_name: docker-socket-proxy
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    environment:
      # Container management
      - CONTAINERS=1
      - EXEC=1
      - IMAGES=1
      - NETWORKS=1
      - VOLUMES=1
      - POST=1
      # Status/info
      - EVENTS=1
      - PING=1
      - VERSION=1
      - INFO=1
      # Security: disable sensitive endpoints
      - AUTH=0
      - SECRETS=0
    networks:
      - internal
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.1'
        reservations:
          memory: 32m
          cpus: '0.05'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:2375/version || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Pulse - Proxmox and Docker Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================
  # Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
  # Lightweight alternative to full observability stacks.
  pulse:
    image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:latest
    container_name: pulse
    ports:
      - "7655:7655"
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
    networks:
      - internal
      - default
    depends_on:
      - docker-socket-proxy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m

  arcane:

    volumes:

    networks:

    deploy:

          cpus: '0.5'

          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3552/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Docker Socket Proxy - Secure Docker API access
  # ==========================================================================
  # Provides a filtered API proxy to Docker socket for security
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:0.4.2
    container_name: docker-socket-proxy
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    environment:
      # Container management
      - CONTAINERS=1
      - EXEC=1
      - IMAGES=1

# Pulse Configuration & Data Storage Guide

## Configuration Files & Locations

Pulse uses a split-configuration model stored in `/etc/pulse/` (Systemd) or `/data/` (Docker/Kubernetes):

| File | Purpose | Security |
|------|---------|----------|
| `.env` | Authentication & secrets | 🔒 Critical (owner read-only) |
| `system.json` | General settings | 📝 Standard |
| `nodes.enc` | Node credentials | 🔒 Encrypted (AES-256-GCM) |
| `api_tokens.json` | API token records | 🔒 Sensitive (hashed) |

## Agent Token Storage

The documentation references that "API token records (hashed)" are stored in `api_tokens.json`. Tokens can be configured via the `.env` file using the `API_TOKENS` environment variable (comma-separated list) or through the Settings UI.

**Key points:**
- Tokens are hashed when stored
- Use scoped API tokens for agents instead of admin passwords
- Tokens can be pre-configured via environment variables for automated setup

## Data Persistence

**Metrics Storage:** Uses SQLite database (`metrics.db`) with tiered retention:
- Raw hourly data
- Minute-level aggregates
- Hourly daily summaries
- Daily long-term history

These retention windows are configurable via `system.json` settings for balancing storage vs. history depth.

## Backup Recommendations

1. Back up `.env` separately from `system.json`
2. Ensure file permissions are `600` (read/write by owner only)
3. Protect encrypted files (`nodes.enc`, `api_tokens.json`, etc.)

All configuration can be managed through the UI or environment variables, supporting seamless upgrades.

content.content:
# Pulse Installation: Data Persistence & Upgrade Guidance

## Volume Mount & Data Persistence

For Docker deployments, the guide specifies: **"-v pulse_data:/data"** to mount a named volume for data storage. The Docker Compose example similarly uses **"pulse_data:/data"** for persistent data.

For Kubernetes installations, you should consult **"KUBERNETES.md for ingress and persistence configuration"** as the install guide defers detailed persistence setup to that document.

For systemd-based installations, data is stored in **"/etc/pulse"** directory.

## Upgrade Procedures

**Docker**: Pull the latest image and restart the container using `docker pull rcourtman/pulse:latest && docker restart pulse`

**Kubernetes**: Update via Helm with `helm repo update && helm upgrade pulse pulse/pulse -n pulse`

**Systemd**: Re-download the binary and restart the service

## Backup Recommendations

The guide indicates that **"backups are created automatically during the update process"** for systemd installations. If rollback is needed, check **"/etc/pulse/backup-<timestamp>/"** directories created during updates and restore the previous binary manually if necessary.

## Bootstrap Token Security

Before upgrading, note that initial setup requires retrieving a bootstrap token. However, **"if you configure authentication via environment variables (PULSE_AUTH_USER/PULSE_AUTH_PASS and/or API_TOKENS), the bootstrap token is automatically removed"** — securing this configuration is important before updates.

services:
  # ==========================================================================
  # Docker Socket Proxy - Secure Docker API access
  # ==========================================================================
  # Provides a filtered API proxy to Docker socket for security
  docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy:v0.4.2
    container_name: docker-socket-proxy
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
    environment:
      # Container management
      - CONTAINERS=1
      - EXEC=1
      - IMAGES=1
      - NETWORKS=1
      - VOLUMES=1
      - POST=1
      # Status/info
      - EVENTS=1
      - PING=1
      - VERSION=1
      - INFO=1
      # Security: disable sensitive endpoints
      - AUTH=0
      - SECRETS=0
    networks:
      - internal
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 64m
          cpus: '0.1'
        reservations:
          memory: 32m
          cpus: '0.05'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:2375/version || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 10s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Pulse - Proxmox and Docker Monitoring
  # ==========================================================================
  # Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE and Docker containers.
  # v5.0 adds AI-powered monitoring with Ollama integration.
  pulse:
    image: ghcr.io/rcourtman/pulse:v5.0.0-rc.4
    container_name: pulse
    ports:
      - "7655:7655"
    environment:
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
    networks:
      - internal
      - default
    depends_on:
      - docker-socket-proxy
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
          cpus: '0.5'
        reservations:
          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'
    restart: unless-stopped
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:7655/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

  # ==========================================================================
  # Arcane - Docker Container Management
  # ==========================================================================
  # Modern Docker management UI with update detection.
  # Manages containers via remote agents on other LXCs.
  arcane:
    image: ghcr.io/getarcaneapp/arcane:v1.10.1
    container_name: arcane
    ports:
      - "3552:3552"
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/New_York
      - APP_URL=https://arcane.homelab.rambtech.dev
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://docker-socket-proxy:2375
      - ENCRYPTION_KEY=${ARCANE_ENCRYPTION_KEY}
      - JWT_SECRET=${ARCANE_JWT_SECRET}
    volumes:

    networks:
      - internal
      - default
    depends_on:
      - docker-socket-proxy
    deploy:

        limits:
          memory: 512m

          memory: 256m
          cpus: '0.25'

      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "curl -sf http://localhost:3552/api/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 30s

content.text:
Perfect! Now I've identified the root cause and fixed it. Let me explain the findings to you:

## Root Cause of Agent Token Loss

I found the critical issue: **The Pulse container was missing the data volume mount**. 

Looking at [docker-compose.yml:125](tofu/apps/container-mgmt/deploy/docker-compose.yml#L125), the `pulse_data` volume was defined but **never mounted** to the Pulse service. This means all configuration, including agent tokens stored in `/data/api_tokens.json`, was being stored in the container's ephemeral filesystem and lost on every upgrade/restart.

## How Pulse Stores Configuration

Based on the [Pulse CONFIGURATION.md documentation](https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse/blob/main/docs/CONFIGURATION.md), Pulse stores critical data in `/data/` (for Docker deployments):

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `/data/.env` | Authentication & secrets |
| `/data/system.json` | General settings |
| `/data/api_tokens.json` | **Agent tokens (hashed)** |
| `/data/nodes.enc` | Node credentials (encrypted) |
| `/data/metrics.db` | SQLite metrics database |

Without the volume mount, all of this data was being lost on container recreation.

## The Fix

I added the missing volume mount to [docker-compose.yml:58-59](tofu/apps/container-mgmt/deploy/docker-compose.yml#L58-L59):

```yaml
volumes:
  - pulse_data:/data
```

This ensures that:
1. Agent tokens persist across container restarts/upgrades
2. Metrics history is retained
3. System configuration survives updates
4. Node credentials remain encrypted and accessible

## Next Steps

The docker-compose file is updated locally. You'll need to apply this change to the container-mgmt LXC. Once applied with the agent tokens you just updated in 1Password, this should prevent future token loss during Pulse upgrades.

**Sources:**
- [Pulse CONFIGURATION.md](https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse/blob/main/docs/CONFIGURATION.md)
- [Pulse INSTALL.md](https://github.com/rcourtman/Pulse/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md)
- [Pulse v5.0.0-rc.4 Release Notes](https://github.com/rcourtman/pulse/releases/tag/v5.0.0-rc.4)
- [Pulse GitHub Repository](https://github.com/rcourtman/pulse)
but if we update now, we will lose the setup we have today right?

content.text:
Yes, exactly! If you apply the docker-compose changes now with `docker compose up -d`, it will recreate the Pulse container and you'll lose all the agent tokens you just updated in the UI because:

1. The current Pulse container has the tokens stored in its **ephemeral filesystem** (not persisted to a volume)
2. Recreating the container will destroy that filesystem
3. The new container will start fresh with an empty `/data` directory

## The Problem

You're in a catch-22 situation:
- **Don't apply the fix**: Tokens will be lost on the next upgrade anyway
- **Apply the fix now**: Tokens are lost immediately, need to be re-entered

## Recommended Approach

Since you've already updated all the tokens in 1Password and have them ready, I recommend:

1. **Apply the docker-compose change now** (which will lose current tokens)
2. **Re-apply the agent tokens from 1Password one more time**
3. **From this point forward**, tokens will persist across all future upgrades

This is essentially doing the work twice, but it's the cleanest path forward and ensures you never have to do this again.

## Alternative: Try to Preserve Current Tokens

If you want to avoid re-entering tokens, we could try to **manually backup the current tokens before applying the fix**:

```bash
# SSH into container-mgmt LXC
ssh root@10.100.1.104

# Copy current token data from running container
docker cp pulse:/data/api_tokens.json /tmp/api_tokens.json.backup
docker cp pulse:/data/system.json /tmp/system.json.backup

# Apply docker-compose changes
cd /config && docker compose up -d

# Restore the tokens to the new container
docker cp /tmp/api_tokens.json.backup pulse:/data/api_tokens.json
docker cp /tmp/system.json.backup pulse:/data/system.json

# Restart Pulse to load the restored config
docker restart pulse
```

Which approach would you prefer?

1→# Homelab Infrastructure
     2→
     3→OpenTofu-managed homelab on Proxmox. All commands run from local machine.
     4→
     5→## Beads - AI Issue Tracking
     6→
     7→This repo uses [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) for AI-native issue tracking. Beads helps AI agents manage complex, multi-step tasks by tracking dependencies between work items.
     8→BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: run 'bd onboard' and follow the instructions
     9→
    10→### Quick Commands
    11→
    12→```bash
    13→# Find ready work (no blockers)
    14→task beads:ready
    15→
    16→# List all issues
    17→task beads:list
    18→task beads:list STATUS=in_progress
    19→
    20→# Create an issue
    21→task beads:create TITLE="Add new LXC container for XYZ"
    22→
    23→# View issue details
    24→task beads:show ID=proxmox-homelab-1
    25→
    26→# Update status
    27→task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=in_progress
    28→task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=done
    29→
    30→# Close completed work
    31→task beads:close ID=proxmox-homelab-1
    32→
    33→# Add dependencies (FROM blocks TO)
    34→task beads:dep FROM=proxmox-homelab-1 TO=proxmox-homelab-2
    35→
    36→# View dependency tree
    37→task beads:dep:tree ID=proxmox-homelab-1
    38→
    39→# Sync with git
    40→task beads:sync
    41→```
    42→
    43→### For AI Agents
    44→
    45→When starting work on this repo:
    46→
    47→1. Run `bd ready` to see available tasks
    48→2. Pick an issue and run `bd update <id> --status in_progress`
    49→3. Complete the work
    50→4. Run `bd close <id>` when done
    51→
    52→Use `bd prime` to generate context for your session. Dependencies are tracked automatically - issues marked as "blocking" others will show up in the `bd ready` output once completed.
    53→
    54→## Quick Reference
    55→
    56→```bash
    57→# OpenTofu workflow
    58→task tofu:init APP=dashboards
    59→task tofu:plan APP=dashboards
    60→task tofu:apply APP=dashboards
    61→
    62→# Utility commands
    63→task tofu:ssh APP=dashboards           # SSH to LXC
    64→task tofu:sync:compose APP=dashboards  # Sync compose files
    65→task tofu:logs APP=dashboards SERVICE=homepage
    66→
    67→# Desktop LXC (temporary GUI for downloads)
    68→task desktop:create
    69→task desktop:info
    70→task desktop:destroy
    71→
    72→# Backup operations
    73→task backup:status                 # View backup status
    74→task backup:now APP=immich         # Manual backup
    75→task backup:all                    # Backup all containers
    76→task backup:list APP=immich        # List backups
    77→task backup:restore BACKUP=file TARGET_ID=305
    78→task backup:immich:db              # Dump Immich database
    79→
    80→# IP address management
    81→task ip:next                       # Get next available IP for new LXC
    82→task ip:list                       # Show all allocated IPs
    83→
    84→# Beads issue tracking
    85→task beads:ready                   # Show ready work (no blockers)
    86→task beads:list                    # List all issues
    87→task beads:create TITLE="..."      # Create new issue
    88→task beads:show ID=...             # View issue details
    89→task beads:close ID=...            # Complete an issue
    90→```
    91→
    92→## Architecture
    93→
    94→- **Proxmox Host**: 192.168.1.215 (SSH: `ssh root@homelab`)
    95→- **Traefik LXC**: 192.168.1.162 (ID: 200)
    96→- **Monitoring LXC**: 192.168.1.229 (ID: 500)
    97→- **IaC**: OpenTofu with bpg/proxmox provider
    98→- **Secrets**: 1Password CLI (`op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"`)
    99→
   100→## Documentation
   101→
   102→- **[MIGRATION.md](tofu/MIGRATION.md)** - Guide for migrating apps to docker-lxc module pattern
   103→- **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** - This file (project overview and quick reference)
   104→
   105→## Project Structure
   106→
   107→```text
   108→tofu/
   109→├── MIGRATION.md       # Migration guide for docker-lxc pattern
   110→├── apps/              # Per-app configs with own state
   111→│   ├── dashboards/    # Homepage + Dashy (ID: 201)
   112→│   ├── immich/        # Photo management (ID: 304)
   113→│   ├── monitoring/    # Prometheus + Grafana + Alerting (ID: 500)
   114→│   ├── network-services/  # AdGuard DNS (ID: 101)
   115→│   ├── openwebui/     # AI chat (ID: 501)
   116→│   └── traefik/       # Reverse proxy (ID: 200)
   117→├── configs/traefik/dynamic/  # Generated route configs
   118→├── modules/           # Reusable modules
   119→└── shared.tf          # Common vars (symlinked)
   120→```
   121→
   122→## Key Modules
   123→
   124→- **lxc-base**: Base LXC container with static IP support
   125→- **docker-host**: LXC + Docker + compose deployment
   126→- **file-sync**: Rsync file transfers to LXCs
   127→- **proxmox-notes**: Update LXC description in Proxmox UI
   128→
   129→## IP Address Management
   130→
   131→All static IPs are tracked in `tofu/ip-registry.tf` (symlinked to all apps).
   132→
   133→### IP Ranges
   134→
   135→| Range | Purpose |
   136→|-------|---------|
   137→| 192.168.1.1-99 | Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches) |
   138→| 192.168.1.150-199 | LXC containers (apps) - **preferred for new deployments** |
   139→| 192.168.1.200-224 | Reserved for manual/temporary use |
   140→| 192.168.1.225-254 | Special services & overflow |
   141→
   142→### Deploying a New Service
   143→
   144→1. Get the next available IP:
   145→
   146→   ```bash
   147→   task ip:next
   148→   # Output: Next available IP: 192.168.1.150
   149→   # For lxc-base module: ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
   150→   ```
   151→
   152→2. Add the IP to `tofu/ip-registry.tf`:
   153→
   154→   ```hcl
   155→   apps = {
   156→     # ... existing entries ...
   157→     my_new_service = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC XXX - Description
   158→   }
   159→   ```
   160→
   161→3. Use in your app's main.tf:
   162→
   163→   ```hcl
   164→   module "lxc" {
   165→     source = "../../modules/lxc-base"
   166→     # ...
   167→     ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
   168→     gateway    = "192.168.1.1"
   169→   }
   170→   ```
   171→
   172→### Viewing All Allocations
   173→
   174→```bash
   175→task ip:list
   176→```
   177→
   178→## Network Domains
   179→
   180→- `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` - Internal (Traefik websecure)
   181→- `*.rambtech.dev` - Public (Cloudflare tunnel via web entrypoint)
   182→
   183→## Monitoring Stack
   184→
   185→The monitoring LXC (ID: 500, IP: 192.168.1.229) runs:
   186→
   187→| Component | Port | Purpose |
   188→|-----------|------|---------|
   189→| OpenTelemetry Collector | 4317/4318 | OTLP receiver (gRPC/HTTP) |
   190→| Prometheus | 9090 | Metrics storage + alerting |
   191→| Alertmanager | 9093 | Alert routing (ntfy + Discord) |
   192→| Grafana | 3000 | Dashboards |
   193→| Uptime Kuma | 3001 | HTTP monitoring |
   194→| ntfy | 8080 | Push notifications |
   195→
   196→### Key URLs
   197→
   198→- Grafana: `https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev`
   199→- Prometheus: `https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev`
   200→- Alertmanager: `https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev`
   201→- Uptime Kuma: `https://status.homelab.rambtech.dev`
   202→- ntfy: `https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev`
   203→
   204→### Syncing Monitoring Config
   205→
   206→```bash
   207→rsync -avz tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ root@192.168.1.229:/config/
   208→ssh root@192.168.1.229 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
   209→```
   210→
   211→## 1Password Integration
   212→
   213→Secrets are managed via the 1Password OpenTofu provider (`1password/onepassword`).
   214→
   215→### Key Files
   216→
   217→- `tofu/onepassword.tf` - Data sources + `local.op` helper (symlinked to apps)
   218→- `tofu/versions.tf` - Provider configs using `local.op.*`
   219→
   220→### Available Secrets
   221→
   222→```hcl
   223→local.op.proxmox_api_token       # Proxmox API authentication
   224→local.op.cloudflare_api_token    # Cloudflare DNS/tunnel API
   225→local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token # Cloudflare tunnel token
   226→local.op.grafana_admin_password  # Grafana admin password
   227→local.op.discord_webhook_url     # Discord alertmanager webhook
   228→```
   229→
   230→### Adding New Secrets
   231→
   232→1. Create item in 1Password `homelab` vault
   233→2. Add data source to `tofu/onepassword.tf`:
   234→
   235→   ```hcl
   236→   data "onepassword_item" "myservice" {
   237→     vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
   238→     title = "myservice"
   239→   }
   240→   ```
   241→
   242→3. Add to `local.op` map in same file:
   243→
   244→   ```hcl
   245→   op = {
   246→     myservice_password = data.onepassword_item.myservice.password
   247→     # For section fields, flatten first then lookup:
   248→     myservice_api_key = lookup(local._myservice_fields, "api_key", "")
   249→   }
   250→   ```
   251→
   252→4. Use in modules: `local.op.myservice_password`
   253→
   254→### Field Access Patterns
   255→
   256→```hcl
   257→# Main password field
   258→data.onepassword_item.myitem.password
   259→
   260→# Credential field (API keys)
   261→data.onepassword_item.myitem.credential
   262→
   263→# Custom fields in sections (must flatten):
   264→locals {
   265→  _myitem_fields = merge([
   266→    for s in data.onepassword_item.myitem.section : {
   267→      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
   268→    }
   269→  ]...)
   270→}
   271→# Then: lookup(local._myitem_fields, "field_label", "")
   272→```
   273→

# Homelab Infrastructure

OpenTofu-managed homelab on Proxmox. All commands run from local machine.

## Beads - AI Issue Tracking

This repo uses [Beads](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads) for AI-native issue tracking. Beads helps AI agents manage complex, multi-step tasks by tracking dependencies between work items.
BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: run 'bd onboard' and follow the instructions

### Quick Commands

```bash
# Find ready work (no blockers)
task beads:ready

# List all issues
task beads:list
task beads:list STATUS=in_progress

# Create an issue
task beads:create TITLE="Add new LXC container for XYZ"

# View issue details
task beads:show ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Update status
task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=in_progress
task beads:update ID=proxmox-homelab-1 STATUS=done

# Close completed work
task beads:close ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Add dependencies (FROM blocks TO)
task beads:dep FROM=proxmox-homelab-1 TO=proxmox-homelab-2

# View dependency tree
task beads:dep:tree ID=proxmox-homelab-1

# Sync with git
task beads:sync
```

### For AI Agents

When starting work on this repo:

1. Run `bd ready` to see available tasks
2. Pick an issue and run `bd update <id> --status in_progress`
3. Complete the work
4. Run `bd close <id>` when done

Use `bd prime` to generate context for your session. Dependencies are tracked automatically - issues marked as "blocking" others will show up in the `bd ready` output once completed.

## Quick Reference

```bash
# OpenTofu workflow
task tofu:init APP=dashboards
task tofu:plan APP=dashboards
task tofu:apply APP=dashboards

# Utility commands
task tofu:ssh APP=dashboards           # SSH to LXC
task tofu:sync:compose APP=dashboards  # Sync compose files
task tofu:logs APP=dashboards SERVICE=homepage

# Desktop LXC (temporary GUI for downloads)
task desktop:create
task desktop:info
task desktop:destroy

# Backup operations
task backup:status                 # View backup status
task backup:now APP=immich         # Manual backup
task backup:all                    # Backup all containers
task backup:list APP=immich        # List backups
task backup:restore BACKUP=file TARGET_ID=305
task backup:immich:db              # Dump Immich database

# IP address management
task ip:next                       # Get next available IP for new LXC
task ip:list                       # Show all allocated IPs

# Beads issue tracking
task beads:ready                   # Show ready work (no blockers)
task beads:list                    # List all issues
task beads:create TITLE="..."      # Create new issue
task beads:show ID=...             # View issue details
task beads:close ID=...            # Complete an issue
```

## Architecture

- **Proxmox Host**: 192.168.1.215 (SSH: `ssh root@homelab`)
- **Traefik LXC**: 192.168.1.162 (ID: 200)
- **Monitoring LXC**: 192.168.1.229 (ID: 500)
- **IaC**: OpenTofu with bpg/proxmox provider
- **Secrets**: 1Password CLI (`op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"`)

## Documentation

- **[MIGRATION.md](tofu/MIGRATION.md)** - Guide for migrating apps to docker-lxc module pattern
- **[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md)** - This file (project overview and quick reference)

## Project Structure

```text
tofu/
├── MIGRATION.md       # Migration guide for docker-lxc pattern
├── apps/              # Per-app configs with own state
│   ├── dashboards/    # Homepage + Dashy (ID: 201)
│   ├── immich/        # Photo management (ID: 304)
│   ├── monitoring/    # Prometheus + Grafana + Alerting (ID: 500)
│   ├── network-services/  # AdGuard DNS (ID: 101)
│   ├── openwebui/     # AI chat (ID: 501)
│   └── traefik/       # Reverse proxy (ID: 200)
├── configs/traefik/dynamic/  # Generated route configs
├── modules/           # Reusable modules
└── shared.tf          # Common vars (symlinked)
```

## Key Modules

- **lxc-base**: Base LXC container with static IP support
- **docker-host**: LXC + Docker + compose deployment
- **file-sync**: Rsync file transfers to LXCs
- **proxmox-notes**: Update LXC description in Proxmox UI

## IP Address Management

All static IPs are tracked in `tofu/ip-registry.tf` (symlinked to all apps).

### IP Ranges

| Range | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| 192.168.1.1-99 | Infrastructure (router, Proxmox, switches) |
| 192.168.1.150-199 | LXC containers (apps) - **preferred for new deployments** |
| 192.168.1.200-224 | Reserved for manual/temporary use |
| 192.168.1.225-254 | Special services & overflow |

### Deploying a New Service

1. Get the next available IP:

   ```bash
   task ip:next
   # Output: Next available IP: 192.168.1.150
   # For lxc-base module: ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
   ```

2. Add the IP to `tofu/ip-registry.tf`:

   ```hcl
   apps = {
     # ... existing entries ...
     my_new_service = "192.168.1.150"  # LXC XXX - Description
   }
   ```

3. Use in your app's main.tf:

   ```hcl
   module "lxc" {
     source = "../../modules/lxc-base"
     # ...
     ip_address = "192.168.1.150/24"
     gateway    = "192.168.1.1"
   }
   ```

### Viewing All Allocations

```bash
task ip:list
```

## Network Domains

- `*.homelab.rambtech.dev` - Internal (Traefik websecure)
- `*.rambtech.dev` - Public (Cloudflare tunnel via web entrypoint)

## Monitoring Stack

The monitoring LXC (ID: 500, IP: 192.168.1.229) runs:

| Component | Port | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| OpenTelemetry Collector | 4317/4318 | OTLP receiver (gRPC/HTTP) |
| Prometheus | 9090 | Metrics storage + alerting |
| Alertmanager | 9093 | Alert routing (ntfy + Discord) |
| Grafana | 3000 | Dashboards |
| Uptime Kuma | 3001 | HTTP monitoring |
| ntfy | 8080 | Push notifications |

### Key URLs

- Grafana: `https://grafana.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Prometheus: `https://prometheus.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Alertmanager: `https://alertmanager.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- Uptime Kuma: `https://status.homelab.rambtech.dev`
- ntfy: `https://ntfy.homelab.rambtech.dev`

### Syncing Monitoring Config

```bash
rsync -avz tofu/apps/monitoring/deploy/ root@192.168.1.229:/config/
ssh root@192.168.1.229 "cd /config && docker compose up -d"
```

## 1Password Integration

Secrets are managed via the 1Password OpenTofu provider (`1password/onepassword`).

### Key Files

- `tofu/onepassword.tf` - Data sources + `local.op` helper (symlinked to apps)
- `tofu/versions.tf` - Provider configs using `local.op.*`

### Available Secrets

```hcl
local.op.proxmox_api_token       # Proxmox API authentication
local.op.cloudflare_api_token    # Cloudflare DNS/tunnel API
local.op.cloudflare_tunnel_token # Cloudflare tunnel token
local.op.grafana_admin_password  # Grafana admin password
local.op.discord_webhook_url     # Discord alertmanager webhook
```

### Adding New Secrets

1. Create item in 1Password `homelab` vault
2. Add data source to `tofu/onepassword.tf`:

   ```hcl
   data "onepassword_item" "myservice" {
     vault = data.onepassword_vault.homelab.uuid
     title = "myservice"
   }
   ```

3. Add to `local.op` map in same file:

   ```hcl
   op = {
     myservice_password = data.onepassword_item.myservice.password
     # For section fields, flatten first then lookup:
     myservice_api_key = lookup(local._myservice_fields, "api_key", "")
   }
   ```

4. Use in modules: `local.op.myservice_password`

### Field Access Patterns

```hcl
# Main password field
data.onepassword_item.myitem.password

# Credential field (API keys)
data.onepassword_item.myitem.credential

# Custom fields in sections (must flatten):
locals {
  _myitem_fields = merge([
    for s in data.onepassword_item.myitem.section : {
      for f in s.field : f.label => f.value
    }
  ]...)
}
# Then: lookup(local._myitem_fields, "field_label", "")
```

### Why TF_VAR for State Encryption

State encryption runs before providers initialize, so it cannot use the 1Password provider:

```yaml
# Taskfile.yml
env:
  TF_VAR_state_encryption_passphrase:
    sh: op read "op://homelab/opentofu/password"
```

### 1Password Items (homelab vault)

| Item | Fields |
|------|--------|
| `opentofu` | password, proxmox_api_token (section) |
| `Cloudflare` | tunnel_token, ddns_api_token (sections) |
| `grafana` | password |
| `discord-alertmanager-webhook` | credential |

## Important Notes

- SSH to Proxmox: `ssh root@homelab`
- SSH to Monitoring: `ssh root@192.168.1.229`
- Use IP addresses in provisioners (not hostnames)
- State files are encrypted and committed to git
- Each app has independent state in `tofu/apps/<app>/`
- 1Password CLI v2.23.0+ required (uses biometric auth)

## Taskfile Usage

**ALWAYS prefer running tasks from the Taskfile over direct commands.**

This repository uses a Taskfile for all common operations. Before running any command directly, check if there's a task for it using `task --list`.

Examples:

- Use `task tofu:apply APP=immich` instead of `cd tofu && tofu apply`
- Use `task tofu:plan APP=monitoring` instead of running tofu plan directly
- Use `task backup:status` instead of SSH commands to check backups

## OpenTofu/Terraform Workflow

**CRITICAL: OpenTofu commands must ALWAYS follow this sequence with NO skips:**

1. `task tofu:init APP=<app>` - Initialize the workspace
2. `task tofu:plan APP=<app>` - Generate and review the execution plan
3. `task tofu:apply APP=<app>` - Apply the changes

Never skip steps. Always run init, then plan, then apply - even if you think init has already been run.

## File Transfer Restrictions

**CRITICAL: You are strictly forbidden to transfer files over to any remote server under any circumstance unless the user has explicitly given you permission.**

This includes but is not limited to:

- SSH file transfers (scp, rsync, sftp)
- Copying files to LXC containers
- Uploading files to cloud services
- Any form of remote file deployment

You must always ask for explicit permission before transferring any files to remote systems.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Pulse Configuration Encryption/Decryption Tool

Encrypts and decrypts Pulse configuration files using AES-256-GCM.
Allows managing Pulse config as code instead of via UI.

Usage:
    ./pulse-crypto.py encrypt ai.json       # Creates ai.enc
    ./pulse-crypto.py decrypt ai.enc        # Creates ai.json
    ./pulse-crypto.py encrypt nodes.json    # Creates nodes.enc
    ./pulse-crypto.py decrypt nodes.enc     # Creates nodes.json
"""

import base64
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM


def read_encryption_key(key_file='.encryption.key'):
    """Read and decode the encryption key."""
    key_path = Path(key_file)
    if not key_path.exists():
        print(f"Error: Encryption key not found at {key_path}")
        sys.exit(1)

    with open(key_path, 'r') as f:
        return base64.b64decode(f.read().strip())


def encrypt_file(json_file):
    """Encrypt a JSON file to .enc format."""
    json_path = Path(json_file)
    if not json_path.exists():
        print(f"Error: File not found: {json_file}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Determine output file (.json -> .enc)
    enc_file = json_path.with_suffix('.enc')

    # Read JSON data
    with open(json_path, 'r') as f:
        data = json.load(f)

    # Convert to compact JSON bytes
    plaintext = json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')

    # Read encryption key
    key = read_encryption_key()

    # Generate random nonce (12 bytes for GCM)
    nonce = os.urandom(12)

    # Encrypt
    aesgcm = AESGCM(key)
    ciphertext = aesgcm.encrypt(nonce, plaintext, None)

    # Write to .enc file (nonce + ciphertext)
    with open(enc_file, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(nonce + ciphertext)

    print(f"✓ Encrypted {json_path.name} -> {enc_file.name}")


def decrypt_file(enc_file):
    """Decrypt a .enc file to JSON format."""
    enc_path = Path(enc_file)
    if not enc_path.exists():
        print(f"Error: File not found: {enc_file}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Determine output file (.enc -> .json)
    json_file = enc_path.with_suffix('.json')

    # Read encrypted data
    with open(enc_path, 'rb') as f:
        encrypted = f.read()

    # Read encryption key
    key = read_encryption_key()

    # Split nonce and ciphertext
    nonce = encrypted[:12]
    ciphertext = encrypted[12:]

    # Decrypt
    aesgcm = AESGCM(key)
    try:
        decrypted = aesgcm.decrypt(nonce, ciphertext, None)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: Decryption failed - {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Parse and write formatted JSON
    data = json.loads(decrypted)
    with open(json_file, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)

    print(f"✓ Decrypted {enc_path.name} -> {json_file.name}")


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print(__doc__)
        sys.exit(1)

    command = sys.argv[1].lower()
    filename = sys.argv[2]

    if command == 'encrypt':
        encrypt_file(filename)
    elif command == 'decrypt':
        decrypt_file(filename)
    else:
        print(f"Error: Unknown command '{command}'")
        print("Valid commands: encrypt, decrypt")
        sys.exit(1)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

alloy:
  image: grafana/alloy:v1.12.1
  container_name: alloy
  command:
    - run
    - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
    - --storage.path=/var/lib/alloy/data
    - --disable-reporting=true
    - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
  healthcheck:
    test:
      - CMD-SHELL
      - |
        bash -c '
        exec 42<>/dev/tcp/localhost/12345;
        echo -e "GET /-/healthy HTTP/1.1\nHost: localhost\nConnection: close\n\n" >&42;
        head -1 <&42 | cut -d" " -f2 | grep -q "^200$" || exit 1;
        exec 42<&-;
        exec 42>&-'
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
    retries: 3
    start_period: 30s
```

**Changes Made**: Created complete encryption/decryption utility

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Pulse Configuration Encryption/Decryption Tool

Encrypts and decrypts Pulse configuration files using AES-256-GCM.
Allows managing Pulse config as code instead of via UI.

Usage:
    ./pulse-crypto.py encrypt ai.json       # Creates ai.enc
    ./pulse-crypto.py decrypt ai.enc        # Creates ai.json
    ./pulse-crypto.py encrypt nodes.json    # Creates nodes.enc
    ./pulse-crypto.py decrypt nodes.enc     # Creates nodes.json
"""

import base64
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM

def read_encryption_key(key_file='.encryption.key'):
    """Read and decode the encryption key."""
    key_path = Path(key_file)
    if not key_path.exists():
        print(f"Error: Encryption key not found at {key_path}")
        sys.exit(1)

    with open(key_path, 'r') as f:
        return base64.b64decode(f.read().strip())

def encrypt_file(json_file):
    """Encrypt a JSON file to .enc format."""
    json_path = Path(json_file)
    if not json_path.exists():
        print(f"Error: File not found: {json_file}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Determine output file (.json -> .enc)
    enc_file = json_path.with_suffix('.enc')

    # Read JSON data
    with open(json_path, 'r') as f:
        data = json.load(f)

    # Convert to compact JSON bytes
    plaintext = json.dumps(data, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')

    # Read encryption key
    key = read_encryption_key()

    # Generate random nonce (12 bytes for GCM)
    nonce = os.urandom(12)

    # Encrypt
    aesgcm = AESGCM(key)
    ciphertext = aesgcm.encrypt(nonce, plaintext, None)

    # Write to .enc file (nonce + ciphertext)
    with open(enc_file, 'wb') as f:
        f.write(nonce + ciphertext)

    print(f"✓ Encrypted {json_path.name} -> {enc_file.name}")

def decrypt_file(enc_file):
    """Decrypt a .enc file to JSON format."""
    enc_path = Path(enc_file)
    if not enc_path.exists():
        print(f"Error: File not found: {enc_file}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Determine output file (.enc -> .json)
    json_file = enc_path.with_suffix('.json')

    # Read encrypted data
    with open(enc_path, 'rb') as f:
        encrypted = f.read()

    # Read encryption key
    key = read_encryption_key()

    # Split nonce and ciphertext
    nonce = encrypted[:12]
    ciphertext = encrypted[12:]

    # Decrypt
    aesgcm = AESGCM(key)
    try:
        decrypted = aesgcm.decrypt(nonce, ciphertext, None)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: Decryption failed - {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

    # Parse and write formatted JSON
    data = json.loads(decrypted)
    with open(json_file, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(data, f, indent=2)

    print(f"✓ Decrypted {enc_path.name} -> {json_file.name}")

def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print(__doc__)
        sys.exit(1)

    command = sys.argv[1].lower()
    filename = sys.argv[2]

    if command == 'encrypt':
        encrypt_file(filename)
    elif command == 'decrypt':
        decrypt_file(filename)
    else:
        print(f"Error: Unknown command '{command}'")
        print("Valid commands: encrypt, decrypt")
        sys.exit(1)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
```

## Core Rules
- Track strategic work in beads (multi-session, dependencies, discovered work)
- Use `bd create` for issues, TodoWrite for simple single-session execution
- When in doubt, prefer bd—persistence you don't need beats lost context
- Git workflow: hooks auto-sync, run `bd sync` at session end
- Session management: check `bd ready` for available work

## Essential Commands

### Finding Work
- `bd ready` - Show issues ready to work (no blockers)
- `bd list --status=open` - All open issues
- `bd list --status=in_progress` - Your active work
- `bd show <id>` - Detailed issue view with dependencies

### Creating & Updating
- `bd create --title="..." --type=task|bug|feature --priority=2` - New issue
  - Priority: 0-4 or P0-P4 (0=critical, 2=medium, 4=backlog). NOT "high"/"medium"/"low"
- `bd update <id> --status=in_progress` - Claim work
- `bd update <id> --assignee=username` - Assign to someone
- `bd close <id>` - Mark complete
- `bd close <id1> <id2> ...` - Close multiple issues at once (more efficient)
- `bd close <id> --reason="explanation"` - Close with reason
- **Tip**: When creating multiple issues/tasks/epics, use parallel subagents for efficiency

### Dependencies & Blocking
- `bd dep add <issue> <depends-on>` - Add dependency (issue depends on depends-on)
- `bd blocked` - Show all blocked issues
- `bd show <id>` - See what's blocking/blocked by this issue

### Sync & Collaboration
- `bd sync` - Sync with git remote (run at session end)
- `bd sync --status` - Check sync status without syncing

### Project Health
- `bd stats` - Project statistics (open/closed/blocked counts)
- `bd doctor` - Check for issues (sync problems, missing hooks)

## Common Workflows

**Starting work:**
```bash
bd ready           # Find available work
bd show <id>       # Review issue details
bd update <id> --status=in_progress  # Claim it
```

**Completing work:**
```bash
bd close <id1> <id2> ...    # Close all completed issues at once
bd sync                     # Push to remote
```

**Creating dependent work:**
```bash
# Run bd create commands in parallel (use subagents for many items)
bd create --title="Implement feature X" --type=feature
bd create --title="Write tests for X" --type=task
bd dep add beads-yyy beads-xxx  # Tests depend on Feature (Feature blocks tests)
